rows.finding: Apple spent $34.04bn on R&D in the first nine months of FY2026, +33% year on year, while payments for property, plant and equipment fell to $6.80bn from $9.47bn. Its foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud.
rows.mechanism: Apple runs an opex-heavy AI strategy: pay for models and rented compute rather than build datacentres, which protects free cash flow but caps frontier scale and hands bargaining power to Google.
rows.benchmark: Hyperscalers capitalise AI infrastructure; Apple's nine-month capex is about 2% of revenue while R&D grows at roughly 30%.
rows.weakens: The R&D step-up is a real cost, +$8.4bn in nine months, with no separately disclosed AI revenue to offset it, so margin is where the bill lands.
rows.implication: Free cash flow stays intact and buybacks continue, but there is no proprietary compute moat to underwrite a higher multiple on AI.
rows.confidence: high — both figures are in the 10-Q cash-flow and income statements
rows.follow_up: What share of the R&D increase is AI infrastructure, and does Apple intend to keep renting frontier models after the Gemini term?

rows.finding: Silicon stays the deepest in-house layer: A20 Pro in the iPhone 18 Pro on a 2nm process versus A19 on 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem reported across the iPhone 18 line. Products gross margin rose on mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by memory costs.
rows.mechanism: Vertical integration in silicon converts into margin or performance at fixed price; the modem insourcing removes a Qualcomm royalty and gives Apple control over cellular power and cost.
rows.benchmark: A19 (3nm) to A20 (2nm) is a full node step; the modem shift ends Apple's dependence on an external cellular supplier.
rows.weakens: The 10-Q warns of advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints expected to intensify; a node advantage does not protect gross margin when memory prices spike.
rows.implication: Silicon is the moat still widening; it supports the products margin line rather than revenue growth.
rows.confidence: medium — 2nm and C2 are press-reported; margins are from the 10-Q
rows.follow_up: What is the C2 versus Qualcomm cost delta per unit, and how much of the FY2027 products margin depends on non-recurring tariff refunds?

rows.finding: Three patent records verified on 2026-10-31: US10551880B1 (filed 2016-08-09, granted 2020-02-04, active to 2037-06-01, Apple sole assignee); US12164344B2 (filed 2022-07-07, granted 2024-12-10, active to 2042-07-07, Apple sole assignee, family in EP/KR/CN); and US20240147644A1 (filed 2023-10-06, published 2024-05-02, pending, co-assigned Apple and Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix Telecom Parts).
rows.mechanism: The foldable hinge is protected at mechanism level by granted, solely owned patents, but at least one later hinge family is jointly owned with the supplier that builds it, so ownership of the newest hinge generation is shared and unassertable alone.
rows.benchmark: Aggregate grant counts said Apple had no blocking family; the individual records show two granted hinge patents and one co-owned pending application, so the aggregate count understated depth and the earlier reading of the hinge as know-how alone was wrong.
rows.weakens: A co-owned family limits exclusivity, and the joint-development agreement is not public, so whether Amphenol can supply rivals from the same design is unresolved.
rows.implication: Underwrite hinge durability on the granted patents and on manufacturing yield, and treat supplier co-ownership as a live exclusivity risk rather than a clean moat.
rows.confidence: high on bibliographic facts (patent records); low on what the co-ownership agreement permits
rows.follow_up: What does the Apple-Amphenol joint-development agreement allow Amphenol to sell to competitors, and does US12164344B2 read on the shipping Duo hinge?

rows.finding: U.S. utility patent grants fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082 in 2024 (-12%), placing Apple seventh, while the two hinge families verified above are narrow, product-specific grants.
rows.mechanism: A broad but shallower portfolio: breadth does not convert into blocking power in any one area, so the moat has to come from switching costs and yield rather than patent breadth.
rows.benchmark: Apple's grant count is declining while U.S. patent activity overall declined; Huawei and TSMC rank ahead of Apple in the same 2025 table.
rows.weakens: A falling grant count is not proof of a weakening moat, and it clearly understated the hinge position; aggregate counts are a poor proxy either way.
rows.implication: Do not underwrite the moat on patent counts in either direction; use verified families and switching costs.
rows.confidence: medium — aggregate counts are third-party (IFI) data and the individual-record check contradicted one inference drawn from them
rows.follow_up: What is the granted-versus-pending mix across the whole foldable and on-device-AI estates?

rows.finding: Health features are shipping and regulated: Apple Watch hypertension notifications were FDA-cleared, with peer-reviewed commentary in Hypertension questioning accuracy and utility; the feature notifies over a 30-day signal rather than measuring blood pressure.
rows.mechanism: Health adds a regulated, trust-based reason to upgrade a watch and raises the cost of leaving the ecosystem, but it is sold inside a hardware product rather than as a therapy.
rows.benchmark: The clinical evidence level is a cleared screening notification, not a diagnostic claim.
rows.weakens: Contested clinical value limits pricing power and invites regulator and litigation scrutiny; it is a differentiator, not a new revenue pool.
rows.implication: Wearables and health support the installed base and ASP without changing the growth slope on their own.
rows.confidence: medium — clearance reported by a peer-reviewed journal; the openFDA device search returned no match
rows.follow_up: What is the attach and upgrade rate for watches with the hypertension feature, and what does the clearance letter allow Apple to claim?

plan.comparison_set: Google (owns Gemini, TPUs and Android), Samsung (licenses Google's stack), Huawei (constrained by domestic process), Microsoft (cloud capex model), and Apple's own prior cycle (iPhone 17, A19 3nm, no foldable).
plan.counter_evidence: AI talent left through 2025; Siri shipped as an English beta in September 2026, two years after Apple Intelligence; capex fell while R&D rose; patent grants fell 12%; the newest hinge family is co-owned with Amphenol, so exclusivity is partial; memory costs threaten products margin.
plan.decision_question: Is Apple's silicon/OS/AI stack a durable moat, or is Apple falling behind in AI while the hardware cycle matures?
plan.mechanism: Vertical integration in silicon and OS converts into margin or performance at a fixed price and into switching costs; buying frontier models and renting TPU compute converts a would-be fixed-cost AI moat into a variable cost paid to a competitor, which protects cash flow but leaves differentiation in hardware, privacy and distribution. Verified patents show the hinge is protected at mechanism level but its newest generation is co-owned with the supplier.
plan.prohibited: AI leader, seamless ecosystem, strong team, huge market, well positioned, innovative company, best-in-class without a metric, 'many patents', 'about' before a figure, any sentence describing how the section is written.
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a very large installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer that the next upgrade cycle is sold on has been rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it.
plan.visual: Verified patent table (three individual records plus the aggregate), the moat table with the replication test, and the evidence component on the Google dependency.
plan.why_different: This section judges mechanism and replicability of the technology itself — how the silicon, OS, AI and patent layers work and what can be copied — not market size, valuation or the industry's growth rate.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a very large installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer the current upgrade cycle is sold on has been rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with a Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capital spending fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026, while the standard iPhone 18, 18e and a second-generation Air are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was repriced to $899. The mechanism is deliberate — sell the expensive, 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March, when yields and memory supply have matured, turning one spike into two. The risk is elasticity: prices rose into a memory-cost cycle, and the December 2026 quarter is the first test. [S112]

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as a beta in English, 23 months after Apple Intelligence first shipped in October 2024 and after the personalised-Siri promise slipped in 2025. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither company confirmed the price. Apple's own contribution is the interface, personal context, onscreen awareness and Private Cloud Compute. On 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI Safety passed under software chief Craig Federighi as John Giannandrea stepped down; Apple bought the part it could not ship and reorganised the rest. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.**

Google confirmed a multi-year deal on 2026-01-12 to supply Gemini models for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year and 1.2 trillion parameters, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface, the data boundary and the device; it does not keep the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The AI bill lands in R&D, not capex

The cost of rented intelligence sits in operating expense, not on the balance sheet: research and development rose by a third in nine months while capital spending fell. Free cash flow stays intact and the buyback continues, because Apple avoids building datacentres whose utilisation it cannot control. The cost is that the marginal AI dollar has no asset behind it, and bargaining power sits with the supplier that also owns Android. A step-up with no disclosed AI revenue line is a margin question, not a technology one.

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A20 Pro process node | 2nm (A19: 3nm) | Apple launch specification | S113, S112 |
| Siri AI availability | Beta, English, from 2026-09-14 | Apple release | S113 |
| Assistant model scale | 1.2tn parameters, reported | Press reports, unconfirmed | S122 |
| R&D, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $34.04bn, +33% | 10-Q | S6 |
| Capex, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $6.80bn (prior year $9.47bn) | 10-Q cash-flow statement | S6 |
| Services gross margin, nine months | 76.3% | 10-Q | S6 |
| U.S. patent grants, 2025 | 2,722, down 12% | IFI CLAIMS | S117 |

### Silicon is the layer still widening

The A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem reported across the iPhone 18 line, are the parts of the stack Apple still owns end to end. At a fixed retail price a node advantage becomes either margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty and gives Apple control of cellular power and cost. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing warns that advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints are expected to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. [S112]

| Dimension | Apple | Google | Samsung | Huawei | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon | In-house A-series, 2nm | In-house Tensor | External suppliers | In-house Kirin | S113, S112 |
| Frontier model | Licensed Gemini | Owns Gemini | Licenses Google | In-house stack | S111 |
| AI compute | Rented Google TPUs | Owns TPUs and datacentres | Rents cloud | Domestic cloud | S118 |
| AI organisation | Software Engineering since 2025-12-01 | DeepMind | Own research | Own research | S127 |
| Distribution | Own devices and services | Android, Pixel, search | Devices | China-led | S111 |

### Where the moat actually sits

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon design and process access | 8 | Custom SoC design, 2nm allocation, modem integration | 4-6 years | S113, S112 |
| OS and installed-base switching costs | 9 | Continuity, App Store, 76.3% services margin | 7+ years | S6 |
| Foldable hinge mechanism | 6 | Granted US12164344B2, but newest family co-owned with the supplier | 2-3 years | S148, S150 |
| Frontier AI model | 3 | Bought from Google, no frontier training at scale | 1-2 years, by licence | S111, S118 |
| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue, defaults under pressure | 5+ years | S6 |
| **Composite moat** | **Strong hardware, weak AI** | Hardware barrier real, intelligence barrier rented | Years on hardware | S113, S6 |

A funded team of 50 holding the published patent could copy the hinge linkage within two to three years but not the process yield behind it, and an A-series-class chip only after a full node cycle; either way it would lack the installed base, and the assistant can be licensed rather than built, as Apple did.

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions whether the alerts are accurate and useful. It is a monthly alert, not a blood-pressure measurement, so the clinical claim is narrow. Vision Pro sits inside the Wearables line with no disclosed revenue and no confirmed successor. These add upgrade reasons and switching costs, but they are sold as features, not as platforms with their own economics.

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Shipping | 2026-09-18 | iPhone $54.25bn in Q3 FY2026, +22% | Not disclosed by model | December 2026 mix | S113, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Shipping | Announced 2026-09-09 | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Durability and returns | S114 |
| Services | Shipping | Ongoing | $91.73bn in nine months, +14% | 76.3% | DMA compliance | S6 |
| Wearables and Vision Pro | Shipping | Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3 in FY2025 | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Health-feature adoption | S5, S124 |

### The hinge is patented; the newest generation is not Apple's alone

Three individual records, pulled from the patent database on 2026-10-31, correct what the aggregate grant count obscured. Apple has held a granted, active hinge patent since 2020-02-04 and a granted four-jurisdiction hinge family since 2024-12-10, both solely owned, both running to 2037 and 2042 — so the Duo's folding mechanism is protected as a mechanism, not merely by process know-how. The qualification is ownership: a later hinge application is co-assigned with Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix Telecom Parts, the supplier that builds it, so the newest generation is jointly held and Apple cannot assert it alone; whether Amphenol may sell the same design to rivals depends on a development agreement that is not public. U.S. utility grants still fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082, ranking Apple seventh, which makes the portfolio broad rather than deepening. No Apple-owned patent on on-device inference routing was verified, so the AI layer's constraint is the Gemini licence rather than the patent estate. [S149, S148, S150, S117]

| Patent or application | Title | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| US10551880B1 | Electronic devices with flexible displays and hinges | US | 2016-08-09 (priority 2015-09-11) | 2020-02-04 | Granted, active to 2037-06-01 | Gear-plate hinge synchronising halves under a flexible display; the family the Duo descends from | S149 |
| US12164344B2 | Hinges for folding display devices | US, with EP4134784A1, KR20230024218A, CN115904004A | 2022-07-07 (priority 2021-08-11) | 2024-12-10 | Granted, active to 2042-07-07 | Interconnected links, friction clutch, crescent slots — crease and hold-angle behaviour | S148 |
| US20240147644A1 | Hinges for Folding Devices | US, with CN117989219A | 2023-10-06 (priority 2022-11-02) | Not yet granted | Pending, published 2024-05-02 | Co-assigned with Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix; shared ownership limits exclusivity | S150 |

If Siri AI leaves beta with usage data showing Apple's integration beating standalone assistants, the AI layer is worth more than a licensed feature; silence after the 2026-11-02 results would confirm the current reading. If the Gemini term is a bridge to its own model, the dependency is temporary. Until then the technology case rests on silicon, yield and switching costs, and the AI case on distribution. Confidence is high on machine and patent facts, medium on model economics, low on what the Amphenol agreement permits.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a very large installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer the current upgrade cycle is sold on has been rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with a Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capital spending fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026, while the standard iPhone 18, 18e and a second-generation Air are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was repriced to $899. The mechanism is deliberate: sell the expensive, 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March, when yields and memory supply have matured. The risk is elasticity: prices rose into a memory-cost cycle, and December 2026 is the first test. [S112]

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as a beta in English, 23 months after Apple Intelligence first shipped in October 2024 and after the personalised-Siri promise slipped in 2025. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither company confirmed the price. Apple's own contribution is the interface, personal context and Private Cloud Compute. On 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI Safety passed under software chief Craig Federighi as John Giannandrea stepped down: Apple bought what it could not ship and reorganised the rest. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.**

Google confirmed a multi-year deal on 2026-01-12 to supply Gemini models for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year and 1.2 trillion parameters, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface, the data boundary and the device; it does not keep the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The AI bill lands in R&D, not capex

Rented intelligence sits in operating expense, not on the balance sheet: R&D rose a third in nine months while capital spending fell. Free cash flow stays intact and the buyback continues. The marginal AI dollar has no asset behind it, and bargaining power sits with the supplier that also owns Android. A step-up with no disclosed AI revenue line is a margin question, not a technology one.

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A20 Pro process node | 2nm (A19: 3nm) | Apple launch specification | S113, S112 |
| Siri AI availability | Beta, English, from 2026-09-14 | Apple release | S113 |
| Assistant model scale | 1.2tn parameters, reported | Press reports, unconfirmed | S122 |
| R&D, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $34.04bn, +33% | 10-Q | S6 |
| Capex, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $6.80bn (prior year $9.47bn) | 10-Q cash-flow statement | S6 |
| Services gross margin, nine months | 76.3% | 10-Q | S6 |

### Silicon is the layer still widening

The A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem reported across the iPhone 18 line, are the parts of the stack Apple still owns end to end. At a fixed price a node advantage becomes margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing warns that advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints are expected to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. [S112]

| Dimension | Apple | Google | Samsung | Huawei | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon | In-house A-series, 2nm | In-house Tensor | External suppliers | In-house Kirin | S113, S112 |
| Frontier model | Licensed Gemini | Owns Gemini | Licenses Google | In-house stack | S111 |
| AI compute | Rented Google TPUs | Owns TPUs and datacentres | Rents cloud | Domestic cloud | S118 |
| Distribution | Own devices and services | Android, Pixel, search | Devices | China-led | S111 |

### Where the moat actually sits

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon design and process access | 8 | Custom SoC, 2nm allocation, modem integration | 4-6 years | S113, S112 |
| OS and installed-base switching costs | 9 | Continuity, App Store, 76.3% services margin | 7+ years | S6 |
| Foldable hinge mechanism | 6 | Granted US12164344B2; newest family co-owned | 2-3 years | S148, S150 |
| Frontier AI model | 3 | Bought from Google, no frontier training at scale | 1-2 years, by licence | S111, S118 |
| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue | 5+ years | S6 |
| **Composite moat** | **Strong hardware, weak AI** | Hardware barrier real, intelligence barrier rented | Years on hardware | S113, S6 |

A funded team of 50 holding the published patent could copy the hinge linkage in two to three years but not the process yield behind it, and an A-series chip only after a full node cycle; either way it would lack the installed base, and the assistant can be licensed, as Apple did.

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions accuracy and usefulness. It is a monthly alert, not a measurement, so the clinical claim is narrow. Vision Pro sits inside the Wearables line with no disclosed revenue and no confirmed successor. They add upgrade reasons but are sold as features, not platforms with their own economics.

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Shipping | 2026-09-18 | iPhone $54.25bn in Q3 FY2026, +22% | Not disclosed by model | December 2026 mix | S113, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Shipping | Announced 2026-09-09 | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Durability and returns | S114 |
| Services | Shipping | Ongoing | $91.73bn in nine months, +14% | 76.3% | DMA compliance | S6 |
| Wearables and Vision Pro | Shipping | Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3 in FY2025 | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Health-feature adoption | S5, S124 |

### The hinge is patented; the newest generation is not Apple's alone

Three records pulled from the patent database on 2026-10-31 correct what the aggregate grant count obscured. Apple has held a granted, active hinge patent since 2020-02-04 and a granted four-jurisdiction hinge family since 2024-12-10, both solely owned — so the Duo's folding mechanism is protected as a mechanism, not merely by know-how. The qualification is ownership: a later hinge application is co-assigned with Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix Telecom Parts, the supplier, so the newest generation is jointly held and Apple cannot assert it alone; whether Amphenol may sell the same design to rivals depends on an agreement that is not public. U.S. utility grants still fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082, ranking Apple seventh. No Apple-owned on-device inference patent was verified; the AI layer's constraint is the Gemini licence, not the patent estate. [S149, S148, S150, S117]

| Patent or application | Title | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| US10551880B1 | Electronic devices with flexible displays and hinges | US | 2016-08-09 (priority 2015-09-11) | 2020-02-04 | Granted, active to 2037-06-01 | Gear-plate hinge synchronising halves; the Duo lineage | S149 |
| US12164344B2 | Hinges for folding display devices | US, with EP4134784A1, KR20230024218A, CN115904004A | 2022-07-07 (priority 2021-08-11) | 2024-12-10 | Granted, active to 2042-07-07 | Links, friction clutch, crescent slots: crease and hold-angle behaviour | S148 |
| US20240147644A1 | Hinges for Folding Devices | US, with CN117989219A | 2023-10-06 (priority 2022-11-02) | Not yet granted | Pending, published 2024-05-02 | Co-assigned with Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix; shared ownership limits exclusivity | S150 |

If Siri AI leaves beta with usage data showing Apple's integration beating standalone assistants, the AI layer is worth more than a licensed feature; silence after the 2026-11-02 results confirms the current reading. Until then the technology case rests on silicon, yield and switching costs, and the AI case on distribution. Confidence is high on machine and patent facts, medium on model economics, low on what the Amphenol agreement permits.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a very large installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer the current upgrade cycle is sold on has been rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with a Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capital spending fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026, while the standard iPhone 18, 18e and a second-generation Air are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was repriced to $899. The mechanism is deliberate: sell the expensive, 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March, when yields and memory supply have matured. The risk is elasticity: prices rose into a memory-cost cycle, and December 2026 is the first test. [S112]

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as a beta in English, 23 months after Apple Intelligence first shipped in October 2024. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither company confirmed the price. Apple's own contribution is the interface, personal context and Private Cloud Compute. On 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI Safety passed under software chief Craig Federighi as John Giannandrea stepped down: Apple bought what it could not ship and reorganised the rest. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.**

Google confirmed a multi-year deal on 2026-01-12 to supply Gemini models for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year and 1.2 trillion parameters, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface, the data boundary and the device; it does not keep the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The AI bill lands in R&D, not capex

Rented intelligence sits in operating expense, not on the balance sheet: R&D rose a third in nine months while capital spending fell. Free cash flow stays intact and the buyback continues. The marginal AI dollar has no asset behind it, and bargaining power sits with the supplier that also owns Android.

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A20 Pro process node | 2nm (A19: 3nm) | Apple launch specification | S113, S112 |
| Siri AI availability | Beta, English, from 2026-09-14 | Apple release | S113 |
| Assistant model scale | 1.2tn parameters, reported | Press reports, unconfirmed | S122 |
| R&D, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $34.04bn, +33% | 10-Q | S6 |
| Capex, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $6.80bn (prior year $9.47bn) | 10-Q cash-flow statement | S6 |
| Services gross margin, nine months | 76.3% | 10-Q | S6 |

### Silicon is the layer still widening

The A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem reported across the iPhone 18 line, are the parts of the stack Apple still owns end to end. At a fixed price a node advantage becomes margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing warns that advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints are expected to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. [S112]

| Dimension | Apple | Google | Samsung | Huawei | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon | In-house A-series, 2nm | In-house Tensor | External suppliers | In-house Kirin | S113, S112 |
| Frontier model | Licensed Gemini | Owns Gemini | Licenses Google | In-house stack | S111 |
| AI compute | Rented Google TPUs | Owns TPUs and datacentres | Rents cloud | Domestic cloud | S118 |
| Distribution | Own devices and services | Android, Pixel, search | Devices | China-led | S111 |

### Where the moat actually sits

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon design and process access | 8 | Custom SoC, 2nm allocation, modem integration | 4-6 years | S113, S112 |
| OS and installed-base switching costs | 9 | Continuity, App Store, 76.3% services margin | 7+ years | S6 |
| Foldable hinge mechanism | 6 | Granted US12164344B2; newest family co-owned | 2-3 years | S148, S150 |
| Frontier AI model | 3 | Bought from Google, no frontier training at scale | 1-2 years, by licence | S111, S118 |
| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue | 5+ years | S6 |
| **Composite moat** | **Strong hardware, weak AI** | Hardware barrier real, intelligence barrier rented | Years on hardware | S113, S6 |

A funded team of 50 holding the published patent could copy the hinge linkage in two to three years but not the process yield behind it, and an A-series chip only after a full node cycle; it would still lack the installed base, and the assistant can be licensed, as Apple did. [S148, S150]

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions accuracy and usefulness. It is a monthly alert, not a measurement, so the clinical claim is narrow. Vision Pro sits inside the Wearables line with no disclosed revenue and no confirmed successor. They add upgrade reasons but are sold as features, not platforms with their own economics.

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Shipping | 2026-09-18 | iPhone $54.25bn in Q3 FY2026, +22% | Not disclosed by model | December 2026 mix | S113, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Shipping | Announced 2026-09-09 | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Durability and returns | S114 |
| Services | Shipping | Ongoing | $91.73bn in nine months, +14% | 76.3% | DMA compliance | S6 |
| Wearables and Vision Pro | Shipping | Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3 in FY2025 | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Health-feature adoption | S5, S124 |

### The hinge is patented; the newest generation is not Apple's alone

Three records pulled from the patent database on 2026-10-31 correct what the aggregate grant count obscured. Apple has held a granted, active hinge patent since 2020-02-04 and a granted four-jurisdiction hinge family since 2024-12-10, both solely owned — so the Duo's folding mechanism is protected as a mechanism, not merely by know-how. The qualification is ownership: a later hinge application is co-assigned with Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix Telecom Parts, the supplier, so the newest generation is jointly held and Apple cannot assert it alone; whether Amphenol may sell the same design to rivals depends on an agreement that is not public. U.S. utility grants still fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082, ranking Apple seventh. No Apple-owned on-device inference patent was verified; the AI layer's constraint is the Gemini licence, not the patent estate. [S149, S148, S150, S117]

| Patent or application | Title | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| US10551880B1 | Electronic devices with flexible displays and hinges | US | 2016-08-09 (priority 2015-09-11) | 2020-02-04 | Granted, active to 2037-06-01 | Gear-plate hinge synchronising halves; the Duo lineage | S149 |
| US12164344B2 | Hinges for folding display devices | US, with EP4134784A1, KR20230024218A, CN115904004A | 2022-07-07 (priority 2021-08-11) | 2024-12-10 | Granted, active to 2042-07-07 | Links, friction clutch, crescent slots: crease and hold-angle behaviour | S148 |
| US20240147644A1 | Hinges for Folding Devices | US, with CN117989219A | 2023-10-06 (priority 2022-11-02) | Not yet granted | Pending, published 2024-05-02 | Co-assigned with Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix; shared ownership limits exclusivity | S150 |

If Siri AI leaves beta with usage data showing Apple's integration beating standalone assistants, the AI layer is worth more than a licensed feature; silence after the 2026-11-02 results would confirm the current reading. Value the hardware and services cash flows on their own and pay little for the AI layer until it shows either usage evidence or a model Apple owns. Confidence is high on machine and patent facts, medium on model economics, low on what the Amphenol agreement permits.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a very large installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer the current upgrade cycle is sold on has been rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with a Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capital spending fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026, while the standard iPhone 18, 18e and a second-generation Air are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was repriced to $899. The mechanism is deliberate: sell the expensive, 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March, when yields and memory supply have matured. The risk is elasticity: prices rose into a memory-cost cycle, and December 2026 is the first test. [S112]

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as a beta in English, 23 months after Apple Intelligence first shipped in October 2024. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither company confirmed the price. Apple's own contribution is the interface, personal context and Private Cloud Compute. On 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI Safety passed under software chief Craig Federighi as John Giannandrea stepped down: Apple bought what it could not ship and reorganised the rest. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.**

Google confirmed a multi-year deal on 2026-01-12 to supply Gemini models for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year and 1.2 trillion parameters, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface, the data boundary and the device; it does not keep the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The AI bill lands in R&D, not capex

Rented intelligence sits in operating expense, not on the balance sheet: R&D rose a third in nine months while capital spending fell. Free cash flow stays intact and the buyback continues. The marginal AI dollar has no asset behind it, and bargaining power sits with the supplier that also owns Android.

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A20 Pro process node | 2nm (A19: 3nm) | Apple launch specification | S113, S112 |
| Siri AI availability | Beta, English, from 2026-09-14 | Apple release | S113 |
| Assistant model scale | 1.2tn parameters, reported | Press reports, unconfirmed | S122 |
| R&D, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $34.04bn, +33% | 10-Q | S6 |
| Capex, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $6.80bn (prior year $9.47bn) | 10-Q cash-flow statement | S6 |
| Services gross margin, nine months | 76.3% | 10-Q | S6 |

### Silicon is the layer still widening

The A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem reported across the iPhone 18 line, are the parts of the stack Apple still owns end to end. At a fixed price a node advantage becomes margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing warns that advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints are expected to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. [S112]

| Dimension | Apple | Google | Samsung | Huawei | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon | In-house A-series, 2nm | In-house Tensor | External suppliers | In-house Kirin | S113, S112 |
| Frontier model | Licensed Gemini | Owns Gemini | Licenses Google | In-house stack | S111 |
| AI compute | Rented Google TPUs | Owns TPUs and datacentres | Rents cloud | Domestic cloud | S118 |
| Distribution | Own devices and services | Android, Pixel, search | Devices | China-led | S111 |

### Where the moat actually sits

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon design and process access | 8 | Custom SoC, 2nm allocation, modem integration | 4-6 years | S113, S112 |
| OS and installed-base switching costs | 9 | Continuity, App Store, 76.3% services margin | 7+ years | S6 |
| Foldable hinge mechanism | 6 | Granted US12164344B2; newest family co-owned | 2-3 years | S148, S150 |
| Frontier AI model | 3 | Bought from Google, no frontier training at scale | 1-2 years, by licence | S111, S118 |
| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue | 5+ years | S6 |
| **Composite moat** | **Strong hardware, weak AI** | Hardware barrier real, intelligence barrier rented | Years on hardware | S113, S6 |

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions accuracy and usefulness. It is a monthly alert, not a measurement, so the clinical claim is narrow. Vision Pro and the watch add upgrade reasons and switching costs, but they are sold as features, not platforms with their own economics.

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Shipping | 2026-09-18 | iPhone $54.25bn in Q3 FY2026, +22% | Not disclosed by model | December 2026 mix | S113, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Shipping | Announced 2026-09-09 | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Durability and returns | S114 |
| Services | Shipping | Ongoing | $91.73bn in nine months, +14% | 76.3% | DMA compliance | S6 |
| Wearables and Vision Pro | Shipping | Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3 in FY2025 | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Health-feature adoption | S5, S124 |

### The hinge is patented; the newest generation is not Apple's alone

Three records pulled from the patent database on 2026-10-31 correct what the aggregate grant count obscured. Apple has held a granted, active hinge patent since 2020-02-04 and a granted four-jurisdiction hinge family since 2024-12-10, both solely owned, so the Duo's folding mechanism is protected as a mechanism, not merely by know-how. The qualification is ownership: a later hinge application is co-assigned with Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix Telecom Parts, the supplier, so the newest generation is jointly held and Apple cannot assert it alone; whether Amphenol may sell the same design to rivals depends on an agreement that is not public. U.S. utility grants still fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082, ranking Apple seventh, and no Apple-owned on-device inference patent was verified, so the AI layer's constraint is the Gemini licence rather than the patent estate. On replication: a funded team of 50 holding US12164344B2 could copy the linkage in two to three years but not the process yield behind it, and an A-series chip only after a full node cycle; it would still lack the installed base, and the assistant can be licensed, as Apple did. [S149, S148, S150, S117]

| Patent or application | Title | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |

| US10551880B1 | Electronic devices with flexible displays and hinges | US | 2016-08-09 (priority 2015-09-11) | 2020-02-04 | Granted, active to 2037-06-01 | Gear-plate hinge synchronising halves; the Duo lineage | S149 |
| US12164344B2 | Hinges for folding display devices | US, with EP4134784A1, KR20230024218A, CN115904004A | 2022-07-07 (priority 2021-08-11) | 2024-12-10 | Granted, active to 2042-07-07 | Links, friction clutch, crescent slots: crease and hold-angle behaviour | S148 |
| US20240147644A1 | Hinges for Folding Devices | US, with CN117989219A | 2023-10-06 (priority 2022-11-02) | Not yet granted | Pending, published 2024-05-02 | Co-assigned with Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix; shared ownership limits exclusivity | S150 |

If Siri AI leaves beta with usage data showing Apple's integration beating standalone assistants, the AI layer is worth more than a licensed feature; silence after the 2026-11-02 results would confirm the current reading. For an investor that argues for valuing the hardware and services cash flows on their own and paying little for the AI optionality until it shows usage evidence or a model Apple owns. Confidence is high on machine and patent facts, medium on model economics, low on what the Amphenol agreement permits.

Apple's profit is unusually cash-true. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 operating cash flow was $146,724M, capital expenditure $10,041M and free cash flow $136,683M against net income of $128,930M — a headline conversion of 1.06x, or 0.97x on a normalised $125,084M, on capex of 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x and 34.9% at Microsoft and 0.08x and 33.9% at Alphabet. The income statement behind that cash grew revenue from $383,285M in FY2023 to $416,161M in FY2025 and $466,823M trailing, with operating margin of 29.8%, 32.0% and 33.2%. The nine months to 27 June 2026 produced an incremental operating margin of 43.0% — $21,809M more operating income on $50,662M more revenue. The question is how much of that increment is repeatable. [S5, S6]

### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

Gross margin went from 44.1% in FY2023 to 46.2%, 46.9%, 49.1% in the nine months of FY2026 and 48.7% trailing, and the June 2026 quarter printed 50.1%, a record. Services, at a 76.3% gross margin, are 40.3% of the gross-profit pool on 25.8% of revenue; products are not. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% on product mix and tariff refunds, and the 30 July 2026 release attributes 2 points of the quarter's gross margin and $0.11 of its $2.02 EPS to them. The cost side has turned: memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 against the 2025 average and the 10-Q expects the component trends "to intensify". A 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1%, is the level to capitalise. [S17, S68]

::: info warning
**Two percentage points of the record 50.1% gross margin are a one-off tariff refund, and the memory cycle is turning against the hardware line (S6, S17).**

The release puts the refund at 2 points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 quarterly EPS (S17); products gross margin of 39.9% compares with 36.9%, and memory prices rose 146% with the 10-Q warning that cost pressure will intensify (S6, S68). Two hundred basis points off trailing gross margin is $0.52 of EPS, or 6.0% of $8.72.
:::

### Cash conversion is real, but a liability accrual did the lifting

Nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,242M to $116,996M while net income rose $16,920M: non-cash add-backs added $1,956M more and working capital $16,366M more. The dominant line is other current and non-current liabilities, +$10,016M against −$15,161M a year earlier. Other non-current liabilities rose $13,531M to $55,080M while other current liabilities fell $4,128M to $62,259M, a combined $9,403M build that reconciles to the cash line within $613M; the prior year carries the ~$15.8B Irish State Aid settlement (cash taxes paid of $37,332M against a $15,381M provision), with the $15,552M added in FY2024 within $250M of the $15.8B payable. The line's clean history is $3,031M in FY2023, −$248M in FY2024 and $4,724M in FY2025, a $2,502M average, so the $14,101M it puts into trailing free cash flow is the soft spot. Replacing it with the $2,502M average gives $125,084M, or 0.97x conversion, a 2.5% free-cash-flow yield and 40.5x price to free cash flow; zeroing the line gives $122,582M and its best clean year $127,306M, so the defensible band is $122.6-127.3B, with $125.1B the midpoint; anything below $122.6B subtracts more than the line contains. The $13,270M of gross intangibles added against investing "other" of only $1,780M is consistent with the $13,531M build being deferred consideration — an unpaid purchase, which would make $123,152M the figure, inside the band. Deferred revenue is no cushion: 3.2% of trailing revenue, with only $7,260M of nine-month revenue out of the opening balance. [S5, S6]

### The balance sheet is not the risk; the asking price is

At 27 June 2026 cash and marketable securities were $146,517M against debt of $84,344M — net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M nine months earlier while $62,094M of stock was retired. FY2025 notes carried $91.3B of principal with $12.4B due within twelve months; leases add $16.8B of fixed obligations and purchase obligations $57.0B of manufacturing plus $29.3B of other commitments. ### Returns clear the cost of capital several times; the multiple does not clear the risk

ROE of 148.8% and ROA of 36.1% are genuine, and the reported ROIC of 320.6% is an artefact of $146.5B of cash and negative working capital that shrink invested capital to $45,347M. The measure that survives is cash return on book capital: normalised free cash flow of $125.1B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, or 65.2%, against 57.3% in FY2025. With the ten-year Treasury at 4.93% and an equity risk premium of 4.5-5.5%, a cost of equity of 9-11% is cleared several times; the constraint is the price: $5,072B of market capitalisation on $128,930M of trailing net income is a 2.5% earnings yield. Capital allocation agrees: nine-month buybacks of $62,094M plus dividends of $11,778M are 67.0% of reported free cash flow and 72.4% of the $102,057M normalised figure, net cash rose, and shares fell 1.7% while net income rose 20.0%, so buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% EPS growth. Not a debt-funded buyback story. [S6, S7, S10]

### What the next print has to clear

No audited fiscal 2026 exists: Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026, and the only forward numbers are guidance of 9-11% revenue growth for the quarter ($111.7-113.7B off $102.5B) with iPhone growth in the mid-teens, against consensus of $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4% on FY2025) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%). Sensitivity on trailing figures after a 17.3% tax rate: 200 basis points of gross margin is $0.52 of EPS (6.0%), 500 basis points is $1.31 (15.0%), losing the $20B search payment is $1.12 (12.9%) and a 10% fall in iPhone revenue at 39.9% is $0.55 (6.3%). Gross margin moves the outcome most because it applies to all $466,823M of revenue while a unit miss applies only to hardware. For the investor, earnings quality is not the constraint; the price is. The open diligence: December-quarter gross margin guidance, FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices, what the $12,116M of net intangibles bought, and what sits in the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Business Model (business_model, revision 4 by Fundamentals Analyst, 7,773 characters)
Apple monetises the same customer twice: once through a hardware sale at a 39.9% gross margin that is paid for before the cost is incurred, and again through a services annuity at a 76.3% gross margin that costs almost nothing incremental to serve. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 the company recorded $466,823M of revenue and $227,123M of gross profit — iPhone $245,540M (52.6% of revenue), Services $120,478M (25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit), Mac $35,863M, Wearables, Home and Accessories $36,290M and iPad $28,652M. Services gross profit of $91,607M covers total company R&D of $42,901M 2.1 times, so the annuity already pays for the AI build-out. The mix, not the growth rate, is what an investor is underwriting. [S5, S6]

### The 2026 acceleration is hardware, not annuity

In the nine months to 27 June 2026 revenue grew 16.1%, but the engines ran at different speeds: iPhone +22.4%, Mac +8.6%, iPad +3.0%, Wearables +2.3%, Services +14.1%. Services therefore fell to 25.2% of revenue from 26.2% in FY2025 — the first year-over-year decline in the mix since at least FY2023, when services were 22.2% of revenue. Greater China grew 30% after shrinking 4% in FY2025. The standard account of Apple as a services compounder is not what the last three quarters show; they show an iPhone cycle carried by Pro-model mix, with the annuity growing at 14.1% against iPhone's 22.4%. The counterpoint is that 14.1% growth on a $109,158M FY2025 base is $15,391M of incremental annual revenue at a 76.3% margin, more gross profit than most software companies generate in total. [S5, S6]

### What one device earns

Apple stopped disclosing unit shipments, so the most defensible unit is the active device. The table divides trailing-twelve-month flows by Apple's own installed-base statement; because that base is an earnings-call figure rather than a filed one, every line is an estimate.

| Line item | Per unit — per active device, per year | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $186.7 | $466,823M TTM ÷ 2,500M devices | S6, S73 |
| of which Services | $48.2 | $120,478M TTM ÷ 2,500M | S6, S73 |
| Gross profit | $90.8 | 48.7% blended gross margin | S6 |
| Selling, general and administrative | ($11.7) | $29,363M TTM | S6 |
| Research and development | ($17.2) | $42,901M TTM | S6 |
| Operating profit | $61.9 | $154,859M TTM | S6 |
| Gross profit ÷ selling cost | 7.8x a year | $90.8 ÷ $11.7 | S6 |
| Cash payback on acquisition | immediate | cash conversion cycle −56.8 days | S5, S6 |

The waterfall ends where most hardware businesses begin: there is no customer-acquisition payback period to compute, because Apple is paid by carriers and retailers before it pays its assemblers. Payables of $64,525M against inventory of $11,092M produced a cash conversion cycle of −56.8 days at 27 June 2026, against +39.2 days at Alphabet; each new device is cash-positive on day one. That advantage is not a scale economy a rival can buy with capital — it is the accounting consequence of owning the customer and outsourcing the factory. [S6, S73]

### The annuity rests on two contested tolls

The 10-K describes Services as advertising (including third-party licensing arrangements), AppleCare, cloud, the App Store, subscription content and payment services, but never splits their revenue. Two of those lines are tolls on other people's commerce. The first is the App Store commission: on 11 December 2025 the Ninth Circuit held that Apple's 27% commission on purchases made after a user follows a link out of an app had a prohibitive effect, and remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, may be charged. The second is the Google default-search licence, where court records show Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and a 2022 payment put at $20B — 16.6% of trailing-twelve-month services revenue of $120,478M and 12.9% of trailing-twelve-month operating income of $154,859M; measured on FY2025 the same $20B would be 18.3% of $109,158M services revenue and 15.0% of $133,050M operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy kept the payments but barred exclusivity and capped any default arrangement at twelve months, and Google's D.C. Circuit brief of 22 May 2026 challenges that judgment. [S69, S70]

| Offer | Price or take rate | Margin or peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone (upfront hardware) | implied ASP $941 ($245,540M TTM ÷ 261M estimated units) | products gross margin 39.9% | S6, S74 |
| App Store (commission, ex-EU) | 15-30%; the 27% link-out commission was ruled prohibitive | services gross margin 76.3% | S6, S69 |
| App Store (EU, from 2026-10-01) | 26% in-app purchase, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission | EU band 5-26% against 15-30% elsewhere | S77, S78 |
| Safari default search | 36% of Safari search advertising; $20B in 2022 | 16.6% of TTM services revenue | S70 |
| Subscriptions and cloud | recurring, bundled at the device sale | services 76.3% vs Microsoft 67.9% in FY2026 | S6, S49 |
| Handset peer — Samsung devices (DX) | — | KRW 0.8tn operating loss in Q3 2026 | S75 |

### The cost side has turned

The 2026 margin record is partly purchased. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% a year earlier, and the 10-Q attributes the gain to product mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher costs including memory; the third-quarter release put the refund benefit at 2 percentage points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS. Against that, memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 versus the 2025 average, and Samsung's mobile memory costs rose 107%. Apple's filing expects the component trends "to intensify, which may materially negatively impact" revenue, costs and gross margin, and concedes that price increases "may also reduce demand" — the elasticity admission a hardware model has to make. A 47-48% gross margin is the defensible base case, not the 50.1% just printed. [S17, S68]

### What this means for the watchlist

The business is a negative-working-capital hardware engine bolted to a high-margin annuity, and the annuity is the terminal value. That structure justifies a premium to hardware peers but not a software multiple on the whole revenue base, because a quarter of revenue sits in a line where two tolls are being repriced in court, and much of the rest faces a memory cycle that turns faster than Apple can re-price handsets. At $344.63 on 30 October 2026 the market capitalisation is $5,072B, or 39.3x trailing EPS of $8.72; the price already assumes the annuity survives intact and that memory costs are passed through. The open diligence is narrow and decisive: does services growth re-accelerate above 15% without hardware mix; what commission does the district court set on remand; and when does memory pricing peak in supplier guidance? Confidence in the mix arithmetic is high because it comes from filed segment data; confidence in the durability of the tolls is medium, because Apple discloses neither their size nor their terms, and the FY2026 10-K expected alongside the 2 November 2026 results is the document that would close the gap. [S6, S7]

::: evidence
**The services annuity is what the multiple buys, and it is a smaller share of revenue than it was a year ago.**

Services produced $120,478M of trailing-twelve-month revenue — 25.8% of the total but 40.3% of gross profit and 2.1x company R&D — while its revenue share fell to 25.2% in the nine months to 27 June 2026 as iPhone revenue grew 22.4% against services growth of 14.1% (S5, S6, S17). Two tolls inside that line, the App Store commission and the Safari search licence worth 16.6% of services revenue on a 2022 court figure, are both under active legal challenge (S69, S70).

Apple is an exceptional franchise priced as a perpetual compounder. At $344.63 on NasdaqGS in US dollars (20:00 UTC, 2026-10-30) Apple's market capitalisation is $5,029.6bn and its enterprise value $4,967.4bn, or 39.5x trailing earnings and 38.8x trailing NOPAT of $128.1bn; that valuation needs either 6.4-6.9% growth in perpetuity at a 9.0-9.5% discount rate, or a 7.0% discount rate on the growth I forecast below. Both are demanding for a company whose revenue compounded at 5.0% a year from FY2021. Forward, 35.2x against a twelve-month average of 35.7x, is still a premium to everyone else. Apple pays 39.5x trailing earnings against a peer median of 20.2x and 32.1x EV/EBIT against 20.5x, a 57% premium only Microsoft at 23.6x comes near. The premium is earned on margin and returns — 48.7% gross margin and 148.8% return on equity, both without peer in the group — not on growth, which is why the discount rate rather than the operating story controls it [S7, S6, S97, S14].

The operating story that supports 39.5x is real but narrower than the headline. The June 2026 quarter grew revenue 16.4% to $109.4bn, with iPhone up 21.7% and Greater China up 22.4%, with the September quarter guided to 9-11% growth. Against that, IDC expects global smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% in 2026, and TrendForce puts the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials up 38% year on year with memory at 34% of it, from 10% a year earlier. Apple is growing by price, mix and share capture in a shrinking unit market while its hardware cost base rises; Samsung's mobile division lost money for the same reason. Price-led growth is the most reversible kind, and FY2027 gross margin, not revenue, is where the memory cycle will show [S17, S84, S99, S72].

Free cash flow is what the buyback and the model rest on, and the trailing figure carries an accrual that has to come out. Trailing FCF of $136.7bn is a 2.7% yield, but it includes $14.1bn from other current and non-current liabilities: +$10.0bn in the nine months to June 2026 and $4.1bn in the September 2025 quarter. The $25.2bn year-on-year swing overstates it, because the prior-year line absorbed the $15.8bn Irish State Aid settlement in the year to September 2025. Netting the line to zero, to its $2.5bn three-year average or to its best clean year of $4.7bn gives normalised FCF of $122.6-127.3bn, $125.1bn central — 0.95-0.99x net income, a 2.4-2.5% yield and 39.5-41.0x P/FCF (40.2x at the midpoint on the $5,029.6bn market value, 40.5x diluted), still ahead of Microsoft's 1.5% and Alphabet's 0.6%. The $122.6bn floor treats the whole build as deferred consideration for the $13.3bn of gross intangibles added, which would make that cash an unpaid purchase; on the $13.5bn non-current build alone the figure is $123.2bn and 41.2x diluted. R&D grew 32.5% to $34.0bn in the nine months and capital expenditure sits at 0.77x depreciation, both capping the margin expansion the multiple assumes. Shareholders have received $438.6bn of repurchases and $75.0bn of dividends in the five fiscal years to FY2025, plus $82.2bn and $15.6bn in the twelve months to June 2026; nine-month buybacks and dividends of $73.9bn cover 72.4% of normalised nine-month free cash flow, against a $100bn authorisation from May 2025. No equity has been raised and total debt fell from $124.7bn to $84.3bn [S5, S6, S1].

A discounted cash flow is the right instrument for a company whose value is almost all terminal, and the least forgiving. I take FY2026 revenue of $477.0bn (nine months actual of $364.4bn plus the guided $112.7bn fourth quarter), growth fading from 9% to 5%, a 33% operating margin, a 17.5% tax rate and capital expenditure 0.2 points above depreciation. At a 9.0% cost of equity — a 4.93% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a 1.05 beta — the shares are worth $212. The market price is reached only near a 7.0% discount rate, and each 50bp on the rate moves value by 15-18%. That is the whole question, whether a 4.93% risk-free rate leaves room for a 7% required return on equity [S10, S6, S72].

Services produced $120.5bn of trailing revenue at a 76.0% gross margin and hardware $346.3bn at 39.1%; allocating the $72.3bn of operating expense 40/60 toward services gives services EBIT of $62.7bn and hardware of $92.1bn. At 23x and 12x — between Microsoft's 23.6x and HP's 9.6x — the parts plus $62.2bn of net cash are worth $177 a share, or $238 at 28x and 18x. The largest single risk inside services is the Google default-search payment, put at $20bn a year; the remedies ruling in United States v. Google barred exclusivity without banning the payments, which reduces that risk to a renegotiation rather than a loss, though the case is on appeal [S5, S70, S101].

Three scenarios bracket the answer. Even the bull case, with revenue growing 14% next year and margins at 35%, is worth $277 — 20% below the market; the bear case is $133. Buying at $344.63 means buying the multiple rather than the business. A 9% three-year return needs an entry near $270, as the exit analysis sets out, or evidence that EPS grows above 12% rather than the 9.9% that consensus prices for iPhone in FY2027 [S71, S7].

The counter-case deserves its weight. The discount rate in my model is a judgement, not an observation: at the low end of the plausible range the base case comes close to the market price. Quality franchises in a high-rate world have held premium multiples for years. What I will not concede is a margin of safety: on every operating assumption I can defend, the buyer's return is set by the exit multiple, which already sits at the top of its own historical range. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the gap to intrinsic value, because it rests on a cost of equity nobody observes. The open gap is consensus revenue, EPS and free cash flow for the next two fiscal years and a sell-side price target, none of which is publicly disclosed here."}],"isError":false}

arguments.markdown:
Apple is a high-quality compounder whose price already capitalises a peak margin and a contested services annuity, so the risks that matter destroy the multiple, not the balance sheet, and none is priced at $344.63. At that price on 2026-10-30 the shares trade at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and the base DCF at a 9.0% cost of equity is $212. Eight risks follow: two are fatal to the price, the rest execution. The strategic risk is AI defending the price without widening the moat. [S7, S97, S10]

::: risk-matrix
| Risk | Probability | Impact | Level | Timing | Signpost | Mitigation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Memory cost pushes hardware gross margin below 46% | High, over 60% | EPS -6% per 200bp; -25% to -30% value | Critical | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | Product margin under 37%; DRAM/NAND prices | Enter at $270 only on the $9.3+ EPS case; else $235 | S17, S6, S99, S136 |
| Google search payment cut or banned on appeal | Medium, 20-25% | EPS -10% to -13%; value -15% to -20% | High | 2027, D.C. Circuit No. 26-5023 | Argument schedule; renewal terms | Cap the position | S70, S76, S135 |
| Multiple reverts to the 31.0x four-year mean | Medium-high, 40-60% | -21.5% at 31x; -38% at 24.6x | High | 0-12 months | Ten-year yield above 5%; forward P/E above 40x | No position at $344.63 | S97, S10 |
| EU DMA fee band spreads to other markets | Medium, 20-40% | EU operating income -1% to -2%; -5% if it spreads | Medium | From 2026-10-01 | Services growth below 10%; developer migration | Underwrite 10-12% services | S77, S78, S102 |
| AI cycle fails; Gemini reprices per device | Medium, 20-40% | EPS -5% to -8% | High | FY2027 | Siri beta exit; services margin | Treat AI as a cost line | S111, S6, S137 |
| China demand falls 20% in H2 2026 | Medium, 30-50% | Revenue -3.5%; EPS -5% to -6% | Medium | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | China revenue; Q4 tracker data | Do not capitalise 30% China growth | S96, S84, S87 |
| Cash quality and inventory | Medium, 30-50% | FCF -$1.9bn to $123.2bn, 40.8x; inventory -$3.3bn | Low | 10-K, 2026-11-02 | Other-liabilities note; inventory $11.1bn | Underwrite the $123.2bn case | S6, S5, S17 |
| Governance and key-person | Low, under 20% | Value -5% to -10% | Low | 12-24 months | No named successor; director exits | Board refresh; retention | S134, S133, S141, S11 |
:::

### The risk that breaks the thesis is the hardware margin, not the platform

The 50.1% gross margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; because that margin applies to $466.8bn of revenue, one point is $4.7bn of operating income. Memory prices rose 146% in Q1 2026 against the 2025 average; TrendForce's 30 September 2026 forecast puts Q4 DRAM contract prices 10-15% higher quarter on quarter and NAND 15-20% higher; the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials is up 38%, memory at 34% against 10%. Two hundred basis points off the margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of the trailing $8.72; a 46% margin takes FY2027 EPS from $9.79 to about $9.3 and, at 29x, puts fair value at $270 — the entry price, not a discount. Inventory of $11.1bn against $5.7bn at FY2025 year-end is the write-down channel. [S17, S6, S99, S136]

::: info danger
**A memory-led gross margin below 46% breaks earnings and the multiple at once.** The margin applies to all $466.8bn of revenue, Apple cannot re-price handsets inside a quarter, and 39.5x leaves no room for a 6% EPS cut: 200bp also invites a de-rating from 35x forward to the 31x mean, together a 25-30% drawdown. The signpost is the December-quarter margin guide on 2026-11-02 (S17, S6, S136).
:::

### The search payment is a renegotiation risk until the appeal says otherwise

The Google trial record put the payment at $20bn in 2022 — 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and 15% of operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy barred exclusivity but preserved non-exclusive payments; the American Antitrust Institute's 4 August 2026 brief asks the D.C. Circuit to strike it, and Google's appeal, No. 26-5023, with the DOJ's cross-appeal, stays live into 2027. I price a 20-25% probability of a ban at -10% to -13% of EPS and -15% to -20% of value. The EU fee schedule from 2026-10-01 — 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission — is modest in situ: Europe is 26.7% of nine-month revenue and each $1bn of commission lost is $0.75bn of gross profit against $154.9bn of operating income. The template is the risk: a 5-15% band extended to the United States would reset services growth to high single digits. [S70, S76, S77, S79, S135]

### The growth swing factors are AI and China

Siri shipped as an English beta on 2026-09-14, 23 months after Apple Intelligence, on a Gemini model licensed at a reported $1bn a year. Apple rents the capability and books the bill in operating expense; no filing names an AI profit-and-loss owner after the 2025-12-01 reorganisation, and X Corp. and xAI's suit survived dismissal. A $1bn licence is 0.6% of operating income, so the base case holds while pricing is annual; per-device pricing across 2.5bn devices would land in the 76.3% services margin, and whether a licensed assistant sells $1,199 handsets is the swing factor. China is a shrinking pool, not a lost share war: Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's, with Apple at 19.5% against Huawei's 21.3%. Greater China was 17.8% of nine-month FY2026 revenue; IDC sees the decline widening to 20% in H2 2026, and a 20% China decline is 3.5% of group revenue and 5-6% of EPS. Supply adds a layer: 25% of iPhones are assembled in India, where production incentives expired on 2026-03-31 and costs exceed China's, and Section 301 duties replaced the IEEPA tariffs struck down on 2026-02-20. [S111, S6, S127, S137, S96, S84, S87, S115]

### Valuation is the risk, and the entry ladder assumes the base EPS

At 39.5x, Apple sits at a five-year high for a company guiding 9-11% growth, and 40.2x trailing free cash flow of $125.1bn (39.5-41.0x across the $122.6-127.3bn band, on $5,029.6bn) makes the multiple the largest driver of return: reversion to the 31.0x mean costs 21.5%, reversion to the 24.6x FY2022 trough 38%. Each 50 basis points on the cost of equity moves the DCF by 15-18%; a 4.93% ten-year Treasury against a 7.0% implied return is the debate. The stress tests separate survivable from fatal. A 30% revenue fall leaves $326.8bn; on the 43.0% nine-month incremental operating margin it leaves $94.6bn of operating income and $5.4 of EPS, but that is an up-cycle margin. On the FY2021-FY2025 average gross margin of 44.5%, with $72.3bn of operating expense held flat, gross profit is $145.3bn, operating income $73.0bn and EPS $4.10 at the 17.3% tax rate on 14.75bn diluted shares — a 58% decremental margin, not 43%; a 10% cost cut lifts EPS to $4.50, and the FY2016-FY2025 average margin of 41.4% gives $3.54. At 29x that is $103-131, at or below the $133 DCF bear. A market 50% smaller is revenue 35% lower and, on the same 44.5% margin, EPS $3.52, $70-88 at 20-25x. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn, 56.4-58.6x, covering the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of buybacks and dividends; a 30% inventory write-down is $3.3bn, 1.9% of operating income; 100 basis points on $84.3bn of debt is $0.84bn, 0.5%. Apple survives all of them on $62.2bn of net cash and $146.5bn of securities; the equity does not. The entry ladder is the same single-point bet: 0.75-1.0% at $270 is 27.6x only on FY2027 EPS of $9.79, with $245 at 25.0x and $225 at 23.0x. A 46% gross margin takes EPS to about $9.3 and $270 to 29.0x; a search cut of 12.9% takes $9.79 to $8.53 and, with the margin, to $8.10, so $270 becomes 31.7x to 33.3x against the 31.0x four-year mean and $245 becomes 28.7x to 30.2x. The same 27.6x that made $270 cheap on $9.79 is $224-235 on $8.10-8.53. The ladder needs a condition, not a new number: $270 only if the 2026-11-02 guide holds FY2027 EPS at $9.3 or better and December gross margin at 47%; otherwise the first tranche belongs at $235 and the second at $210, with the 5% cap unchanged. [S10, S97, S6, S5, S151, S70]

### Governance, unknowns and the call

Governance and key-person risk are monitors. Cook is Executive Chair and Ternus CEO under a nine-director board with two non-independent members, after the board waived its age guideline for two directors who stood in 2026. Srouji's 2025-12-06 departure report is superseded by his 2026-04-20 promotion to Chief Hardware Officer with hardware engineering added to his silicon remit, which concentrates rather than removes the dependency, with no disclosed successor or retention award. Cash quality is smaller than it looked: the $13,531M non-current liability build against $13,270M of gross intangibles added reads as deferred consideration, but net of a $4,128M current-liability fall it is $9,403M, inside the $10,016M line; if unpaid, free cash flow is $123.2bn, inside the $122.6-127.3bn band, and the 10-K on 2026-11-02 must tie the intangibles to the liability. Outside the filings: a Taiwan Strait disruption stopping 2nm supply, and an appellate remedy treating the Gemini default as the next search payment. The downside is a de-rating, not insolvency, so position size carries the risk; open diligence is the December-quarter margin guide, the 10-K working-capital note, the appellate schedule and the Gemini renewal terms. None changes the call: the price, not the business, is the problem, and the $270 entry holds only if December confirms the margin trough and EPS near $9.3. [S134, S133, S141, S11, S5, S6]

arguments.markdown:
Apple's markets are large but no longer volume-growth markets: the smartphone unit pool is contracting at the fastest rate on record in 2026 while its dollar value rises, so growth to 2030 must come from holding more than 40% of smartphone value, monetising a record installed base through services, and a foldable and AI-driven cycle, not from market growth. Apple's revenue compounded 3.3% from FY2021 to FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and then accelerated to 16% in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone revenue up 22% [S5, S6].

| Measure | Figure | Period | Method and note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global smartphone units | 1.26B | 2025 | Counterpoint full year, +2% YoY; Omdia 1.25B | S92 |
| Global smartphone units | just over 1.0B | 2026E | IDC, -16.7% YoY, steepest annual fall on record | S84 |
| Global smartphone value | $613B | 2026E | IDC, +6.3% YoY | S84 |
| Global smartphone ASP | $581 | 2026E | IDC, +27.6%; Omdia independently $565 (+21%) | S84, S88 |
| Premium segment (wholesale ASP $600+) | 29% of units | H1 2026 | Counterpoint; 25% in H1 2025, 20% in H1 2022 | S94 |
| Apple iPhone revenue | $209.6B FY2025; $196.5B 9M FY2026 | FY2025 / 9M FY2026 | Apple filings; +22% in 9M FY2026 | S5, S6 |
| Apple implied iPhone revenue per unit | ~$830 FY2025; ~$1,100 2026E | FY2025 / 2026E | Calculated: iPhone revenue / iOS units (20% of 1.26B; 23.6% of ~1.0B) | S5, S6, S92, S84 |
| Apple share of smartphone value | 36% FY2025; 42.7% 2026 | FY2025 / 2026 | Calculated: iPhone revenue / market value | S5, S6, S92, S88 |
| Wearables units | 625M | 2026E | IDC, +1.7%; 2.4% CAGR to 687M by 2030 | S85 |
| Global advertising pool | $1.34T | 2026E | WARC, +11.9% | S89 |

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units. TAM: IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while value rises 6.3% to $613B on a 27.6% ASP increase to $581; Omdia independently forecasts $565, a 21% increase it calls the largest on record. SAM: the premium segment (29% of units at $600 or more) plus the iOS installed base for services, where Apple's 65% premium share sets the addressable pool. SOM: Apple's current capture, $466.8B of trailing-twelve-month revenue to June 2026, of which $245.5B is iPhone and $120.5B services. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line. The mechanism is a memory cost shock: NAND and DRAM costs more than 300% above a year earlier are passed through to shelf prices, so the market is being repriced, not expanded [S84, S88, S94, S6].

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026 from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those units with 9% growth. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3% [S94, S92, S84]. On my calculation Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B [S5, S6, S92, S88]. Value capture, not unit share, is the franchise an investor is buying.

### The 27.6% price rise is cost pass-through, and Apple is pricing above it

The increase is not demand-led. IDC attributes the 27.6% ASP rise to a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier passed into shelf prices, and TrendForce shows the cost landing on Apple directly: the iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials rose 38% year on year, memory reaching 34% of the BOM in Q3 2026 from about 10% a year earlier. Apple then raised iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max list prices by $100 and held the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027 [S84, S99, S112]. What supports willingness to pay is sell-through at those prices: Counterpoint recorded iPhone 18 Pro sales up 23.5% in the first three weeks in China, and Apple's installed base reached an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter [S96, S17]. What weakens it is provenance and timing: Apple discloses no upgrade rate and no unit volumes, so an upgrade-cycle claim rests on third-party panels, and IDC attributes part of China's Q3 strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half increases, with the Chinese market possibly down 20% in H2 2026 [S87]. On IDC's unit base Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose from about $830 in FY2025 to about $1,100 annualised in 2026, 32% against the market's 27.6%; on the higher 261M unit estimate for FY2026 the rise is 21% [S5, S6, S92, S84, S74]. The direction is unambiguous — Apple is pricing above the market average — but the magnitude depends on a unit count Apple does not publish, so the gain should be read as cost recovery plus Pro mix, not as proof of an upgrade super-cycle. An upgrade-rate series from a consumer panel would settle it and is not in this evidence set.

Three pools can add revenue to 2030, and only one is large enough to change the trajectory. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Services: $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026, up 14.1% in nine months at a 76.3% gross margin, against a $1.34T advertising pool in 2026 and an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods and services in 2025 [S84, S6, S17, S89, S83]. Wearables and PC: a 2.4% CAGR market to 2030 with smartwatches shrinking 3.7% in 2026 while glasses grow 18.1%, and Apple took 18.2% of combined PC and tablet units in Q2 2026 [S85, S152]. The non-phone pools, $33.7B of Mac and $35.7B of wearables in FY2025, are too small to carry group growth alone [S5].
