|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Europe | Not published | Apple +16.1% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 26.7% of revenue | DMA take-rate cuts from 2026-10-01; GDPR | Samsung, Xiaomi, Google | S77, S6 |
| Greater China | 66M units in Q2 2026 | Market -10% in Q3 2026 (Counterpoint), -15.4% (IDC); Apple +30.0% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 19.5% in Q3 2026 on Counterpoint and 17.8% on IDC, against Huawei's 21.3% and 21.1%; Apple +4.8 points YoY | Market access; local champion; data rules; WeChat as a distribution layer | Huawei, OPPO, vivo, Xiaomi, Honor | S139, S140, S96, S87, S6 |

Geography splits the durability question, and policy is a live variable in every region. Greater China was 15.5% of FY2025 revenue and produced 30% growth in the first nine months of FY2026; Europe is 26.7% and grew 16%, the Americas 42.9% and 11%, Japan 6.9% and 10%, Rest of Asia-Pacific 8.1% and 19% [S6]. China is the most fragile in size, not share: the market fell 10% in Q3 2026 to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 on Counterpoint's count, yet Apple's share rose 4.8 points to 19.5%, and IDC's lower 17.8% counts shipments rather than sell-through, a gap consistent with channel inventory drawing down [S139, S140, S96]. The EU cut the commission on externally distributed digital transactions to 5% from 1 October 2026 [S77]. US tariffs moved twice in 2026: the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026 and Section 301 duties followed, while the Section 232 semiconductor review produced no additional tariffs on Apple products on 14 January 2026 [S87]. Demand is organic consumer replacement, not policy-created: China's subsidies faded in 2026 and India's incentives are supply-side. The budget owner is the consumer or a carrier financing plan; the procurement cycle follows the September launch; willingness to pay is being tested by the 27.6% ASP increase. Confidence is high on 2026 data and low on 2027-2030 regional sizing, because regional market values are paywalled and Apple discloses no units; the open questions are how much iPhone growth is units versus price, whether services growth is users or price, how much China demand was pulled forward, and how much memory cost Apple can pass through in FY2027.

::: evidence

The 2026 price rise is cost pass-through — TrendForce puts memory at 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials against about 10% a year earlier (S99) — and Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose about 32% on IDC's unit base against 27.6% for the market (S5, S6, S92, S84). Foldables ($45.7B of category value by 2027) and services ($120.5B trailing twelve months at 76.3% gross margin) are the only pools large enough to move group growth; wearables grow 2.4% a year to 2030 (IDC, S85).

arguments.markdown:
Apple's markets are large but no longer volume-growth markets: the smartphone unit pool is contracting at the fastest rate on record in 2026 while its dollar value rises, so growth to 2030 must come from holding more than 40% of smartphone value, monetising a record installed base through services, and a foldable and AI-driven cycle, not from market growth. Apple's revenue compounded 3.3% from FY2021 to FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and then accelerated to 16% in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone revenue up 22% [S5, S6].

| Measure | Figure | Period | Method and note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global smartphone units | 1.26B | 2025 | Counterpoint full year, +2% YoY; Omdia 1.25B | S92 |
| Global smartphone units | just over 1.0B | 2026E | IDC, -16.7% YoY, steepest annual fall on record | S84 |
| Global smartphone value | $613B | 2026E | IDC, +6.3% YoY | S84 |
| Global smartphone ASP | $581 | 2026E | IDC, +27.6%; Omdia independently $565 (+21%) | S84, S88 |
| Premium segment (wholesale ASP $600+) | 29% of units | H1 2026 | Counterpoint; 25% in H1 2025, 20% in H1 2022 | S94 |
| Apple iPhone revenue | $209.6B FY2025; $196.5B 9M FY2026 | FY2025 / 9M FY2026 | Apple filings; +22% in 9M FY2026 | S5, S6 |
| Apple implied iPhone revenue per unit | ~$830 FY2025; ~$1,100 2026E | FY2025 / 2026E | Calculated: iPhone revenue / iOS units (20% of 1.26B; 23.6% of ~1.0B) | S5, S6, S92, S84 |
| Apple share of smartphone value | 36% FY2025; 42.7% 2026 | FY2025 / 2026 | Calculated: iPhone revenue / market value | S5, S6, S92, S88 |
| Wearables units | 625M | 2026E | IDC, +1.7%; 2.4% CAGR to 687M by 2030 | S85 |

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units. TAM: IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while value rises 6.3% to $613B on a 27.6% ASP increase to $581, against Omdia's independent $565 (+21%). SAM: the premium segment (29% of units at $600 or more) plus the iOS installed base for services, where Apple's 65% premium share sets the addressable pool. SOM: Apple's current capture, $466.8B of trailing-twelve-month revenue to June 2026, of which $245.5B is iPhone and $120.5B services. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line. The mechanism is a memory cost shock: NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier are passed into shelf prices, so the market is being repriced, not expanded [S84, S88, S94, S6].

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026 from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those units with 9% growth. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3% [S94, S92, S84]. Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B [S5, S6, S92, S88]. Value capture, not unit share, is the franchise an investor is buying.

### The 27.6% price rise is cost pass-through, and Apple is pricing above it

The increase is not demand-led. IDC attributes the 27.6% ASP rise to a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier passed into shelf prices, and TrendForce shows the cost landing on Apple directly: the iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials rose 38% year on year, memory reaching 34% of the BOM in Q3 2026 from about 10% a year earlier. Apple then raised iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max list prices by $100 and held the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027 [S84, S99, S112]. What supports willingness to pay is sell-through at those prices: Counterpoint recorded iPhone 18 Pro sales up 23.5% in the first three weeks in China, and Apple's installed base reached an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter [S96, S17]. What weakens it is provenance and timing: Apple discloses no upgrade rate and no unit volumes, so an upgrade-cycle claim rests on third-party panels, and IDC attributes part of China's Q3 strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half increases, with the Chinese market possibly down 20% in H2 2026 [S87]. On IDC's unit base Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose from about $830 in FY2025 to about $1,100 annualised in 2026, 32% against the market's 27.6%; on the higher 261M unit estimate for FY2026 the rise is 21% [S5, S6, S92, S84, S74]. Apple is therefore pricing above the market average, but the magnitude rests on a unit count it does not publish: the gain is cost recovery plus Pro mix, not proof of an upgrade super-cycle. A consumer-panel upgrade rate would settle it and is not in this evidence set.

Three pools can add revenue to 2030, and only one is large enough to change the trajectory. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Services: $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026, up 14.1% in nine months at a 76.3% gross margin, against a $1.34T advertising pool in 2026 and an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods and services in 2025 [S84, S6, S17, S89, S83]. Wearables and PC: a 2.4% CAGR market to 2030 with smartwatches shrinking 3.7% in 2026 while glasses grow 18.1%, and Apple took 18.2% of combined PC and tablet units in Q2 2026 [S85, S152]. The non-phone pools, $33.7B of Mac and $35.7B of wearables in FY2025, are too small to carry group growth alone [S5].

Geography splits the durability question, and policy is a live variable in every region. Greater China was 15.5% of FY2025 revenue and grew 30% in the first nine months of FY2026; Europe is 26.7% and grew 16%, the Americas 42.9% and 11%, Japan 6.9% and 10%, Rest of Asia-Pacific 8.1% and 19% [S6]. China is the most fragile in size, not share: the market fell 10% in Q3 2026 to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 on Counterpoint's count, yet Apple's share rose 4.8 points to 19.5%, while IDC's lower 17.8% counts shipments rather than sell-through, a gap consistent with channel inventory drawing down [S139, S140, S96]. The EU cut the commission on externally distributed digital transactions to 5% from 1 October 2026 [S77]. US tariffs moved twice in 2026: the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026 and Section 301 duties followed, while the Section 232 semiconductor review produced no additional tariffs on Apple products on 14 January 2026 [S87]. Demand is organic consumer replacement, not policy-created: China's subsidies faded in 2026 and India's incentives are supply-side. The budget owner is the consumer or a carrier financing plan; the procurement cycle follows the September launch. Confidence is high on 2026 data and low on 2027-2030 regional sizing, because regional market values are paywalled and Apple discloses no units; the open questions are how much iPhone growth is units versus price, whether services growth is users or price, and how much memory cost Apple can pass through in FY2027.

::: evidence
**Apple's markets are growing in dollars while shrinking in units, so its growth is price- and share-led, not market-led.**

The global pool is $613B of smartphone value in 2026 against just over 1.0B units, with a 27.6% ASP increase doing the work volume used to do (IDC, S84). Premium concentration (29% of units) and Apple's 65% share of it explain why Apple captures 36-43% of value on 20-24% of units (Counterpoint, S94; Apple filings, S5, S6). Foldables ($45.7B of category value by 2027) and services ($120.5B trailing twelve months at 76.3% gross margin) are the only pools large enough to move group growth; wearables grow 2.4% a year to 2030 (IDC, S85).
:::

arguments.markdown:
Apple is a high-quality compounder whose price already capitalises a peak margin and a contested services annuity, so the risks that matter destroy the multiple, not the balance sheet, and none is priced at $344.63. At that price on 2026-10-30 the shares trade at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and the base DCF at a 9.0% cost of equity is $212. Eight risks follow: two are fatal to the price, the rest execution. The strategic risk is AI defending the price without widening the moat. [S7, S97, S10]

::: risk-matrix
| Risk | Probability | Impact | Level | Timing | Signpost | Mitigation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Memory cost pushes hardware gross margin below 46% | High, over 60% | EPS -6% per 200bp; -25% to -30% value | Critical | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | Product margin under 37%; DRAM/NAND prices | Enter at $270 only on the $9.3+ EPS case | S17, S6, S99, S136 |
| Google search payment cut or banned on appeal | Medium, 20-25% | EPS -10% to -13%; value -15% to -20% | High | 2027, D.C. Circuit No. 26-5023 | Argument schedule; renewal terms | Cap the position | S70, S76, S135 |
| Multiple reverts to the 31.0x four-year mean | Medium-high, 40-60% | -21.5% at 31x; -38% at 24.6x | High | 0-12 months | Ten-year yield above 5%; forward P/E above 40x | No position at $344.63 | S97, S10 |
| EU DMA fee band spreads to other markets | Medium, 20-40% | EU operating income -1% to -2%; -5% if it spreads | Medium | From 2026-10-01 | Services growth below 10%; developer migration | Underwrite 10-12% services | S77, S78, S102 |
| AI cycle fails; Gemini reprices per device | Medium, 20-40% | EPS -5% to -8% | High | FY2027 | Siri beta exit; services margin | Treat AI as a cost line | S111, S6, S137 |
| China demand falls 20% in H2 2026 | Medium, 30-50% | Revenue -3.5%; EPS -5% to -6% | Medium | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | China revenue; Q4 tracker data | Do not capitalise 30% China growth | S96, S84, S87 |
| Cash quality and inventory | Medium, 30-50% | FCF -$1.9bn to $123.2bn, 40.8x; inventory -$3.3bn | Low | 10-K, 2026-11-02 | Other-liabilities note; inventory $11.1bn | Underwrite the $123.2bn case | S6, S5, S17 |
| Governance and key-person | Low, under 20% | Value -5% to -10% | Low | 12-24 months | No named successor; director exits | Board refresh; retention | S134, S133, S141, S11 |
:::

### The risk that breaks the thesis is the hardware margin, not the platform

The 50.1% gross margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; because that margin applies to $466.8bn of revenue, one point is $4.7bn of operating income. Memory prices rose 146% in Q1 2026 against the 2025 average; TrendForce's 30 September 2026 forecast puts Q4 DRAM contract prices 10-15% higher quarter on quarter and NAND 15-20% higher; the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials is up 38%, memory at 34% against 10%. Two hundred basis points off the margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of the trailing $8.72; a 46% margin takes FY2027 EPS from $9.79 to about $9.3 and, at 29x, puts fair value at $270 — the entry price, not a discount. [S17, S6, S99, S136]

::: info danger
**A memory-led gross margin below 46% breaks earnings and the multiple at once.** The margin applies to all $466.8bn of revenue, Apple cannot re-price handsets inside a quarter, and 39.5x leaves no room for a 6% EPS cut: 200bp also invites a de-rating from 35x forward to the 31x mean, together a 25-30% drawdown. The signpost is the December-quarter margin guide on 2026-11-02 (S17, S6, S136).
:::

### The search payment is a renegotiation risk until the appeal says otherwise

The Google trial record put the payment at $20bn in 2022 — 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and 15% of operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy preserved non-exclusive payments; the American Antitrust Institute's 4 August 2026 brief asks the D.C. Circuit to strike it, and Google's appeal, No. 26-5023, with the DOJ's cross-appeal, stays live into 2027. I price a 20-25% probability of a ban at -10% to -13% of EPS and -15% to -20% of value. The EU fee schedule from 2026-10-01 — 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission — is modest in situ: Europe is 26.7% of nine-month revenue and each $1bn of commission lost is $0.75bn of gross profit. The template is the risk: a 5-15% band extended to the United States would reset services growth to high single digits. [S70, S76, S77, S79, S135]

### The growth swing factors are AI and China

Siri shipped as an English beta on 2026-09-14 on a Gemini model licensed at a reported $1bn a year. Apple rents the capability and books the bill in operating expense; no filing names an AI profit-and-loss owner after the 2025-12-01 reorganisation, and X Corp. and xAI's suit survived dismissal. A $1bn licence is 0.6% of operating income, so the base case holds while pricing is annual; per-device pricing across 2.5bn devices would land in the 76.3% services margin, and whether a licensed assistant sells $1,199 handsets is the swing factor. China is a shrinking pool, not a lost share war: Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's, with Apple at 19.5% against Huawei's 21.3%. Greater China was 17.8% of nine-month FY2026 revenue; IDC sees the decline widening to 20% in H2 2026, and a 20% China decline is 3.5% of group revenue and 5-6% of EPS. Supply adds India — 25% of iPhones, incentives expired 2026-03-31, costs above China's — and Section 301 duties replacing the IEEPA tariffs struck down on 2026-02-20. [S111, S6, S127, S137, S96, S84, S87, S115]

### Valuation is the risk, and the entry ladder assumes the base EPS

At 39.5x, Apple sits at a five-year high for a company guiding 9-11% growth, and 40.2x trailing free cash flow of $125.1bn (39.5-41.0x across the $122.6-127.3bn band, on $5,029.6bn) makes the multiple the largest driver of return: reversion to the 31.0x mean costs 21.5%, reversion to the 24.6x FY2022 trough 38%. Each 50bp on the cost of equity moves the DCF 15-18%; the ten-year Treasury is 4.93% against a 7.0% implied return. A 30% revenue fall leaves $326.8bn; on the 43.0% nine-month incremental operating margin it leaves $94.6bn of operating income and $5.4 of EPS, but that is an up-cycle margin. On the FY2021-FY2025 average gross margin of 44.5%, with $72.3bn of operating expense held flat, gross profit is $145.3bn, operating income $73.0bn and EPS $4.10 at the 17.3% tax rate on 14.75bn diluted shares — a 58% decremental margin, not 43%; a 10% cost cut lifts EPS to $4.50, and the FY2016-FY2025 average margin of 41.4% gives $3.54. At 29x that is $103-131, at or below the $133 DCF bear. A market 50% smaller is revenue 35% lower and, on the same 44.5% margin, EPS $3.52, $70-88 at 20-25x. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn, 56.4-58.6x, covering the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of buybacks and dividends; a 30% inventory write-down is $3.3bn, 1.9% of operating income; 100 basis points on $84.3bn of debt is $0.84bn, 0.5%. Apple survives all of them on $62.2bn of net cash and $146.5bn of securities; the equity does not. The entry ladder is the same single-point bet: 0.75-1.0% at $270 is 27.6x only on FY2027 EPS of $9.79. A 46% gross margin takes EPS to about $9.3 and $270 to 29.0x; a search cut of 12.9% takes $9.79 to $8.53 and, with the margin, to $8.10, so $270 becomes 31.7x to 33.3x against the 31.0x four-year mean and $245 becomes 28.7x to 30.2x. The same 27.6x that made $270 cheap on $9.79 is $224-235 on $8.10-8.53. The ladder needs a condition, not a new number: $270 only if the 2026-11-02 guide holds FY2027 EPS at $9.3 or better and December gross margin at 47%; otherwise the first tranche belongs at $235 and the second at $210, with the 5% cap unchanged. [S10, S97, S6, S5, S151, S70]

### Governance, unknowns and the call

Governance and key-person risk are monitors. Cook is Executive Chair and Ternus CEO under a nine-director board with two non-independent members. Srouji's 2025-12-06 departure report is superseded by his 2026-04-20 promotion to Chief Hardware Officer with hardware engineering added to his silicon remit, which concentrates rather than removes the dependency. Cash quality is smaller than it looked: the $13,531M non-current liability build against $13,270M of gross intangibles added reads as deferred consideration, but net of a $4,128M current-liability fall it is $9,403M, inside the $10,016M line; if unpaid, free cash flow is $123.2bn, inside the $122.6-127.3bn band. Outside the filings: a Taiwan Strait disruption stopping 2nm supply, and an appellate remedy treating the Gemini default as the next search payment. The downside is a de-rating, not insolvency, so position size carries the risk; open diligence is the December-quarter margin guide, the 10-K working-capital note, the appellate schedule and the Gemini renewal terms. None changes the call: the price, not the business, is the problem, and the $270 entry holds only if December confirms the margin trough and EPS near $9.3. [S134, S133, S141, S11, S5, S6]

arguments.markdown:
Apple's markets are large but no longer volume-growth markets: the smartphone unit pool is contracting at the fastest rate on record in 2026 while its dollar value rises, so growth to 2030 must come from holding more than 40% of smartphone value, monetising a record installed base through services, and a foldable and AI-driven cycle, not from market growth. Apple's revenue compounded 3.3% from FY2021 to FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and then accelerated to 16% in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone revenue up 22% [S5, S6].

| Measure | Figure | Period | Method and note | Source |

| Global smartphone units | just over 1.0B | 2026E | IDC, -16.7% YoY, steepest annual fall on record | S84 |
| Global smartphone value | $613B | 2026E | IDC, +6.3% YoY | S84 |
| Global smartphone ASP | $581 | 2026E | IDC, +27.6%; Omdia independently $565 (+21%) | S84, S88 |
| Premium segment (wholesale ASP $600+) | 29% of units | H1 2026 | Counterpoint; 25% in H1 2025, 20% in H1 2022 | S94 |
| Apple iPhone revenue | $209.6B FY2025; $196.5B 9M FY2026 | FY2025 / 9M FY2026 | Apple filings; +22% in 9M FY2026 | S5, S6 |
| Apple implied iPhone revenue per unit | ~$830 FY2025; ~$1,100 2026E | FY2025 / 2026E | Calculated: iPhone revenue / iOS units (20% of 1.26B; 23.6% of ~1.0B) | S5, S6, S92, S84 |
| Apple share of smartphone value | 36% FY2025; 42.7% 2026 | FY2025 / 2026 | Calculated: iPhone revenue / market value | S5, S6, S92, S88 |

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units. TAM: IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while value rises 6.3% to $613B on a 27.6% ASP increase to $581, against Omdia's independent $565 (+21%). SAM: the premium segment (29% of units at $600 or more) plus the iOS installed base for services, where Apple's 65% premium share sets the addressable pool. SOM: Apple's current capture, $466.8B of trailing-twelve-month revenue to June 2026, of which $245.5B is iPhone and $120.5B services. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line. The mechanism is a memory cost shock: NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier are passed into shelf prices, so the market is being repriced, not expanded [S84, S88, S94, S6].

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026 from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those units with 9% growth. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3% [S94, S92, S84]. Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B [S5, S6, S92, S88]. Value capture, not unit share, is the franchise an investor is buying.

### The 27.6% price rise is cost pass-through, and Apple is pricing above it

The increase is not demand-led. IDC attributes the 27.6% ASP rise to a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier passed into shelf prices, and TrendForce shows the cost landing on Apple directly: the iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials rose 38% year on year, memory reaching 34% of the BOM in Q3 2026 from about 10% a year earlier. Apple then raised Pro and Pro Max list prices by $100 and held the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027 [S84, S99, S112]. What supports willingness to pay is sell-through at those prices: Counterpoint recorded iPhone 18 Pro sales up 23.5% in the first three weeks in China, and Apple's installed base reached an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter [S96, S17]. What weakens it: Apple discloses no upgrade rate or unit volumes, so an upgrade-cycle claim rests on third-party panels, and IDC attributes part of China's Q3 strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half increases, with the market possibly down 20% in H2 2026 [S87]. On IDC's unit base Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose from about $830 in FY2025 to about $1,100 annualised in 2026, 32% against the market's 27.6%; on the higher 261M unit estimate for FY2026 the rise is 21% [S5, S6, S92, S84, S74]. Apple is therefore pricing above the market average, but the magnitude rests on a unit count it does not publish: the gain is cost recovery plus Pro mix, not proof of an upgrade super-cycle. A consumer-panel upgrade rate would settle it, and none is in this evidence set.

Three pools can add revenue to 2030, and only one is large enough to change the trajectory. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Services: $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026, up 14.1% in nine months at a 76.3% gross margin, against a $1.34T advertising pool in 2026 and an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods and services in 2025 [S84, S6, S17, S89, S83]. Wearables and PC: a 2.4% CAGR market to 2030 with smartwatches shrinking 3.7% in 2026 while glasses grow 18.1%, and Apple took 18.2% of combined PC and tablet units in Q2 2026 [S85, S152]. The non-phone pools, $33.7B of Mac and $35.7B of wearables in FY2025, are too small to carry group growth alone [S5].

arguments.markdown:
Apple is a high-quality compounder whose price already capitalises a peak margin and a contested services annuity, so the risks that matter destroy the multiple, not the balance sheet, and none is priced at $344.63. At that price on 2026-10-30 the shares trade at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and the base DCF at a 9.0% cost of equity is $212. Eight risks follow: two are fatal to the price, the rest execution. The strategic risk is AI defending the price without widening the moat. [S7, S97, S10]

::: risk-matrix
| Risk | Probability | Impact | Level | Timing | Signpost | Mitigation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Memory cost pushes hardware gross margin below 46% | High, over 60% | EPS -6% per 200bp; -25% to -30% value | Critical | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | Product margin under 37%; DRAM/NAND prices | Enter at $270 only on the $9.3+ EPS case | S17, S6, S99, S136 |
| Google search payment cut or banned on appeal | Medium, 20-25% | EPS -10% to -13%; value -15% to -20% | High | 2027, D.C. Circuit No. 26-5023 | Argument schedule; renewal terms | Cap the position | S70, S76, S135 |
| Multiple reverts to the 31.0x four-year mean | Medium-high, 40-60% | -21.5% at 31x; -38% at 24.6x | High | 0-12 months | Ten-year yield above 5%; forward P/E above 40x | No position at $344.63 | S97, S10 |
| EU DMA fee band spreads to other markets | Medium, 20-40% | EU operating income -1% to -2%; -5% if it spreads | Medium | From 2026-10-01 | Services growth below 10%; developer migration | Underwrite 10-12% services | S77, S78, S102 |
| AI cycle fails; Gemini reprices per device | Medium, 20-40% | EPS -5% to -8% | High | FY2027 | Siri beta exit; services margin | Treat AI as a cost line | S111, S6, S137 |
| China demand falls 20% in H2 2026 | Medium, 30-50% | Revenue -3.5%; EPS -5% to -6% | Medium | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | China revenue; Q4 tracker data | Do not capitalise 30% China growth | S96, S84, S87 |
| Cash quality and inventory | Medium, 30-50% | FCF -$1.9bn to $123.2bn, 40.8x; inventory -$3.3bn | Low | 10-K, 2026-11-02 | Other-liabilities note; inventory $11.1bn | Underwrite the $123.2bn case | S6, S5, S17 |
| Governance and key-person | Low, under 20% | Value -5% to -10% | Low | 12-24 months | No named successor; director exits | Board refresh; retention | S134, S133, S141, S11 |
:::

### The risk that breaks the thesis is the hardware margin, not the platform

The 50.1% gross margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; because that margin applies to $466.8bn of revenue, one point is $4.7bn of operating income. Memory prices rose 146% in Q1 2026 against the 2025 average; TrendForce's 30 September 2026 forecast puts Q4 DRAM contract prices 10-15% higher quarter on quarter and NAND 15-20% higher; the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials is up 38%, memory at 34% against 10%. Two hundred basis points off the margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of the trailing $8.72; a 46% margin takes FY2027 EPS from $9.79 to about $9.3 and, at 29x, puts fair value at $270 — the entry price, not a discount. [S17, S6, S99, S136]

::: info danger
**A memory-led gross margin below 46% breaks earnings and the multiple at once.** The margin applies to all $466.8bn of revenue, Apple cannot re-price handsets inside a quarter, and 39.5x leaves no room for a 6% EPS cut: 200bp also invites a de-rating from 35x forward to the 31x mean, together a 25-30% drawdown. The signpost is the December-quarter margin guide on 2026-11-02 (S17, S6, S136).
:::

### The search payment is a renegotiation risk until the appeal says otherwise

The Google trial record put the payment at $20bn in 2022 — 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and 15% of operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy preserved non-exclusive payments; the American Antitrust Institute's 4 August 2026 brief asks the D.C. Circuit to strike it, and Google's appeal, No. 26-5023, with the DOJ's cross-appeal, stays live into 2027. I price a 20-25% probability of a ban at -10% to -13% of EPS and -15% to -20% of value. The EU fee schedule from 2026-10-01 — 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission — is modest in situ: Europe is 26.7% of nine-month revenue and each $1bn of commission lost is $0.75bn of gross profit. A 5-15% band extended to the United States would reset services growth to high single digits. [S70, S76, S77, S79, S135]

### The growth swing factors are AI and China

Siri shipped as an English beta on 2026-09-14 on a Gemini model licensed at about $1bn a year. Apple rents the capability and books the bill in operating expense; no filing names an AI profit-and-loss owner after the 2025-12-01 reorganisation, and X Corp. and xAI's suit survived dismissal. A $1bn licence is 0.6% of operating income, so the base case holds while pricing is annual; per-device pricing across 2.5bn devices would land in the 76.3% services margin, and whether a licensed assistant sells $1,199 handsets is the swing factor. China is a shrinking pool, not a lost share war: Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's, with Apple at 19.5% against Huawei's 21.3%. Greater China was 17.8% of nine-month FY2026 revenue; IDC sees the decline widening to 20% in H2 2026, and a 20% China decline is 3.5% of group revenue and 5-6% of EPS. Supply adds India — 25% of iPhones, incentives expired 2026-03-31, costs above China's — and Section 301 duties replacing the IEEPA tariffs struck down on 2026-02-20. [S111, S6, S127, S137, S96, S84, S87, S115]

### Valuation is the risk, and the entry ladder assumes the base EPS

At 39.5x, Apple sits at a five-year high for a company guiding 9-11% growth, and 40.2x trailing free cash flow of $125.1bn (39.5-41.0x across the $122.6-127.3bn band, on $5,029.6bn) makes the multiple the largest driver of return: reversion to the 31.0x mean costs 21.5%, reversion to the 24.6x FY2022 trough 38%. Each 50bp on the cost of equity moves the DCF 15-18%; the ten-year Treasury is 4.93% against a 7.0% implied return. A 30% revenue fall leaves $326.8bn; on the 43.0% nine-month incremental operating margin it leaves $94.6bn of operating income and $5.4 of EPS, but that is an up-cycle margin. On the FY2021-FY2025 average gross margin of 44.5%, with $72.3bn of operating expense held flat, gross profit is $145.3bn, operating income $73.0bn and EPS $4.10 at the 17.3% tax rate on 14.75bn diluted shares — a 58% decremental margin, not 43%; a 10% cost cut lifts EPS to $4.50, and the FY2016-FY2025 average margin of 41.4% gives $3.54. At 29x that is $103-131, at or below the $133 DCF bear. A market 50% smaller is revenue 35% lower and EPS $3.52, $70-88 at 20-25x. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn, 56.4-58.6x, covering the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of buybacks and dividends; a 30% inventory write-down is $3.3bn, 1.9% of operating income; 100 basis points on $84.3bn of debt is $0.84bn, 0.5%. Apple survives all of them on $62.2bn of net cash and $146.5bn of securities; the equity does not. The entry ladder is the same single-point bet: 0.75-1.0% at $270 is 27.6x only on FY2027 EPS of $9.79. A 46% gross margin takes EPS to about $9.3 and $270 to 29.0x; a search cut of 12.9% takes $9.79 to $8.53 and, with the margin, to $8.10, so $270 becomes 31.7x to 33.3x against the 31.0x four-year mean and $245 becomes 28.7x to 30.2x. The same 27.6x that made $270 cheap on $9.79 is $224-235 on $8.10-8.53. The ladder needs a condition, not a new number: $270 only if the 2026-11-02 guide holds FY2027 EPS at $9.3 or better and December gross margin at 47%; otherwise the first tranche belongs at $235 and the second at $210, with the 5% cap unchanged. [S10, S97, S6, S5, S151, S70]

### Governance, unknowns and the call

Governance and key-person risk are monitors. Cook is Executive Chair and Ternus CEO under a nine-director board. Srouji's 2025-12-06 departure report is superseded by his 2026-04-20 promotion to Chief Hardware Officer with hardware engineering added to his silicon remit, which concentrates rather than removes the dependency. Cash quality is smaller than it looked: the $13,531M non-current liability build against $13,270M of gross intangibles added reads as deferred consideration, but net of a $4,128M current-liability fall it is $9,403M, inside the $10,016M line; if unpaid, free cash flow is $123.2bn, inside the $122.6-127.3bn band. Outside the filings: a Taiwan Strait disruption stopping 2nm supply, and an appellate remedy treating the Gemini default as the next search payment. The downside is a de-rating, not insolvency, so position size carries the risk; open diligence is the December-quarter margin guide, the 10-K working-capital note, the appellate schedule and the Gemini renewal terms. None changes the call: the price, not the business, is the problem, and the $270 entry holds only if December confirms the margin trough and EPS near $9.3. [S134, S133, S141, S11, S5, S6]

| Apple share of smartphone value | 36% FY2025; 42.7% 2026 | FY2025 / 2026 | Calculated: iPhone revenue / market value | S5, S6, S92, S88 |

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units. TAM: IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while value rises 6.3% to $613B on a 27.6% ASP increase to $581, against Omdia's independent $565 (+21%). SAM: the premium segment (29% of units at $600 or more) plus the iOS installed base for services, where Apple's 65% premium share sets the addressable pool. SOM: Apple's current capture, $466.8B of trailing-twelve-month revenue to June 2026, of which $245.5B is iPhone and $120.5B services. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line. The mechanism is a memory cost shock: NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier are passed into shelf prices, so the market is being repriced, not expanded [S84, S88, S94, S6].

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026 from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those units with 9% growth. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3% [S94, S92, S84]. Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B [S5, S6, S92, S88]. Value capture, not unit share, is the franchise an investor is buying.

### The 27.6% price rise is cost pass-through, and Apple is pricing above it

The increase is not demand-led. IDC attributes the 27.6% ASP rise to a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM up more than 300% and passed into shelf prices, and TrendForce shows the cost landing on Apple directly: the iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials rose 38% year on year, memory reaching 34% of the BOM in Q3 2026 from about 10% a year earlier. Apple then raised Pro and Pro Max list prices by $100 and held the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027 [S84, S99, S112]. What supports willingness to pay is sell-through at those prices: Counterpoint recorded iPhone 18 Pro sales up 23.5% in the first three weeks in China, and Apple's installed base reached an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter [S96, S17]. What weakens it: Apple discloses no upgrade rate or unit volumes, so an upgrade-cycle claim rests on third-party panels, and IDC attributes part of China's Q3 strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half increases, with the market possibly down 20% in H2 2026 [S87]. On IDC's unit base Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose from about $830 in FY2025 to about $1,100 annualised in 2026, 32% against the market's 27.6%; on the higher 261M unit estimate for FY2026 the rise is 21% [S5, S6, S92, S84, S74]. Apple is therefore pricing above the market average, but the magnitude rests on a unit count it does not publish: the gain is cost recovery plus Pro mix, not proof of an upgrade super-cycle. A consumer-panel upgrade rate would settle it and is not available here.

Three pools can add revenue to 2030, and only one is large enough to change the trajectory. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Services: $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026, up 14.1% in nine months at a 76.3% gross margin, against a $1.34T advertising pool in 2026 and an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods and services in 2025 [S84, S6, S17, S89, S83]. Wearables and PC: a 2.4% CAGR market to 2030 with smartwatches shrinking 3.7% in 2026 while glasses grow 18.1%, and Apple took 18.2% of combined PC and tablet units in Q2 2026 [S85, S152]. The non-phone pools, $33.7B of Mac and $35.7B of wearables in FY2025, are too small to carry group growth alone [S5].

arguments.markdown:
Apple's markets are large but no longer volume-growth markets: the smartphone unit pool is contracting at the fastest rate on record in 2026 while its dollar value rises, so growth to 2030 must come from holding more than 40% of smartphone value, monetising a record installed base through services, and a foldable and AI-driven cycle, not from market growth. Apple's revenue compounded 3.3% from FY2021 to FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and then accelerated to 16% in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone revenue up 22% [S5, S6].

| Measure | Figure | Period | Method and note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global smartphone units | 1.26B | 2025 | Counterpoint full year, +2% YoY; Omdia 1.25B | S92 |
| Global smartphone units | just over 1.0B | 2026E | IDC, -16.7% YoY, steepest annual fall on record | S84 |
| Global smartphone value | $613B | 2026E | IDC, +6.3% YoY | S84 |
| Global smartphone ASP | $581 | 2026E | IDC, +27.6%; Omdia independently $565 (+21%) | S84, S88 |
| Premium segment (wholesale ASP $600+) | 29% of units | H1 2026 | Counterpoint; 25% in H1 2025, 20% in H1 2022 | S94 |
| Apple iPhone revenue | $209.6B FY2025; $196.5B 9M FY2026 | FY2025 / 9M FY2026 | Apple filings; +22% in 9M FY2026 | S5, S6 |
| Apple implied iPhone revenue per unit | $832 FY2025; $1,101 2026E | FY2025 / 2026E | Calculated: iPhone revenue / iOS units (252M = 20% of 1.26B; 238M = 23.6% of 1.01B) | S5, S6, S92, S84 |
| Apple share of smartphone value | 36% FY2025; 42.7% 2026 | FY2025 / 2026 | Calculated: iPhone revenue / market value | S5, S6, S92, S88 |

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units. TAM: IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while value rises 6.3% to $613B on a 27.6% ASP increase to $581, against Omdia's independent $565 (+21%). SAM: the premium segment (29% of units at $600 or more) plus the iOS installed base for services, where Apple's 65% premium share sets the addressable pool. SOM: Apple's current capture, $466.8B of trailing-twelve-month revenue to June 2026, of which $245.5B is iPhone and $120.5B services. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line. The mechanism is a memory cost shock: NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier are passed into shelf prices, so the market is being repriced, not expanded [S84, S88, S94, S6].

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026 from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those units with 9% growth. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3%. Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B. Value capture, not unit share, is the franchise an investor is buying [S94, S92, S84, S5, S6, S88].

### The 27.6% price rise is cost pass-through, and Apple is pricing above it

The increase is not demand-led. IDC attributes the 27.6% ASP rise to a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM up more than 300% and passed into shelf prices, and TrendForce shows the cost landing on Apple directly: the iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials rose 38% year on year, memory reaching 34% of the BOM in Q3 2026 against one-tenth a year earlier. Apple then raised Pro and Pro Max list prices by $100 and held the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027. What supports willingness to pay is sell-through at those prices: Counterpoint recorded iPhone 18 Pro sales up 23.5% in the first three weeks in China, and Apple's installed base reached an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter. What weakens it: Apple discloses no upgrade rate or unit volumes, so an upgrade-cycle claim rests on third-party panels, and IDC attributes part of China's Q3 strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half increases, with the market possibly down 20% in H2 2026 [S84, S99, S112, S96, S17, S87].

That leaves the decomposition. On IDC's unit base Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose from $832 in FY2025 to $1,101 annualised in 2026, 32% against the market's 27.6%; on the higher 261M unit estimate for FY2026 the rise is 21% [S5, S6, S92, S84, S74]. Apple is pricing above the market average, but the magnitude rests on a unit count it does not publish: the gain is cost recovery plus Pro mix, not proof of an upgrade super-cycle. A consumer-panel upgrade rate would settle it and is not available here.

Three pools can add revenue to 2030, and only one is large enough to change the trajectory. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Services: $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026, up 14.1% in nine months at a 76.3% gross margin, against a $1.34T advertising pool in 2026 and an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods and services in 2025. Wearables and PC: a 2.4% CAGR market to 2030 with smartwatches shrinking 3.7% in 2026 while glasses grow 18.1%, and Apple took 18.2% of combined PC and tablet units in Q2 2026. The non-phone pools, $33.7B of Mac and $35.7B of wearables in FY2025, are too small to carry group growth alone [S84, S6, S17, S89, S83, S85, S152, S5].

| Region | Market size (latest dated) | Growth | Company's position | Barriers | Key competitors | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Americas | Not published; global $613B (2026E) | Apple +11.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; home market; 42.9% of FY2025 revenue | US tariffs; platform antitrust | Samsung, Google, Motorola | S84, S5, S6 |
| Europe | Not published | Apple +16.1% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 26.7% of revenue | DMA take-rate cuts from 2026-10-01; GDPR | Samsung, Xiaomi, Google | S77, S6 |
| Greater China | 66M units in Q2 2026 | Market -10% in Q3 2026 (Counterpoint), -15.4% (IDC); Apple +30.0% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 19.5% in Q3 2026 on Counterpoint and 17.8% on IDC, against Huawei's 21.3% and 21.1%; Apple +4.8 points YoY | Market access; local champion; data rules; WeChat as a distribution layer | Huawei, OPPO, vivo, Xiaomi, Honor | S139, S140, S96, S87, S6 |
| Japan | Not published | Apple +10.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 6.9% of revenue | Yen weakness; carrier-controlled channel | Samsung, Google, Sharp | S6 |
| Rest of Asia-Pacific | Not published; emerging markets forecast down more than 20% in 2026 | Apple +19.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 8.1% of revenue; India manufacturing and retail | Price sensitivity; tariffs | Samsung, Xiaomi, vivo, OPPO, Transsion | S84, S6 |

Geography splits the durability question. Greater China was 15.5% of FY2025 revenue and grew 30% in the first nine months of FY2026; Europe is 26.7% and grew 16%, the Americas 42.9% and 11%, Japan 6.9% and 10%, Rest of Asia-Pacific 8.1% and 19%. China is the most fragile in size, not share: the market fell 10% in Q3 2026 to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 on Counterpoint's count, yet Apple's share rose 4.8 points to 19.5%, while IDC's lower 17.8% counts shipments rather than sell-through, a gap consistent with channel inventory drawing down. The EU cut the commission on externally distributed digital transactions to 5% from 1 October 2026. Demand is organic consumer replacement, not policy-created: China's subsidies faded in 2026 and India's incentives are supply-side [S6, S139, S140, S96, S77].

The budget owner is the consumer or a carrier financing plan; the procurement cycle follows the September launch. Confidence is high on 2026 data and low on 2027-2030 regional sizing, because regional market values are paywalled and Apple discloses no units; the open questions are how much iPhone growth is units versus price, whether services growth is users or price, and how much memory cost Apple can pass through in FY2027 [S84, S6].

::: evidence
**Apple's markets are growing in dollars while shrinking in units, so its growth is price- and share-led, not market-led.**

The global pool is $613B of smartphone value in 2026 against just over 1.0B units, with a 27.6% ASP increase doing the work volume used to do (IDC, S84). Premium concentration of 29% of units and Apple's 65% share of it explain why it captures 36-43% of value on 20-24% of units (Counterpoint, S94; S5, S6). The 2026 price rise is cost pass-through — TrendForce puts memory at 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials against 10% a year earlier (S99) — and Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose 32% on IDC's unit base against 27.6% for the market (S5, S6, S92, S84). Foldables ($45.7B of category value by 2027) and services ($120.5B trailing twelve months at 76.3% gross margin) are the only pools large enough to move group growth; wearables grow 2.4% a year to 2030 (IDC, S85).
:::

arguments.markdown:
Apple is a high-quality compounder whose price already capitalises a peak margin and a contested services annuity, so the risks that matter destroy the multiple, not the balance sheet, and none is priced at $344.63. At that price on 2026-10-30 the shares trade at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and the base DCF at a 9.0% cost of equity is $212. Eight risks follow: two are fatal to the price, the rest execution. The strategic risk is AI defending the price without widening the moat. [S7, S97, S10]

::: risk-matrix
| Risk | Probability | Impact | Level | Timing | Signpost | Mitigation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Memory cost pushes hardware gross margin below 46% | High, over 60% | EPS -6% per 200bp; -25% to -30% value | Critical | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | Product margin under 37%; DRAM/NAND prices | Enter at $270 only on the $9.27+ EPS case | S17, S6, S99, S136 |
| Google search payment cut or banned on appeal | Medium, 20-25% | EPS -10% to -13%; value -15% to -20% | High | 2027, D.C. Circuit No. 26-5023 | Argument schedule; renewal terms | Cap the position | S70, S76, S135 |
| Multiple reverts to the 31.0x four-year mean | Medium-high, 40-60% | -21.5% at 31x; -38% at 24.6x | High | 0-12 months | Ten-year yield above 5%; forward P/E above 40x | No position at $344.63 | S97, S10 |
| EU DMA fee band spreads to other markets | Medium, 20-40% | EU operating income -1% to -2%; -5% if it spreads | Medium | From 2026-10-01 | Services growth below 10%; developer migration | Underwrite 10-12% services | S77, S78, S102 |
| AI cycle fails; Gemini reprices per device | Medium, 20-40% | EPS -5% to -8% | High | FY2027 | Siri beta exit; services margin | Treat AI as a cost line | S111, S6, S137 |
| China demand falls 20% in H2 2026 | Medium, 30-50% | Revenue -3.5%; EPS -5% to -6% | Medium | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | China revenue; Q4 tracker data | Do not capitalise 30% China growth | S96, S84, S87 |
| Cash quality and inventory | Medium, 30-50% | FCF -$1.9bn to $123.2bn, 40.8x; inventory -$3.3bn | Low | 10-K, 2026-11-02 | Other-liabilities note; inventory $11.1bn | Underwrite the $123.2bn case | S6, S5, S17 |
| Governance and key-person | Low, under 20% | Value -5% to -10% | Low | 12-24 months | No named successor; director exits | Board refresh; retention | S134, S133, S141, S11 |
:::

### The risk that breaks the thesis is the hardware margin, not the platform

The 50.1% gross margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; because that margin applies to $466.8bn of revenue, one point is $4.7bn of operating income. Memory prices rose 146% in Q1 2026 versus 2025; TrendForce's 30 September 2026 forecast puts Q4 DRAM contract prices 10-15% higher quarter on quarter and NAND 15-20% higher; the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials is up 38%, memory at 34% against 10%. Two hundred basis points off the margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of the trailing $8.72; a 46% margin, 200bp below the 48% top of the base range, takes FY2027 EPS from $9.79 to $9.27 and, at 29x, puts fair value at $269 — the entry price, not a discount. [S17, S6, S99, S136]

::: info danger
**A memory-led gross margin below 46% breaks earnings and the multiple at once.** The margin applies to all $466.8bn of revenue, Apple cannot re-price handsets inside a quarter, and 39.5x leaves no room for a 6% EPS cut: 200bp also invites a de-rating from 35x forward to the 31x mean, together a 25-30% drawdown. The signpost is the December-quarter margin guide on 2026-11-02 (S17, S6, S136).
:::

### The search payment is a renegotiation risk until the appeal says otherwise

The trial record put the payment at $20bn in 2022 — 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and 15% of operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy preserved non-exclusive payments; the American Antitrust Institute's 4 August 2026 brief asks the D.C. Circuit to strike it, and Google's appeal, No. 26-5023, with the DOJ's cross-appeal, stays live into 2027. I price a 20-25% probability of a ban at -10% to -13% of EPS and -15% to -20% of value. The EU fee schedule from 2026-10-01 — 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission — is modest in situ: Europe is 26.7% of nine-month revenue and each $1bn of commission lost is $0.75bn of gross profit. A 5-15% band extended to the United States would reset services growth to high single digits. [S70, S76, S77, S79, S135]

### The growth swing factors are AI and China

Siri shipped as an English beta on 2026-09-14 on a Gemini model licensed at a reported $1bn a year. Apple rents the capability and books the bill in operating expense; no filing names an AI profit-and-loss owner after the 2025-12-01 reorganisation, and X Corp. and xAI's suit survived dismissal. A $1bn licence is 0.6% of operating income, so the base case holds while pricing is annual; per-device pricing across 2.5bn devices would land in the 76.3% services margin, and whether a licensed assistant sells $1,199 handsets is the swing factor. China is a shrinking pool, not a lost share war: Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's, with Apple at 19.5% against Huawei's 21.3%. Greater China was 17.8% of nine-month FY2026 revenue; IDC sees the decline widening to 20% in H2 2026, and a 20% China decline is 3.5% of group revenue and 5-6% of EPS. Supply adds India — 25% of iPhones, incentives expired 2026-03-31, costs above China's — and Section 301 duties replacing the IEEPA tariffs struck down on 2026-02-20. [S111, S6, S127, S137, S96, S84, S87, S115]

### Valuation is the risk, and the entry ladder assumes the base EPS

At 39.5x, Apple sits at a five-year high for a company guiding 9-11% growth, and 40.2x trailing free cash flow of $125.1bn (39.5-41.0x across the $122.6-127.3bn band, on $5,029.6bn) makes the multiple the largest driver of return: reversion to the 31.0x mean costs 21.5%, reversion to the 24.6x FY2022 trough 38%. Each 50bp on the cost of equity moves the DCF 15-18%; the ten-year is 4.93% against a 7.0% implied return. A 30% revenue fall leaves $326.8bn; on the 43.0% nine-month incremental operating margin it leaves $94.6bn of operating income and $5.4 of EPS, but that is an up-cycle margin. On the FY2021-FY2025 average gross margin of 44.5%, with $72.3bn of operating expense held flat, gross profit is $145.3bn, operating income $73.0bn and EPS $4.10 at the 17.3% tax rate on 14.75bn diluted shares — a 58% decremental margin, not 43%; a 10% cost cut lifts EPS to $4.50, and the FY2016-FY2025 average margin of 41.4% gives $3.54. At 29x that is $103-131, at or below the $133 DCF bear. A market 50% smaller is revenue 35% lower and EPS $3.52, $70-88 at 20-25x. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn, 56.4-58.6x, covering the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of buybacks and dividends; a 30% inventory write-down is $3.3bn, 1.9% of operating income; 100 basis points on $84.3bn of debt is $0.84bn, 0.5%. Apple survives all of them on $62.2bn of net cash and $146.5bn of securities; the equity does not. The entry ladder is the same single-point bet: 0.75-1.0% at $270 is 27.6x only on FY2027 EPS of $9.79. A 46% gross margin takes EPS to $9.27 and $270 to 29.1x; a search cut of 12.9% takes $9.79 to $8.53 and, with the margin, to $8.07, so $270 becomes 31.7x to 33.5x against the 31.0x four-year mean and $245 becomes 28.7x to 30.4x. The same 27.6x is $223-235 on $8.07-8.53. The ladder needs a condition, not a new number: $270 only if the 2026-11-02 guide holds FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and December gross margin at 47%; otherwise the first tranche belongs at $235 and the second at $210, with the 5% cap unchanged. [S10, S97, S6, S5, S151, S70]

### Governance, unknowns and the call

Governance and key-person risk are monitors. Cook is Executive Chair and Ternus CEO under a nine-director board. Srouji's 2025-12-06 departure report is superseded by his 2026-04-20 promotion to Chief Hardware Officer with hardware engineering added to his silicon remit, which concentrates rather than removes the dependency. Cash quality is smaller than it looked: the $13,531M non-current liability build against $13,270M of gross intangibles added reads as deferred consideration, but net of a $4,128M current-liability fall it is $9,403M, inside the $10,016M line; if unpaid, free cash flow is $123.2bn, inside the $122.6-127.3bn band. Outside the filings: a Taiwan Strait disruption stopping 2nm supply, and an appellate remedy treating the Gemini default as the next search payment. The downside is a de-rating, not insolvency, so position size carries the risk; open diligence is the December-quarter margin guide, the 10-K working-capital note, the appellate schedule and the Gemini renewal terms. None changes the call: the price, not the business, is the problem, and the $270 entry holds only if December confirms the margin trough and EPS at $9.27 or better. [S134, S133, S141, S11, S5, S6]

arguments.markdown:
Apple's markets are large but no longer volume-growth markets: the smartphone unit pool is contracting at the fastest rate on record in 2026 while its dollar value rises, so growth to 2030 must come from holding more than 40% of smartphone value, monetising a record installed base through services, and a foldable and AI-driven cycle, not from market growth. Apple's revenue compounded 3.3% from FY2021 to FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and then accelerated to 16% in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone revenue up 22% [S5, S6].

| Measure | Figure | Period | Method and note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global smartphone units | 1.26B | 2025 | Counterpoint full year, +2% YoY; Omdia 1.25B | S92 |
| Global smartphone units | just over 1.0B | 2026E | IDC, -16.7% YoY, steepest annual fall on record | S84 |
| Global smartphone value | $613B | 2026E | IDC, +6.3% YoY | S84 |
| Global smartphone ASP | $581 | 2026E | IDC, +27.6%; Omdia independently $565 (+21%) | S84, S88 |
| Premium segment (wholesale ASP $600+) | 29% of units | H1 2026 | Counterpoint; 25% in H1 2025, 20% in H1 2022 | S94 |
| Apple iPhone revenue | $209.6B FY2025; $196.5B 9M FY2026 | FY2025 / 9M FY2026 | Apple filings; +22% in 9M FY2026 | S5, S6 |
| Apple implied iPhone revenue per unit | $832 FY2025; $1,101 2026E | FY2025 / 2026E | Calculated: iPhone revenue / iOS units (252M = 20% of 1.26B; 238M = 23.6% of 1.01B) | S5, S6, S92, S84 |
| Apple share of smartphone value | 36% FY2025; 42.7% 2026 | FY2025 / 2026 | Calculated: iPhone revenue / market value | S5, S6, S92, S88 |

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units. TAM: IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while value rises 6.3% to $613B on a 27.6% ASP increase to $581, against Omdia's independent $565 (+21%). SAM: the premium segment (29% of units at $600 or more) plus the iOS installed base for services, where Apple's 65% premium share sets the addressable pool. SOM: Apple's current capture, $466.8B of trailing-twelve-month revenue to June 2026, of which $245.5B is iPhone and $120.5B services. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line. The mechanism is a memory cost shock: NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier are passed into shelf prices, so the market is being repriced, not expanded [S84, S88, S94, S6].

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026 from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those units with 9% growth. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3%. Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B. Value capture, not unit share, is the franchise an investor is buying [S94, S92, S84, S5, S6, S88].

### The 27.6% price rise is cost pass-through, and Apple is pricing above it

The increase is not demand-led. IDC attributes the 27.6% ASP rise to a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM up more than 300% and passed into shelf prices, and TrendForce shows the cost landing on Apple directly: the iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials rose 38% year on year, memory reaching 34% of the BOM in Q3 2026 against one-tenth a year earlier. Apple then raised Pro and Pro Max list prices by $100 and held the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027. What supports willingness to pay is sell-through at those prices: Counterpoint recorded iPhone 18 Pro sales up 23.5% in the first three weeks in China, and Apple's installed base reached an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter. What weakens it: Apple discloses no upgrade rate or unit volumes, so an upgrade-cycle claim rests on third-party panels, and IDC attributes part of China's Q3 strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half increases, with the market possibly down 20% in H2 2026. On IDC's unit base Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose from $832 in FY2025 to $1,101 annualised in 2026, 32% against the market's 27.6%; on the higher 261M unit estimate for FY2026 the rise is 21%. Apple is pricing above the market average, but the magnitude rests on a unit count it does not publish: the gain is cost recovery plus Pro mix, not proof of an upgrade super-cycle. A consumer-panel upgrade rate would settle it and is not available here [S84, S99, S112, S96, S17, S87, S74].

Three pools can add revenue to 2030, and only one is large enough to change the trajectory. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Services: $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026, up 14.1% in nine months at a 76.3% gross margin, against a $1.34T advertising pool in 2026 and an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods and services in 2025. Wearables and PC: a 2.4% CAGR market to 2030 with smartwatches shrinking 3.7% in 2026 while glasses grow 18.1%, and Apple took 18.2% of combined PC and tablet units in Q2 2026. The non-phone pools, $33.7B of Mac and $35.7B of wearables in FY2025, are too small to carry group growth alone [S84, S6, S17, S89, S83, S85, S152, S5].

| Region | Market size (latest dated) | Growth | Company's position | Barriers | Key competitors | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Americas | Not published; global $613B (2026E) | Apple +11.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; home market; 42.9% of FY2025 revenue | US tariffs; platform antitrust | Samsung, Google, Motorola | S84, S5, S6 |
| Europe | Not published | Apple +16.1% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 26.7% of revenue | DMA take-rate cuts from 2026-10-01; GDPR | Samsung, Xiaomi, Google | S77, S6 |
| Greater China | 66M units in Q2 2026 | Market -10% in Q3 2026 (Counterpoint), -15.4% (IDC); Apple +30.0% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 19.5% in Q3 2026 on Counterpoint and 17.8% on IDC, against Huawei's 21.3% and 21.1%; Apple +4.8 points YoY | Market access; local champion; data rules; WeChat as a distribution layer | Huawei, OPPO, vivo, Xiaomi, Honor | S139, S140, S96, S87, S6 |
| Japan | Not published | Apple +10.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 6.9% of revenue | Yen weakness; carrier-controlled channel | Samsung, Google, Sharp | S6 |
| Rest of Asia-Pacific | Not published; emerging markets forecast down more than 20% in 2026 | Apple +19.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 8.1% of revenue; India manufacturing and retail | Price sensitivity; tariffs | Samsung, Xiaomi, vivo, OPPO, Transsion | S84, S6 |

Geography splits the durability question. Greater China was 15.5% of FY2025 revenue and grew 30% in the first nine months of FY2026; Europe is 26.7% and grew 16%, the Americas 42.9% and 11%, Japan 6.9% and 10%, Rest of Asia-Pacific 8.1% and 19%. China is the most fragile in size, not share: the market fell 10% in Q3 2026 to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 on Counterpoint's count, yet Apple's share rose 4.8 points to 19.5%, while IDC's lower 17.8% counts shipments rather than sell-through, a gap consistent with channel inventory drawing down. The EU cut the commission on externally distributed digital transactions to 5% from 1 October 2026. Demand is organic consumer replacement, not policy-created: China's subsidies faded in 2026 and India's incentives are supply-side. The budget owner is the consumer or a carrier financing plan; the procurement cycle follows the September launch. Confidence is high on 2026 data and low on 2027-2030 regional sizing, because regional market values are paywalled and Apple discloses no units; the open questions are how much iPhone growth is units versus price, whether services growth is users or price, and how much memory cost Apple can pass through in FY2027 [S6, S139, S140, S96, S77, S84].

::: evidence
**Apple's markets are growing in dollars while shrinking in units, so its growth is price- and share-led, not market-led.**

The global pool is $613B of smartphone value in 2026 against just over 1.0B units, with a 27.6% ASP increase doing the work volume used to do (IDC, S84). Premium concentration of 29% of units and Apple's 65% share of it explain why it captures 36-43% of value on 20-24% of units (Counterpoint, S94; S5, S6). The 2026 price rise is cost pass-through — TrendForce puts memory at 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials against 10% a year earlier (S99) — and Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose 32% on IDC's unit base against 27.6% for the market (S5, S6, S92, S84). Foldables ($45.7B of category value by 2027) and services ($120.5B trailing twelve months at 76.3% gross margin) are the only pools large enough to move group growth; wearables grow 2.4% a year to 2030 (IDC, S85).
:::

China is where the share question splits. Counterpoint's 19.5% and IDC's 17.8% measure different things, sell-through against shipments, and the 1.7-point gap is consistent with channel inventory drawing down after the iPhone 18 Pro launch; both trackers agree that Huawei leads (21.3% and 21.1%), that Apple gained share while the market fell (10% on Counterpoint's count, 15.4% on IDC's) to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012, and that Apple's Greater China revenue grew 30% in the first nine months of FY2026 [S139, S140, S96, S87]. The vulnerability is pool size and price level, not lost share: IDC expects component costs elevated through much of 2027, Apple raised Pro prices by $100 and holds the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027, so part of the Q3 gain is pull-forward and launch timing. Huawei remains the most dangerous rival to the hardware pool because it is the only one that takes premium share in a large market while funding its own silicon, OS and supply chain, with CNY192.3B of R&D on 21.8% of CNY880.9B of 2025 revenue [S86].

The distribution pool is where the newest competition is. Epic won a Ninth Circuit ruling on 2025-12-11 that the 27% commission Apple charged on link-outs had a prohibitive effect, collapsing the practical difference between in-app purchase and external payment [S69, S79]. Apple's EU answer from 1 October 2026 is a 26% commission on in-app purchases, 20% on alternative payment processing, 15% on link-outs and a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web, after the European Commission fined it EUR500M in 2025; AltStore PAL, Aptoide and Setapp Mobile exist only because the DMA compels Apple to admit them [S77, S102, S78]. The rent at stake is the highest-margin line Apple has: services earned $120.5B on a trailing-twelve-month basis to June 2026 at a 76.3% gross margin, and Europe is 26.7% of group revenue [S6]. No alternative storefront discloses meaningful EU share, so the near-term effect is a price war over 5-15 points of take rate rather than a transfer of volume.

The assistant layer is the threat Apple has least control over. ChatGPT reached 900M weekly active users and 50M paying subscribers by 2026-02-27, distribution comparable to a second operating system [S153]. The exposure is indirect but lands on a real pool: if users ask an assistant rather than search, the roughly $20B a year Google pays Apple for the Safari default, disclosed at 36% of Safari search ad revenue, loses its rationale [S70, S80]. Microsoft attacks the same layer from the enterprise side with Copilot and Copilot+ PCs, yet the measurable outcome is the opposite of a rout: in Q2 2026 Windows personal computing device shipments fell 6.7% while macOS grew 17.4%, and Apple held 18.2% of the combined PC and tablet market to Lenovo's 20.1% [S152]. Neither Microsoft nor IDC discloses Windows on Arm's share, which is itself a finding, and Microsoft's 10-K describes Windows as competing with "alternative platforms and devices" without claiming share gains [S49]. Open-weight models matter more than either vendor: the AI Index puts DeepSeek-R1 level with the top US model in February 2025 and the US lead at 2.7% by March 2026, so model capability is not a moat Apple can charge for, and Apple has already licensed Gemini for its next Siri, converting a would-be differentiator into a cost line [S155, S111].

In China the substitute is not a rival phone but a rival operating system inside the phone. Weixin reached 1,418M combined monthly users at 2025-12-31 and Tencent grew marketing services 19% to RMB145.0B on closed-loop advertising into Mini Programs, Mini Shops and Mini Games [S154]. Commerce and lightweight apps that run inside WeChat never pass through Apple's store, so the China services pool has a ceiling set by a company Apple does not compete with on hardware, whatever its handset share. The same logic caps the foldable opportunity: Apple's newest hinge patent family is co-assigned with supplier Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix, so even the mechanical exclusivity over Samsung and Chinese entrants is partial [S148, S150].

Apple's wedge is silicon, OS control and an installed base at an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter, which supports 40.1% product gross margins while Samsung's mobile division loses money and Xiaomi earns 8.5% [S17, S91, S90]. That wedge defends the hardware pool, which integration protects, and does not defend the distribution pool, which regulation is dismantling. The competitive position supports a quality-compounder view with a regulated ceiling on services and an unpriced assistant threat, not a share-gain growth story; confidence is high on hardware share, medium on China because two trackers use different bases, and medium-low on the assistant threat, where displacement has not yet shown in services growth of 14.1% in nine months [S6].

A discounted cash flow is the right instrument for a company whose value is almost all terminal, and the least forgiving. I take FY2026 revenue of $477.1bn (nine months actual of $364.4bn plus the guided $112.7bn fourth quarter), growth fading from 9% to 5%, a 33% operating margin, a 17.5% tax rate and capital expenditure 0.2 points above depreciation. The market price is reached near a 7.1% discount rate, and each 50bp on the rate moves value by 15-18%. That is the whole question: whether a 4.93% risk-free rate leaves room for a 7.1% required return on equity.

The two bulls are not the same animal. The DCF bull at an 8.5% cost of equity, a 35% operating margin and 14% first-year growth is worth $277 — 20% below the price — because it still discounts cash flows at 3.6 points above the 4.93% risk-free rate. The $357 that the thesis weights as its bull is a multiple-based target: 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20, which is today's 35.2x forward multiple held on earnings 4.2% above the $9.79 base. It is what the market would pay if the multiple does not compress, not what the business is worth on its cash flows. The $80 gap between them is the value of the multiple itself, and it is the single largest assumption in the case [S6, S7, S10, S97].

The entry ladder should not hang on one EPS point, so the bridge matters. Trailing diluted EPS is $8.72: FY2025 $7.46 plus nine months of FY2026 $6.88 less nine months of FY2025 $5.62. The September quarter, on the guided 9-11% revenue growth at the $112.7bn midpoint, my 47.5% gross-margin assumption, operating expenses near the June quarter's $19.1bn and a 17.3% tax rate, adds $1.93-1.99, for FY2026E EPS of $8.81-8.87. The 35.2x forward multiple then implies FY2027E EPS of $9.79 — 10.4-11.1% growth, consistent with S&P Global Market Intelligence's consensus iPhone revenue of $277.4bn (+9.9%) plus a 1.8% lower share count. FY2029E EPS of $11.45 in the exit analysis is 8.2% a year from there, below the iPhone growth rate. Every step is an assumption, but the chain is visible; the $9.79 is implied by the multiple rather than taken from a licensed consensus feed [S5, S6, S71, S72, S97].

Splitting Apple up shows how much of the price is a single-security premium. Services produced $120.5bn of trailing revenue at a 76.0% gross margin and hardware $346.3bn at 39.1%; allocating the $72.3bn of operating expense 40/60 toward services gives services EBIT of $62.7bn and hardware of $92.1bn. At 23x and 12x — between Microsoft's 23.6x and HP's 9.6x — the parts plus $62.2bn of net cash are worth $177 a share, or $238 at 28x and 18x. The largest single risk inside services is the Google default-search payment, put at $20bn a year; the remedies ruling in United States v. Google barred exclusivity without banning the payments, which reduces that risk to a renegotiation rather than a loss, though the case is on appeal [S5, S70, S101].

Three scenarios bracket the answer, and the price sits at the top of them. The scenario range runs from $241 at 24.6x FY2027E EPS to $357 at 35x $10.20, around a $284 base and a $291.5 probability-weighted value 15% below the price; the DCF range of $133-$277 sits mostly beneath it. At $344.63 the buyer pays 121% of the scenario base and 97% of the scenario bull, so the bull returns 3.6% before the dividend while the base costs 18% and the bear 30% — negative asymmetry on the sell side's own earnings. The DCF bull at $277 is 20% below the market and does not rescue the price. A margin of safety has to come from entry: $270 is 27.6x FY2027E $9.79, 95% of the scenario base and 12% above the scenario bear, and it is where the three-year return spans 5.0-13.3% across 27-34x exits; $245 is 25.0x and 86% of the base, $225 is 23.0x and 79%. Each step down also raises the buyback's retirement rate from 1.6% of the shares at today's price to 2.1% at $270. The conclusion is a price range, not a point: own Apple below the high-$200s, or on evidence that FY2027 EPS is tracking above $10.20; at $344.63 the market has already paid for the bull [S6, S7, S97].

The counter-case deserves its weight. The discount rate is a judgement, not an observation: at 7.1% the base DCF reaches the market price, and quality franchises in a high-rate world have held premium multiples for years. What I will not concede is a margin of safety: on every operating assumption I can defend, the buyer's return is set by the exit multiple, which already sits at the top of its own historical range. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the gap to intrinsic value, because it rests on a cost of equity nobody observes. The sell-side targets I can see — $338-355 across four retail aggregators, with TickFlow at $339.35 from 50 analysts and vcpscanner at $340.88 from 112 — are unverified, cluster at the price rather than at intrinsic value, and are not a substitute for a licensed consensus feed, which the register does not hold [S142, S144, S157, S158].
