| Samsung | Galaxy S26, Z Fold 7 | Android; Exynos 2600 | Unrestricted | Foldable at parity | Premium | 19% global 2025; 23% Q3 2026 | Foldable head start; carrier breadth | Mobile division lost KRW0.6T in Q3 2026 | S91, S92, S120 |
| Huawei | Mate, Pura; HarmonyOS | Kirin; HarmonyOS NEXT | China scale; US export curbs | Premium camera and battery | Premium | 21.3% China Q3 2026 (Counterpoint); 21.1% (IDC) | Domestic supply chain; HarmonyOS NEXT 1.6% of global PCD | Little share outside China | S139, S140, S86, S152 |
| Epic Games, AltStore PAL, Aptoide, Setapp Mobile | Fortnite; Epic Games Store; alternative iOS stores | Direct distribution, sideloading | Won contempt ruling; 27% link-out fee prohibited; EU 5% CTC | Legal leverage on the take rate | Free or commission | Not disclosed | Developer alignment; EU regulation | No hardware; small catalogues; EU only | S69, S79, S77, S102, S78 |
| OpenAI | ChatGPT, agent apps | GPT-5.x; cloud inference | Copyright and safety scrutiny | 900M weekly users; 50M paying | Free and subscription | Not disclosed | Consumer AI brand | No device or OS; pays for compute | S153 |
| Microsoft | Copilot, Copilot+ PCs, Windows on Arm | Windows on x86 and Arm | Unrestricted | Windows PCD down 6.7% in Q2 2026 | Bundled with OEM licences | Arm share not disclosed | Enterprise base; Office | Has not taken share from the Mac | S49, S152 |
| Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral | Llama, DeepSeek, Mistral | Open-weight models | Mixed licences; Chinese models restricted in some markets | DeepSeek-R1 levelled with the top US model, February 2025 | Free or self-hosted | Not disclosed | Cost; local deployment | No consumer distribution | S155 |
| Tencent | WeChat, Mini Programs, Mini Shops | Super-app distribution | Chinese regulation | 1,418M monthly users; Mini Program ad growth | Free to users | Not disclosed | Owns China's messaging graph | China only | S154 |

China is where the share question splits. Counterpoint's 19.5% and IDC's 17.8% measure sell-through against shipments, and the 1.7-point gap is consistent with channel inventory drawing down after launch; both trackers agree Huawei leads (21.3% and 21.1%), that Apple gained share while the market fell 10% on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's, and that Apple's Greater China revenue grew 30% in 9M FY2026. The vulnerability is pool size, not lost share: Pro prices rose $100 and the standard iPhone 18 waits until spring 2027, so part of the Q3 gain is pull-forward. Huawei is the most dangerous rival to the hardware pool: the only one taking premium share in a large market while funding its own silicon, OS and supply chain, with CNY192.3B of R&D [S139, S140, S96, S87, S86].

The distribution pool is where the newest competition is. Epic won a Ninth Circuit ruling on 2025-12-11 that the 27% commission Apple charged on link-outs had a prohibitive effect, collapsing the gap between in-app purchase and external payment. Apple's EU answer from 1 October 2026 is a 26% commission on in-app purchases, 15% on link-outs and a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web. The rent at stake is Apple's highest-margin line: services earned $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026 at a 76.3% gross margin. No alternative storefront discloses meaningful EU share, so the near-term effect is a price war over 5-15 points of take rate, not a shift of volume [S69, S79, S77, S102, S78, S6].

| Substitute | Apple profit pool attacked | Size of the pool | Mechanism | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Epic Games and DMA storefronts | App Store commission | Services $120.5B TTM, 76.3% margin | Take rate falls from 30% to 5-15%; the 27% link-out fee is unenforceable | S69, S77, S6 |
| OpenAI and assistant apps | Search licensing and app discovery | Google pays Apple about $20B a year for the Safari default | Answers replace queries; the assistant becomes the discovery layer | S70, S80, S153 |
| Microsoft Copilot and Windows on Arm | Mac hardware | Mac $33.7B of FY2025 revenue | Copilot+ PCs at price and feature parity | S152, S5 |
| Open-weight models | Apple Intelligence differentiation | Not separately disclosed | A 2.7% capability gap removes any premium for model quality | S155 |
| WeChat mini-programmes | China App Store commission | Not disclosed | Commerce runs inside the super-app, outside Apple's billing | S154 |

The assistant layer is the threat Apple controls least. ChatGPT reached 900M weekly active users by 2026-02-27, and if users ask an assistant rather than search, the roughly $20B a year Google pays Apple loses its rationale. Microsoft attacks the same layer from the enterprise side with Copilot and Copilot+ PCs, yet the measurable outcome is the opposite of a rout: in Q2 2026 Windows personal computing device shipments fell 6.7% while macOS grew 17.4%. Windows on Arm share is undisclosed, and Microsoft's 10-K describes Windows as competing with alternative platforms without claiming share gains. Open-weight models matter more than either vendor: the AI Index puts DeepSeek-R1 level with the top US model in February 2025 and the US lead at 2.7% by March 2026, so model capability is not a moat Apple can charge for, and Apple has licensed Gemini for its next Siri, converting a differentiator into a cost line [S153, S70, S80, S152, S49, S155, S111].

In China the substitute is not a rival phone but a rival operating system inside the phone. Weixin reached 1,418M combined monthly users at 2025-12-31 and Tencent grew marketing services 19% to RMB145.0B on closed-loop advertising into Mini Programs and Mini Shops; commerce inside WeChat never passes through Apple's store, so the China services pool has a ceiling set by a company Apple does not compete with. Apple's newest hinge patent family is co-assigned with supplier Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix, so even mechanical exclusivity over Samsung and Chinese entrants is partial [S154, S148, S150].

| Product | Position | Challenger | Niche | Emerging threat | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone (premium) | Leader: Apple | Samsung | Google Pixel | Huawei in China; foldables | S94, S139, S140 |
| Mac and iPad | Leader in detachables: Apple (55.3%) | Lenovo (25.6% of notebooks) | HP, Dell workstations | Copilot+ PCs | S152 |
| App distribution | Leader in its own store: Apple | Epic and DMA storefronts | AltStore PAL, Aptoide | WeChat mini-programmes in China | S69, S77, S154 |
| Assistant and AI | Leaders: Google Gemini, OpenAI | Apple | Meta and Mistral open weights | Chinese open-weight models | S153, S155, S111 |

Apple's wedge is silicon, OS control and an installed base at an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter, which supports 40.1% product gross margins while Samsung's mobile division loses money. That wedge defends the hardware pool, not the distribution pool that regulation is dismantling. The position supports a quality-compounder view with a regulated ceiling on services and an unpriced assistant threat, not a share-gain story; confidence is high on hardware share, medium on China because the trackers use different bases, and medium-low on the assistant threat, where displacement is absent from services growth of 14.1% in nine months [S17, S91, S6].

::: quad
| Quadrant | Points | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Strengths | 65% of premium phone units; 40.1% product gross margin; $120.5B services at 76.3% gross margin | S94, S17, S6 |
| Weaknesses | 19.5% China share against Huawei's 21.3%; no advertising scale; 50.4% of revenue from iPhone | S139, S140, S5 |
| Opportunities | Foldables above 17M units by 2027; services advertising; Mac share gains | S84, S152 |
| Threats | DMA take rate of 5-15%; Epic precedent; ChatGPT at 900M weekly users; memory costs up more than 300% | S77, S69, S153, S84 |
:::

::: evidence
**Apple's advantage is profit capture in hardware; its distribution rent is the exposed flank.**

Apple holds 20% of phone units but 65% of premium units and 36-43% of market value at a 40.1% product gross margin, against Xiaomi's 8.5% and a loss at Samsung's mobile division (S94, S84, S17, S90, S91). In China, Q3 2026 share is 19.5% on Counterpoint and 17.8% on IDC behind Huawei's 21.3% and 21.1% (S139, S140). The App Store take rate is being competed away by Epic and the DMA storefronts, and the assistant layer by ChatGPT's 900M weekly users (S69, S77, S153).
:::

The measure that survives is cash return on book capital: normalised free cash flow of $125.1B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, 65.2% against 57.3% in FY2025. With the ten-year Treasury at 4.93%, a 9-11% cost of equity is cleared several times; the constraint is the price. Nine-month buybacks and dividends of $73,872M are 72.4% of normalised free cash flow and net cash still rose. [S6, S7, S10]

### What $9.79 requires

The $284 base case, the $270 entry and the $440 sale trigger all divide by one number: $9.79 of FY2027 EPS, which is $344.63 divided by the 35.21x forward multiple quoted on 2026-10-30, not a figure Apple publishes. The gross margin carries the bridge: 48.0% is above FY2025's 46.9% and above the 47-48% band the record quarter supports once the refund is stripped, while iPhone revenue grows 9.9% against 8.3% for everything else and products earn 39.9% against services' 76.3%. Each 100 basis points is $0.30 of FY2027 EPS — $9.19 at 46.0%, $10.08 at 49.0% — so the earnings base is a band of $9.19-10.08, not a point.

### The downside is larger than the up-cycle margin implies

The 30% revenue-fall stress cannot be run at 43%. That rate says $1 of lost revenue costs $0.43 of operating income, but Apple's cost base does not fall with revenue: R&D rose 14.0% in FY2023 while revenue fell 2.8%. On through-cycle margins — revenue 30% lower at $364.6bn, gross margin at the FY2023 trough of 44.1%, operating expense held at $80.0bn — operating income falls to $80.8bn from $170.1bn, a 57% decremental margin, and EPS to $4.68, 52% below what the price implies. At 43% the same stress returns $5.95 and overstates stress EPS by 27%; at a 42.0% gross margin, between the FY2021 and FY2022 levels, EPS is $4.24. At the 24.6x multiple Apple carried out of FY2022 that is $104-115, which is why the $133 cash-flow bear is the permanent-loss anchor rather than a trading drawdown. A 30% fall needs a memory and remedy convergence no filed evidence supports: it belongs in the tail, priced. [S2, S3, S5, S6]

### One share count, one multiple

The 10-Q states 14,608,963 thousand shares outstanding at 27 June 2026, so market value at $344.63 is $5,034bn. The $5,029.6bn used in the valuation and exit work implies 14,594M shares, 15M fewer or 0.1%, consistent with July 2026 buybacks; the $5,072bn used for the business model is the 14,715M diluted quarterly average, 106M shares and 0.8% more. The multiple is 39.5x either way — price divided by the $8.72 diluted EPS — against 39.0x on trailing net income over the outstanding count, 0.2 turns no conclusion turns on. [S6, S7, S97]

The ladder is a single-point bet because $270 is 27.6x $9.79: on the low end the same $270 is 29.4x, on the high end 26.8x. In multiples it becomes $254-278 entry, $267-292 fair value and $414-454 sale, so three tranches at $278, $266 and $254 hold the multiple inside 27-28x whatever FY2027 delivers, and the sale becomes 44-48x forward rather than a price. A 6% lower earnings path turns the 9.9% three-year return at $270 into 7.6%.

### What the next print has to clear

Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026, guided to 9-11% growth ($111.7-113.7B off $102,466M) with iPhone growth in the mid-teens; consensus puts iPhone revenue at $252.4bn for FY2026 and $277.4bn for FY2027. After a 17.3% tax rate, 200 basis points of gross margin is $0.52 of trailing EPS (6.0%), 500 points $1.31 (15.0%), losing the $20B search payment $1.12 (12.9%) and a 10% fall in iPhone revenue $0.55 (6.3%). Gross margin moves the outcome most because it applies to all $466,823M of revenue. Earnings quality is not the constraint; the price is. Diligence: December-quarter gross-margin guidance, FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices, and what sits in the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities. [S71, S72]

arguments.markdown:
Apple is a superior franchise whose price already capitalises the scenario bull. At $344.63 on NasdaqGS (2026-10-30 20:00 UTC) and 14,715m diluted shares its market capitalisation is $5,071.2bn — not the $5,029.6bn screens show on 14,594m cover-page shares — and its enterprise value $5,009.1bn after $84.3bn of debt and $146.5bn of cash and securities. That is 39.3x trailing earnings ($5,071.2bn over $128,930M of net income) and 39.1x trailing NOPAT; the data feed's 39.5x is price over the $8.72 sum-of-quarters diluted EPS, a 0.2x gap that is the EPS approximation, not a different earnings base. Forward, 35.2x on the $9.79 that multiple implies, is 1.9 times the S&P 500's 18.7x forward multiple (FactSet, 2026-10-23) and a 95% premium to the 20.2x peer median. The price needs 6.5-7.0% perpetual growth at a 9.0-9.5% discount rate, or a 7.1% discount rate on my forecast, for revenue that compounded 3.3% a year from FY2021 to FY2025 [S6, S7, S97, S156].

| Liquidity | 40.41m shares and $13.84bn a day (20-day); 41.34m and $13.56bn (3-month) | S7 |

Samsung and Xiaomi file no US GAAP statements; their multiples are not disclosed here, so the hardware leg leans on HP and Dell.

The operating story that supports 39.3x is real but narrower than the headline. The June 2026 quarter grew revenue 16.4% to $109.4bn, with iPhone up 21.7% and Greater China up 22.4%, and the September quarter is guided to 9-11% growth. Against that, IDC expects global smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% in 2026, and TrendForce puts the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials up 38% year on year with memory at 34% of it, from 10% a year earlier. Apple is growing by price and mix in a shrinking unit market while its cost base rises; Samsung's mobile division lost money for the same reason. Price-led growth is the most reversible kind, and FY2027 gross margin is where the memory cycle will show [S17, S84, S99, S72].

Free cash flow is what the buyback and the model rest on, and the trailing figure carries an accrual that has to come out. Trailing FCF of $136.7bn is a 2.7% yield, but it includes $14.1bn from other current and non-current liabilities — $10.0bn in the nine months to June 2026 and $4.1bn in the September 2025 quarter — against a $2.5bn three-year average. Netting the line to those levels gives normalised FCF of $122.6-127.3bn, $125.1bn central: 0.95-0.99x net income, a 2.4-2.5% yield and 40.5x P/FCF on the $5,071.2bn market value. The $122.6bn floor treats the build as deferred consideration for $13.3bn of gross intangibles added. Shareholders have received $438.6bn of repurchases and $75.0bn of dividends in the five fiscal years to FY2025; no equity has been raised [S5, S6, S1].

A discounted cash flow is the right instrument for a company whose value is almost all terminal, and the least forgiving. I take FY2026 revenue of $477.1bn (nine months actual $364.4bn plus the guided $112.7bn fourth quarter), growth fading from 9% to 5%, a 33% operating margin and a 17.5% tax rate. At a 9.0% cost of equity — a 4.93% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a 1.05 beta — the shares are worth $212; the market price is reached near a 7.1% discount rate. The two bulls are not the same animal. The DCF bull at an 8.5% cost of equity, a 35% margin and 14% first-year growth is worth $277 — 20% below the price — because it still discounts at 3.6 points above the 4.93% risk-free rate. The $357 that the thesis weights as its bull is a multiple-based target: 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20, today's 35.2x forward multiple held on earnings 4.2% above the $9.79 base. It is what the market would pay if the multiple holds, not what the business is worth on its cash flows; the $80 gap is the value of the multiple itself [S6, S7, S10, S97].

| Sum of the parts | 23x services EBIT of $62.7bn, 12x hardware EBIT of $92.1bn, plus $62.2bn net cash; 28x/18x gives $238 | $177 | S6, S17, S14, S104 |
| Own-history multiple | 31.0x four-year mean P/E (FY2022-25; FY2021 price not available) on FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $303 | S7, S97 |

The entry ladder should not hang on one EPS point, so the bridge matters. Trailing diluted EPS is $8.72: FY2025 $7.46 plus nine months of FY2026 $6.88 less nine months of FY2025 $5.62. The September quarter, on the guided 9-11% revenue growth at the $112.7bn midpoint, a 47.5% gross margin, operating expenses near the June quarter's $19.1bn and a 17.3% tax rate, adds $1.93-1.99, for FY2026E EPS of $8.81-8.87. The 35.2x forward multiple then implies FY2027E EPS of $9.79 — 10.4-11.1% growth, consistent with S&P Global Market Intelligence's consensus iPhone revenue of $277.4bn (+9.9%) plus a 1.8% lower share count. FY2029E EPS of $11.45 in the exit analysis is 8.2% a year from there. The $9.79 is implied by the multiple rather than taken from a licensed consensus feed [S5, S6, S71, S72, S97].

| Scenario | Assumptions | Value per share | vs $344.63 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DCF bear | growth 4/3/2/2/2%, margin 30%, discount 9.5% | $133 | -61% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario bear | 24.6x FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $241 | -30% | S7, S97 |
| DCF base | growth 9/8/7/6/5%, margin 33%, discount 9.0% | $212 | -38% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario base | 29x FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $284 | -18% | S7, S97 |
| DCF bull | growth 14/11/9/7/6%, margin 35%, discount 8.5% | $277 | -20% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario bull | 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 | $357 | +3.6% | S7, S97 |
| Probability-weighted | 25/50/25 on the scenario values | $291.5 | -15% | S6, S7 |

Three scenarios bracket the answer, and the price sits at the top of them. The scenario range runs from $241 at 24.6x FY2027E EPS to $357 at 35x $10.20, around a $284 base and a $291.5 probability-weighted value 15% below the price; the DCF range of $133-$277 sits mostly beneath it, and the sum of the parts is $177-238. At $344.63 the buyer pays 121% of the scenario base and 97% of the scenario bull, so the bull returns 3.6% before the dividend while the base costs 18% and the bear 30%. A margin of safety has to come from entry: $270 is 27.6x FY2027E $9.79, 95% of the scenario base and 12% above the scenario bear, and it is where the three-year return spans 5.0-13.3% across 27-34x exits. The $20bn Google search payment survives as a renegotiation rather than a ban, but it is on appeal. The dated catalysts are the 2026-11-02 fourth-quarter release, the May 2027 buyback authorisation and the D.C. Circuit's search-remedy decision expected in 2027. The conclusion is a price range, not a point: own Apple below the high-$200s, or on evidence that FY2027 EPS is tracking above $10.20; at $344.63 the market has paid for the bull. The sell-side targets I can see — $338-355 across four retail aggregators, TickFlow $339.35 from 50 analysts and vcpscanner $340.88 from 112 — are unverified and cluster at the price rather than at intrinsic value [S5, S7, S70, S97, S101, S142, S144, S157, S158].

The counter-case deserves its weight. The discount rate is a judgement: at 7.1% the base DCF reaches the market price, and quality franchises have held premium multiples for years. What I will not concede is a margin of safety: on every operating assumption I can defend, the buyer's return is set by the exit multiple, which already sits at the top of its own historical range. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the gap to intrinsic value.

The June 2026 quarter grew revenue 16.4% to $109.4bn, with iPhone up 21.7% and Greater China up 22.4%, and the September quarter is guided to 9-11% growth. Against that, IDC expects global smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% in 2026, and TrendForce puts the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials up 38% year on year with memory at 34% of it, from 10% a year earlier. Apple is growing by price and mix in a shrinking unit market while its cost base rises; Samsung's mobile division lost money for the same reason. Price-led growth is the most reversible kind, and FY2027 gross margin is where the memory cycle will show [S17, S84, S99, S72].

Free cash flow is what the buyback and the model rest on, and the trailing figure carries an accrual that has to come out. Trailing FCF of $136.7bn is a 2.7% yield, but it includes $14.1bn from other current and non-current liabilities — $10.0bn in the nine months to June 2026 and $4.1bn in the September 2025 quarter — against a $2.5bn three-year average. Netting the line to those levels gives normalised FCF of $122.6-127.3bn, $125.1bn central: 0.95-0.99x net income, a 2.4-2.5% yield and 40.5x P/FCF on the $5,071.2bn market value. The $122.6bn floor treats the build as deferred consideration for $13.3bn of gross intangibles added. Shareholders have received $438.6bn of repurchases and $75.0bn of dividends in the five fiscal years to FY2025; no equity has been raised [S5, S6, S1].

A discounted cash flow is the right instrument for a company whose value is almost all terminal, and the least forgiving. I take FY2026 revenue of $477.1bn (nine months actual $364.4bn plus the guided $112.7bn fourth quarter), growth fading from 9% to 5%, a 33% operating margin and a 17.5% tax rate. At a 9.0% cost of equity — a 4.93% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a 1.05 beta — the shares are worth $212; the market price is reached near a 7.1% discount rate. The two bulls are not the same animal. The DCF bull at an 8.5% cost of equity, a 35% margin and 14% first-year growth is worth $277 — 20% below the price — because it still discounts at 3.6 points above the 4.93% risk-free rate. The $357 that the thesis weights as its bull is a multiple-based target: 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20, today's 35.2x forward multiple held on earnings 4.2% above the $9.79 base. It is what the market would pay if the multiple holds, not what the business is worth on its cash flows; the $80 gap is the value of the multiple itself [S6, S7, S10, S97].

| Method | Key inputs | Value per share | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| DCF, base | WACC 9.0%, terminal growth 4.0%, revenue 9/8/7/6/5%, margin 33%, tax 17.5% | $212 | S6, S10, S72 |
| DCF, bull | WACC 8.5%, margin 35%, revenue 14/11/9/7/6% | $277 | S6, S10, S72 |
| Scenario bull (multiple) | 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 | $357 | S7, S97 |
| Sum of the parts | 23x services EBIT of $62.7bn, 12x hardware EBIT of $92.1bn, plus $62.2bn net cash; 28x/18x gives $238 | $177 | S6, S17, S14, S104 |
| Own-history multiple | 31.0x four-year mean P/E (FY2022-25; FY2021 price not available) on FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $303 | S7, S97 |

The entry ladder should not hang on one EPS point, so the bridge matters. Trailing diluted EPS is $8.72: FY2025 $7.46 plus nine months of FY2026 $6.88 less nine months of FY2025 $5.62. The September quarter, on the guided 9-11% revenue growth at the $112.7bn midpoint, a 47.5% gross margin, operating expenses near the June quarter's $19.1bn and a 17.3% tax rate, adds $1.93-1.99, for FY2026E EPS of $8.81-8.87. The 35.2x forward multiple then implies FY2027E EPS of $9.79 — 10.4-11.1% growth, consistent with S&P Global Market Intelligence's consensus iPhone revenue of $277.4bn (+9.9%) plus a 1.8% lower share count. FY2029E EPS of $11.45 in the exit analysis is 8.2% a year from there. The $9.79 is implied by the multiple rather than taken from a licensed consensus feed [S5, S6, S71, S72, S97].

| Scenario | Assumptions | Value per share | vs $344.63 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DCF bear | growth 4/3/2/2/2%, margin 30%, discount 9.5% | $133 | -61% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario bear | 24.6x FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $241 | -30% | S7, S97 |
| DCF base | growth 9/8/7/6/5%, margin 33%, discount 9.0% | $212 | -38% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario base | 29x FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $284 | -18% | S7, S97 |
| DCF bull | growth 14/11/9/7/6%, margin 35%, discount 8.5% | $277 | -20% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario bull | 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 | $357 | +3.6% | S7, S97 |
| Probability-weighted | 25/50/25 on the scenario values | $291.5 | -15% | S6, S7 |

Three scenarios bracket the answer, and the price sits at the top of them. The scenario range runs from $241 at 24.6x FY2027E EPS to $357 at 35x $10.20, around a $284 base and a $291.5 probability-weighted value 15% below the price; the DCF range of $133-$277 sits mostly beneath it, and the sum of the parts is $177-238. At $344.63 the buyer pays 121% of the scenario base and 97% of the scenario bull, so the bull returns 3.6% before the dividend while the base costs 18% and the bear 30%. A margin of safety has to come from entry: $270 is 27.6x FY2027E $9.79, 95% of the scenario base and 12% above the scenario bear, and it is where the three-year return spans 5.0-13.3% across 27-34x exits. The $20bn Google search payment survives as a renegotiation rather than a ban, but it is on appeal. The dated catalysts are the 2026-11-02 fourth-quarter release, the May 2027 buyback authorisation and the D.C. Circuit's search-remedy decision expected in 2027. The conclusion is a price range, not a point: own Apple below the high-$200s, or on evidence that FY2027 EPS is tracking above $10.20; at $344.63 the market has paid for the bull. The sell-side targets I can see — $338-355 across four retail aggregators, TickFlow $339.35 from 50 analysts and vcpscanner $340.88 from 112 — are unverified and cluster at the price rather than at intrinsic value [S5, S7, S70, S97, S101, S142, S144, S157, S158].

The counter-case deserves its weight. The discount rate is a judgement, not an observation: at the low end of the plausible range the base DCF reaches the market price, and quality franchises have held premium multiples for years. What I will not concede is a margin of safety: on every operating assumption I can defend, the buyer's return is set by the exit multiple, which already sits at the top of its own historical range. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the gap to intrinsic value.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's earnings are cash-true and its returns real; what an investor pays $344.63 for is 39.5x a margin that a memory cycle and two legal remedies can move, on FY2027 earnings that require a gross margin above any year before 2026. Trailing free cash flow was $136,683M against net income of $128,930M — 1.06x, or 0.97x on a normalised $125,084M, on capex of 2.2% of revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft and 33.9% at Alphabet. Revenue rose from $383,285M in FY2023 to $466,823M trailing with operating margin up from 29.8% to 33.2%, and the nine months to 27 June 2026 earned a 43.0% incremental operating margin: $21,809M more operating income on $50,662M more revenue. That 43% is an up-cycle marginal rate. [S5, S6]

| Revenue | 383,285 | 391,035 | 416,161 | 364,357 | 466,823 | S5, S6 |
| Gross profit | 169,148 | 180,683 | 195,201 | 178,782 | 227,123 | S5, S6 |

| Net income | 96,995 | 93,736 | 112,010 | 101,464 | 128,930 | S5, S6 |

| Operating cash flow | 110,543 | 118,254 | 111,482 | 116,996 | 146,724 | S5, S6 |

### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

Gross margin went from 44.1% in FY2023 to 46.9% in FY2025, 49.1% in the nine months of FY2026 and 48.7% trailing; the June 2026 quarter printed 50.1%, a record. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9%, and the 30 July 2026 release attributes 2 points of the quarter's gross margin and $0.11 of its $2.02 EPS to tariff refunds. Against that, memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 and memory is now 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials against 10% a year earlier, and the 10-Q expects the component trends "to intensify". A 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1%, is the level to capitalise. [S17, S68, S99]

::: info warning
**Two percentage points of the record 50.1% gross margin are a one-off tariff refund, and memory is turning against the hardware line (S6, S17).**

The refund is 2 points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 quarterly EPS (S17); memory rose 146% and the 10-Q warns cost pressure will intensify (S6, S68). Two hundred basis points off trailing gross margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of $8.72.
:::

### Cash conversion is real, but a liability accrual did the lifting

Nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,242M to $116,996M against a $16,920M rise in net income, and the dominant line is other current and non-current liabilities: +$10,016M against −$15,161M a year earlier, when the Irish State Aid settlement sat in it. Its clean three-year average is $2,502M ($3,031M; −$248M; $4,724M), so the $14,101M it puts into trailing free cash flow is the soft spot. Replacing it with that average gives $125,084M, 0.97x net income; zeroing it gives $122,582M and its best clean year $127,306M, so the band is $122.6-127.3B and $125.1B the midpoint. The $13,270M of gross intangibles added against investing "other" of $1,780M suggests the $13,531M non-current build is deferred consideration, putting the figure at $123,152M. [S5, S6]

### The balance sheet is not the risk; the asking price is

At 27 June 2026 cash and marketable securities were $146,517M against debt of $84,344M — net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M nine months earlier while $62,094M of stock was retired. FY2025 notes carried $91.3B of principal with $12.4B due within twelve months; leases add $16.8B and purchase obligations $86.3B. Two items need a question: $2,604M of unrealised securities losses, and intangibles up to $25,417M net from $13,301M without the 10-Q saying what was bought. [S5, S6]

| Returns and working capital | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | TTM | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on equity | 171.9% | 157.4% | 171.4% | 148.8% | S5, S6 |
| Return on assets | 27.5% | 26.1% | 30.9% | 36.1% | S5, S6 |
| ROIC (equity + debt − cash; distorted) | 1,527% | 1,036% | 479% | 321% | S5, S6 |
| Net cash | 51,011 | 50,021 | 33,763 | 62,173 | S5, S6 |
| Days sales outstanding | 28.1 | 31.2 | 34.9 | 24.5 | S5, S6 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | −67.8 | −75.8 | −71.1 | −56.8 | S5, S6 |
| Effective tax rate | 14.7% | 24.1% | 15.6% | 17.3% | S5, S6 |

ROE of 148.8% and ROA of 36.1% are genuine; the 320.6% ROIC is an artefact of cash and negative working capital shrinking invested capital to $45,347M. The measure that survives is cash return on book capital: normalised free cash flow of $125.1B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, 65.2% against 57.3% in FY2025. With the ten-year Treasury at 4.93%, a 9-11% cost of equity is cleared several times; the constraint is the price. Nine-month buybacks and dividends of $73,872M are 72.4% of normalised free cash flow and net cash still rose. [S6, S7, S10]

### What $9.79 requires

The $284 base case, the $270 entry and the $440 sale trigger all divide by one number: $9.79 of FY2027 EPS, which is $344.63 divided by the 35.21x forward multiple quoted on 2026-10-30, not a figure Apple publishes. Rebuilt from filed and consensus inputs it needs consensus iPhone revenue of $277.4bn (+9.9%) and $243.4bn of everything else. [S71, S97]

| FY2027 build to $9.79 | Value | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $520.8bn | iPhone $277.4bn + $243.4bn; +9.2% on FY2026E $477.1bn | S71, S72 |
| Gross margin | 48.0% | $250.0bn gross profit | S6 |
| Operating expense | $80.0bn | nine months $56.4bn, held to 6.5% growth after 21.9% | S6 |
| Operating income | $170.1bn | 32.7% margin | derived |
| Other income; tax at 17.3% | $1.0bn; $29.6bn | trailing rates | S6 |
| Net income; diluted shares | $141.5bn; 14,450M | 14,715M less 1.8% buyback | S6 |
| EPS | $9.79 | $141.5bn ÷ 14,450M | S97 |

The gross margin carries the bridge: 48.0% is above FY2025's 46.9% and above the 47-48% band the record quarter supports once the refund is stripped, while iPhone revenue grows 9.9% against 8.3% for everything else and products earn 39.9% against services' 76.3%. Each 100 basis points is $0.30 of FY2027 EPS — $9.19 at 46.0%, $10.08 at 49.0% — so the earnings base is a band of $9.19-10.08, not a point.

### The downside is larger than the up-cycle margin implies

The 30% revenue-fall stress cannot be run at 43%. That rate says $1 of lost revenue costs $0.43 of operating income, but Apple's cost base does not fall with revenue: R&D rose 14.0% in FY2023 while revenue fell 2.8%. On through-cycle margins — revenue 30% lower at $364.6bn, gross margin at the FY2023 trough of 44.1%, operating expense held at $80.0bn — operating income falls to $80.8bn from $170.1bn, a 57% decremental margin, and EPS to $4.68, 52% below what the price implies. At 43% the same stress returns $5.95, overstating stress EPS by 27%; at a 42.0% gross margin EPS is $4.24. At the 24.6x multiple Apple carried out of FY2022 that is $104-115, which is why the $133 cash-flow bear is the permanent-loss anchor rather than a trading drawdown. A 30% fall needs a memory and remedy convergence no filed evidence supports: tail, priced. [S2, S3, S5, S6]

### One share count, one multiple

The 10-Q states 14,608,963 thousand shares outstanding at 27 June 2026, so market value at $344.63 is $5,034bn. The $5,029.6bn used in the valuation and exit work implies 14,594M shares, 15M fewer or 0.1%; the $5,072bn used for the business model is the 14,715M diluted quarterly average, 106M shares and 0.8% more. The multiple is 39.5x either way — price divided by the $8.72 diluted EPS — against 39.0x on trailing net income over the outstanding count; the difference is 0.2 turns. [S6, S7, S97]

The ladder is a single-point bet because $270 is 27.6x $9.79: on the low end of the band the same $270 is 29.4x, on the high end 26.8x. Priced in multiples, the entry is $254-278 (27.6x $9.19 to $10.08), fair value $267-292 and a sale at 44-48x forward, $414-454. Three tranches at $278, $266 and $254 hold the multiple inside 27-28x whatever FY2027 delivers, and a 6% lower earnings path turns the 9.9% three-year return at $270 into 7.6%.

### What the next print has to clear

Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026, guided to 9-11% growth ($111.7-113.7B off $102,466M); consensus puts iPhone revenue at $252.4bn for FY2026 and $277.4bn for FY2027. Gross margin moves the outcome most because it applies to all $466,823M of revenue. Earnings quality is not the constraint; the price is. Diligence: December-quarter gross-margin guidance, FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices, and what sits in the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities. [S71, S72]

arguments.markdown:
Apple closed at $344.63 on 30 October 2026, a $5,072bn market capitalisation and a 27.5% total return over twelve months; the last reported period is the June quarter, with Q4 FY2026 results due on 2 November 2026, so the price contains no post-results adjustment. The market it trades in is near its high: the S&P 500 at 7,580.07 is up 10.7% year to date and 3.4% below its record, the Nasdaq is 8.2% below its high, the VIX is 19.42 at the 77th percentile, and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.93%. Technology is the laggard, down 8.3% over one month while the SPY fell 0.9% — a regime that penalises long-duration multiples [S7, S97, S8, S9, S10].

The business is not the problem. Apple converts profit into cash at 0.97 times net income, 0.95 times at the low end of the normalised band, on capex of 2.2% of revenue; it holds $62,173M of net cash and earns 40.3% of gross profit from services on 25.8% of revenue; a 30% revenue fall still leaves the company solvent and stops the buyback rather than breaking the balance sheet. What has changed is the margin: the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin carried two points of tariff refunds, memory costs have turned, and the base case underwrites 47-48% [S6, S17].

The price is the problem. At 39.3 times trailing and 35.2 times forward earnings against 18.09 times for the S&P 500, the shares discount a 7.0% cost of equity or 6.4-6.9% perpetual growth; the DCF at 9.0% is $212, its 8.5% discount-rate bull is $277 (20% below the close), the sum of the parts is $177-238, and the base scenario is $284, 18% below the close. The recommendation rests on the base case and on the 25/50/25 probability-weighted value of $291.5, 15% below the price — not on either bull. The scenario bull is $357 at 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20, a 25% branch with a +4% return. The market is capitalising a peak margin and a peak multiple at the same time [S7, S97, S146].

Two facts would change the call. A gross margin at the low end of the range takes fair value to the first entry tranche, so the tranche becomes the base case rather than a discount to it; an appellate ban on the search payment moves the bear toward the discounted-cash-flow floor. The one question below decides which of the two the next twelve months delivers.

The view is non-consensus on price, not on franchise. The sell side's median target sits at the spot price, so the Street sees fair value where this analysis sees an overvaluation; the difference is the normalised margin and the exit multiple, not the quality of the installed base.

Positioning follows from that: zero today, a conditional staged entry below the base case, and a sell discipline tied to the multiple and to services growth. The first tranche at $270 requires the 2026-11-02 guide to hold FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and gross margin at 47%; if it fails, the first tranche moves to $235 and the second to $210. The first hard test is the FY2026 10-K and the December-quarter guide on 2 November 2026, two days after this version. The follow-up diligence is threefold: the working-capital and intangibles note in that filing, a primary consensus feed for FY2027 EPS, and the D.C. Circuit briefing and decision [S6, S7].

The payment is the largest single item in services and runs at near-pure margin. A ban or a materially lower rate resets the services multiple that carries most of the valuation and moves fair value from the base case toward the bear case, regardless of how well the hardware cycle trades.
:::

::: takeaways
1. Watchlist, not ownership: at $344.63 the shares trade at 35.2 times forward earnings against 18.09 for the index, and the base case of $284 is 18% below the price [S7, S97, S146].
2. The franchise is not the problem: services earn 40.3% of gross profit, cash conversion is 0.97x, 0.95x at the band floor, and net cash is $62,173M, so a 30% revenue fall leaves the company solvent [S6].
3. The entry is a price, not a narrative: a conditional 0.75-1.0% at $270 only if the 2 November guide holds FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and gross margin at 47%; otherwise $235, a second tranche at $245 or $210, and the 5% cap below $225 [S6, S7].
:::

arguments.markdown:
Apple is a superior franchise whose price already capitalises the scenario bull. At $344.63 on NasdaqGS (2026-10-30 20:00 UTC) and 14,715m diluted shares its market capitalisation is $5,071.2bn — not the $5,029.6bn screens show on 14,594m cover-page shares — and its enterprise value $5,009.1bn after $84.3bn of debt and $146.5bn of cash and securities. That is 39.3x trailing earnings ($5,071.2bn over $128,930M of net income) and 39.1x trailing NOPAT; the data feed's 39.5x is price over the $8.72 sum-of-quarters diluted EPS, a 0.2x gap that is the EPS approximation, not a different earnings base. Forward, 35.2x on the $9.79 that multiple implies, is 1.9 times the S&P 500's 18.7x forward multiple (FactSet, 2026-10-23) and a 95% premium to the 20.2x peer median. The price needs 6.5-7.0% perpetual growth at a 9.0-9.5% discount rate, or a 7.1% discount rate on my forecast, for revenue that compounded 3.3% a year from FY2021 to FY2025 [S6, S7, S97, S156].

Samsung and Xiaomi file no US GAAP statements; their multiples are not disclosed here, so the hardware leg leans on HP and Dell.

The operating story that supports 39.3x is real but narrower than the headline. The June 2026 quarter grew revenue 16.4% to $109.4bn, with iPhone up 21.7% and Greater China up 22.4%, and the September quarter is guided to 9-11% growth. Against that, IDC expects global smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% in 2026, and TrendForce puts the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials up 38% year on year with memory at 34% of it, from 10% a year earlier. Apple is growing by price and mix in a shrinking unit market while its cost base rises; Samsung's mobile division lost money for the same reason. Price-led growth is the most reversible kind, and FY2027 gross margin is where the memory cycle will show [S17, S84, S99, S72].

Free cash flow is what the buyback and the model rest on, and the trailing figure carries an accrual that has to come out. Trailing FCF of $136.7bn is a 2.7% yield, but it includes $14.1bn from other current and non-current liabilities — $10.0bn in the nine months to June 2026 and $4.1bn in the September 2025 quarter — against a $2.5bn three-year average. Netting the line to those levels gives normalised FCF of $122.6-127.3bn, $125.1bn central: 0.95-0.99x net income, a 2.4-2.5% yield and 40.5x P/FCF on the $5,071.2bn market value. The $122.6bn floor treats the build as deferred consideration for $13.3bn of gross intangibles added. Shareholders have received $438.6bn of repurchases and $75.0bn of dividends in the five fiscal years to FY2025; no equity has been raised [S5, S6, S1].

A discounted cash flow is the right instrument for a company whose value is almost all terminal, and the least forgiving. I take FY2026 revenue of $477.1bn (nine months actual $364.4bn plus the guided $112.7bn fourth quarter), growth fading from 9% to 5%, a 33% operating margin and a 17.5% tax rate. At a 9.0% cost of equity — a 4.93% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a 1.05 beta — the shares are worth $212; the market price is reached near a 7.1% discount rate. The two bulls are not the same animal. The DCF bull at an 8.5% cost of equity, a 35% margin and 14% first-year growth is worth $277 — 20% below the price — because it still discounts at 3.6 points above the 4.93% risk-free rate. The $357 that the thesis weights as its bull is a multiple-based target: 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20, today's 35.2x forward multiple held on earnings 4.2% above the $9.79 base. It is what the market would pay if the multiple holds, not what the business is worth on its cash flows; the $80 gap is the value of the multiple itself [S6, S7, S10, S97].

| DCF, bull | WACC 8.5%, margin 35%, revenue 14/11/9/7/6% | $277 | S6, S10, S72 |
| Scenario bull (multiple) | 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 | $357 | S7, S97 |
| Sum of the parts | 23x services EBIT of $62.7bn, 12x hardware EBIT of $92.1bn, plus $62.2bn net cash; 28x/18x gives $238 | $177 | S6, S17, S14, S104 |
| Own-history multiple | 31.0x four-year mean P/E (FY2022-25; FY2021 price not available) on FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $303 | S7, S97 |

The bridge matters. Trailing diluted EPS is $8.72: FY2025 $7.46 plus nine months of FY2026 $6.88 less nine months of FY2025 $5.62. The September quarter, on the guided 9-11% revenue growth at the $112.7bn midpoint, a 47.5% gross margin, operating expenses near the June quarter's $19.1bn and a 17.3% tax rate, adds $1.93-1.99, for FY2026E EPS of $8.81-8.87. The 35.2x forward multiple then implies FY2027E EPS of $9.79 — 10.4-11.1% growth, consistent with S&P Global Market Intelligence's consensus iPhone revenue of $277.4bn (+9.9%) plus a 1.8% lower share count. FY2029E EPS of $11.45 in the exit analysis is 8.2% a year from there. The $9.79 is implied by the multiple rather than taken from a licensed consensus feed [S5, S6, S71, S72, S97].

| Scenario | Assumptions | Value per share | vs $344.63 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DCF bear | growth 4/3/2/2/2%, margin 30%, discount 9.5% | $133 | -61% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario bear | 24.6x FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $241 | -30% | S7, S97 |
| DCF base | growth 9/8/7/6/5%, margin 33%, discount 9.0% | $212 | -38% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario base | 29x FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $284 | -18% | S7, S97 |
| DCF bull | growth 14/11/9/7/6%, margin 35%, discount 8.5% | $277 | -20% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario bull | 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 | $357 | +3.6% | S7, S97 |
| Probability-weighted | 25/50/25 on the scenario values | $291.5 | -15% | S6, S7 |

Three scenarios bracket the answer, and the price sits at the top of them. The scenario range runs from $241 at 24.6x FY2027E EPS to $357 at 35x $10.20, around a $284 base and a $291.5 probability-weighted value 15% below the price; the DCF range of $133-$277 sits mostly beneath it, and the sum of the parts is $177-238. At $344.63 the buyer pays 121% of the scenario base and 97% of the scenario bull, so the bull returns 3.6% before the dividend while the base costs 18% and the bear 30%. A margin of safety has to come from entry: $270 is 27.6x FY2027E $9.79, 95% of the scenario base and 12% above the scenario bear, and it is where the three-year return spans 5.0-13.3% across 27-34x exits. The $20bn Google search payment survives as a renegotiation rather than a ban, but it is on appeal. The dated catalysts are the 2026-11-02 fourth-quarter release, the May 2027 buyback authorisation and the D.C. Circuit's search-remedy decision expected in 2027. The conclusion is a price range, not a point: own Apple below the high-$200s, or on evidence that FY2027 EPS is tracking above $10.20; at $344.63 the market has paid for the bull. The sell-side targets I can see — $338-355 across four retail aggregators, TickFlow $339.35 from 50 analysts and vcpscanner $340.88 from 112 — are unverified and cluster at the price rather than at intrinsic value [S5, S7, S70, S97, S101, S142, S144, S157, S158].

The counter-case deserves its weight. The discount rate is a judgement: at the low end of the range the base DCF reaches the market price, and quality franchises have held premium multiples for years. What I will not concede is a margin of safety: on every operating assumption I can defend, the buyer's return is set by the exit multiple, already at the top of its own historical range. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the gap to intrinsic value.

plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's advantage is profit capture in hardware; its distribution rent is the exposed flank.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's earnings are cash-true and its returns real; what an investor pays $344.63 for is 39.5x a margin that a memory cycle and two legal remedies can move, on FY2027 earnings that require a gross margin above any year before 2026. Trailing free cash flow was $136,683M against net income of $128,930M — 1.06x, or 0.97x on a normalised $125,084M, on capex of 2.2% of revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft and 33.9% at Alphabet. Revenue rose from $383,285M in FY2023 to $466,823M trailing with operating margin up from 29.8% to 33.2%, and the nine months to 27 June 2026 earned a 43.0% incremental operating margin: $21,809M more operating income on $50,662M more revenue. That 43% is an up-cycle marginal rate. [S5, S6]

| $M unless stated | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M FY2026 | TTM | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 383,285 | 391,035 | 416,161 | 364,357 | 466,823 | S5, S6 |
| Gross profit | 169,148 | 180,683 | 195,201 | 178,782 | 227,123 | S5, S6 |
| Operating income | 114,301 | 123,216 | 133,050 | 122,432 | 154,859 | S5, S6 |
| Net income | 96,995 | 93,736 | 112,010 | 101,464 | 128,930 | S5, S6 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 6.13 | 6.08 | 7.46 | 6.88 | 8.72 | S5, S6 |
| Diluted shares (M) | 15,813 | 15,408 | 15,005 | 14,750 | — | S5, S6 |
| Operating cash flow | 110,543 | 118,254 | 111,482 | 116,996 | 146,724 | S5, S6 |
| Capital expenditure | 10,959 | 9,447 | 12,715 | 6,799 | 10,041 | S5, S6 |
| Free cash flow | 99,584 | 108,807 | 98,767 | 110,197 | 136,683 | S5, S6 |

### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

Gross margin went from 44.1% in FY2023 to 46.9% in FY2025, 49.1% in the nine months of FY2026 and 48.7% trailing; the June 2026 quarter printed 50.1%, a record. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9%, and the 30 July 2026 release attributes 2 points of the quarter's gross margin and $0.11 of its $2.02 EPS to tariff refunds. Against that, memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 and memory is now 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials against 10% a year earlier, and the 10-Q expects the component trends "to intensify". A 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1%, is the level to capitalise. [S17, S68, S99]

::: info warning
**Two percentage points of the record 50.1% gross margin are a one-off tariff refund, and memory is turning against the hardware line (S6, S17).**

The refund is 2 points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 quarterly EPS (S17); memory rose 146% and the 10-Q warns cost pressure will intensify (S6, S68). Two hundred basis points off trailing gross margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of $8.72.
:::

### Cash conversion is real, but a liability accrual did the lifting

Nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,242M to $116,996M against a $16,920M rise in net income, and the dominant line is other current and non-current liabilities: +$10,016M against −$15,161M a year earlier, when the Irish State Aid settlement sat in it. Its clean three-year average is $2,502M ($3,031M; −$248M; $4,724M), so the $14,101M it puts into trailing free cash flow is the soft spot. Replacing it with that average gives $125,084M, 0.97x net income; zeroing it gives $122,582M and its best clean year $127,306M, so the band is $122.6-127.3B and $125.1B the midpoint. The $13,270M of gross intangibles added against investing "other" of $1,780M suggests the $13,531M non-current build is deferred consideration, putting the figure at $123,152M. [S5, S6]

### The balance sheet is not the risk; the asking price is

At 27 June 2026 cash and marketable securities were $146,517M against debt of $84,344M — net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M nine months earlier while $62,094M of stock was retired. FY2025 notes carried $91.3B of principal with $12.4B due within twelve months; leases add $16.8B and purchase obligations $86.3B. Two items need a question: $2,604M of unrealised securities losses, and intangibles up to $25,417M net from $13,301M without the 10-Q saying what was bought. [S5, S6]

| Returns and working capital | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | TTM | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on equity | 171.9% | 157.4% | 171.4% | 148.8% | S5, S6 |
| Return on assets | 27.5% | 26.1% | 30.9% | 36.1% | S5, S6 |
| ROIC (equity + debt − cash; distorted) | 1,527% | 1,036% | 479% | 321% | S5, S6 |
| Net cash | 51,011 | 50,021 | 33,763 | 62,173 | S5, S6 |
| Days sales outstanding | 28.1 | 31.2 | 34.9 | 24.5 | S5, S6 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | −67.8 | −75.8 | −71.1 | −56.8 | S5, S6 |
| Effective tax rate | 14.7% | 24.1% | 15.6% | 17.3% | S5, S6 |

ROE of 148.8% and ROA of 36.1% are genuine; the 320.6% ROIC is an artefact of cash and negative working capital shrinking invested capital to $45,347M. The measure that survives is cash return on book capital: normalised free cash flow of $125.1B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, 65.2% against 57.3% in FY2025. With the ten-year Treasury at 4.93%, a 9-11% cost of equity is cleared several times; the constraint is the price. Nine-month buybacks and dividends of $73,872M are 72.4% of normalised free cash flow and net cash still rose. [S6, S7, S10]

### What $9.79 requires

The $284 base case, the $270 entry and the $440 sale trigger all divide by one number: $9.79 of FY2027 EPS, which is $344.63 divided by the 35.21x forward multiple quoted on 2026-10-30, not a figure Apple publishes. [S97]

| FY2027 build to $9.79 | Value | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $520.8bn | iPhone consensus $277.4bn + $243.4bn of services and other hardware; +9.2% on FY2026E $477.1bn | S71, S72 |
| Gross margin | 48.0% | $250.0bn gross profit | S6 |
| Operating expense | $80.0bn | nine months $56.4bn, held to 6.5% growth after 21.9% | S6 |
| Operating income | $170.1bn | 32.7% margin | derived |
| Other income; tax at 17.3% | $1.0bn; $29.6bn | trailing rates | S6 |
| Net income; diluted shares | $141.5bn; 14,450M | 14,715M less 1.8% buyback | S6 |
| EPS | $9.79 | $141.5bn ÷ 14,450M | S97 |

The gross margin carries the bridge: 48.0% is above FY2025's 46.9% and above the 47-48% band the record quarter supports once the refund is stripped, while iPhone revenue grows 9.9% against 8.3% for everything else and products earn 39.9% against services' 76.3%. Each 100 basis points is $0.30 of FY2027 EPS — $9.19 at 46.0%, $10.08 at 49.0% — so the earnings base is a band of $9.19-10.08, not a point.

### The downside is larger than the up-cycle margin implies

The 30% revenue-fall stress cannot be run at 43%. That rate says $1 of lost revenue costs $0.43 of operating income, but Apple's cost base does not fall with revenue: R&D rose 14.0% in FY2023 while revenue fell 2.8%. On through-cycle margins — revenue 30% lower at $364.6bn, gross margin at the FY2023 trough of 44.1%, operating expense held at $80.0bn — operating income falls to $80.8bn from $170.1bn, a 57% decremental margin, and EPS to $4.68, 52% below what the price implies. At 43% the same stress returns $5.95, overstating stress EPS by 27%; at a 42.0% gross margin EPS is $4.24. At the 24.6x multiple Apple carried out of FY2022 that is $104-115, which is why the $133 cash-flow bear is the permanent-loss anchor rather than a trading drawdown. A 30% fall needs a memory and remedy convergence no filed evidence supports: tail, priced. [S2, S3, S5, S6]

### One share count, one multiple

The 10-Q states 14,608,963 thousand shares outstanding at 27 June 2026, so market value at $344.63 is $5,034bn. The $5,029.6bn used in the valuation and exit work implies 14,594M shares, 15M fewer or 0.1%; the $5,072bn used for the business model is the 14,715M diluted quarterly average, 106M shares and 0.8% more. The multiple is 39.5x either way — price divided by the $8.72 diluted EPS — against 39.0x on trailing net income over the outstanding count; the difference is 0.2 turns. [S6, S7, S97]

The ladder is a single-point bet because $270 is 27.6x $9.79: on the low end of the band the same $270 is 29.4x, on the high end 26.8x. Priced in multiples, the entry is $254-278 (27.6x $9.19 to $10.08), fair value $267-292 and a sale at 44-48x forward, $414-454. Three tranches at $278, $266 and $254 hold the multiple inside 27-28x whatever FY2027 delivers, and a 6% lower earnings path turns the 9.9% three-year return at $270 into 7.6%.

### What the next print has to clear

Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026, guided to 9-11% growth ($111.7-113.7B off $102,466M); consensus puts iPhone revenue at $252.4bn for FY2026 and $277.4bn for FY2027. After a 17.3% tax rate, 200 basis points of gross margin is $0.52 of trailing EPS (6.0%), 500 points $1.31 (15.0%), losing the $20B search payment $1.12 (12.9%) and a 10% fall in iPhone revenue $0.55 (6.3%). Gross margin moves the outcome most because it applies to all $466,823M of revenue. Earnings quality is not the constraint; the price is. Diligence: December-quarter gross-margin guidance, FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices, and what sits in the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities. [S71, S72]

arguments.markdown:
Apple closed at $344.63 on 30 October 2026, a $5,072bn market capitalisation and a 27.5% total return over twelve months; the last reported period is the June quarter, with Q4 FY2026 results due on 2 November 2026, so the price contains no post-results adjustment. The market it trades in is near its high: the S&P 500 at 7,580.07 is up 10.7% year to date and 3.4% below its record, the Nasdaq is 8.2% below its high, the VIX is 19.42 at the 77th percentile, and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.93%. Technology is the laggard, down 8.3% over one month while the SPY fell 0.9% — a regime that penalises long-duration multiples [S7, S97, S8, S9, S10].

The business is not the problem. Apple converts profit into cash at 0.97 times net income, 0.95 times at the low end of the normalised band, on capex of 2.2% of revenue; it holds $62,173M of net cash and earns 40.3% of gross profit from services on 25.8% of revenue; a 30% revenue fall still leaves the company solvent and stops the buyback rather than breaking the balance sheet. What has changed is the margin: the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin carried two points of tariff refunds, memory costs have turned, and the base case underwrites 47-48% [S6, S17].

The price is the problem. At 39.3 times trailing and 35.2 times forward earnings against 18.09 times for the S&P 500, the shares discount a 7.0% cost of equity or 6.4-6.9% perpetual growth; the DCF at 9.0% is $212, its 8.5% discount-rate bull is $277 (20% below the close), the sum of the parts is $177-238, and the base scenario is $284, 18% below the close. The recommendation rests on the base case and on the 25/50/25 probability-weighted value of $291.5, 15% below the price — not on either bull. The scenario bull is $357 at 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20, a 25% branch with a +4% return. The market is capitalising a peak margin and a peak multiple at the same time [S7, S97, S146].

Two facts would change the call. A gross margin at the low end of the range takes fair value to the first entry tranche, so the tranche becomes the base case rather than a discount to it; an appellate ban on the search payment moves the bear toward the discounted-cash-flow floor. The one question below decides which of the two the next twelve months delivers.

The view is non-consensus on price, not on franchise. The sell side's median target sits at the spot price, so the Street sees fair value where this analysis sees an overvaluation; the difference is the normalised margin and the exit multiple, not the quality of the installed base.

Positioning follows from that: zero today, a conditional staged entry below the base case, and a sell discipline tied to the multiple and to services growth. The first tranche at $270 requires the 2026-11-02 guide to hold FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and gross margin at 47%; if it fails, the first tranche moves to $235 and the second to $210. The first hard test is the FY2026 10-K and the December-quarter guide on 2 November 2026, two days after this version. The follow-up diligence is threefold: the working-capital and intangibles note in that filing, a primary consensus feed for FY2027 EPS, and the D.C. Circuit briefing and decision [S6, S7].

arguments.markdown:
Apple's earnings are cash-true and its returns real; what an investor pays $344.63 for is 39.5x a margin that a memory cycle and two legal remedies can move, on FY2027 earnings that require a gross margin above any year before 2026. Trailing free cash flow was $136,683M against net income of $128,930M — 1.06x, or 0.97x on a normalised $125,084M, on capex of 2.2% of revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft and 33.9% at Alphabet. Revenue rose from $383,285M in FY2023 to $466,823M trailing with operating margin up from 29.8% to 33.2%, and the nine months to 27 June 2026 earned a 43.0% incremental operating margin: $21,809M more operating income on $50,662M more revenue. That 43% is an up-cycle rate. [S5, S6]

### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

Gross margin went from 44.1% in FY2023 to 46.9% in FY2025, 49.1% in the nine months of FY2026 and 48.7% trailing; the June 2026 quarter printed 50.1%, a record. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9%, and the 30 July 2026 release attributes 2 points of the quarter's gross margin and $0.11 of its $2.02 EPS to tariff refunds. Against that, memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 and memory is now 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials against 10% a year earlier, and the 10-Q expects the component trends "to intensify". A 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1%, is the level to capitalise. [S17, S68, S99]

::: info warning
**Two percentage points of the record 50.1% gross margin are a one-off tariff refund, and memory is turning against the hardware line (S6, S17).**

The refund is 2 points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 quarterly EPS (S17); memory rose 146% and the 10-Q warns cost pressure will intensify (S6, S68). Two hundred basis points off trailing gross margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of $8.72.
:::

### Cash conversion is real, but a liability accrual did the lifting

Nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,242M to $116,996M against a $16,920M rise in net income, and the dominant line is other current and non-current liabilities: +$10,016M against −$15,161M a year earlier, when the Irish State Aid settlement sat in it. Its clean three-year average is $2,502M ($3,031M; −$248M; $4,724M), so the $14,101M it puts into trailing free cash flow is the soft spot. Replacing it with that average gives $125,084M, 0.97x net income; zeroing it gives $122,582M and its best clean year $127,306M, so the band is $122.6-127.3B and $125.1B the midpoint. The $13,270M of gross intangibles added against investing "other" of $1,780M suggests the $13,531M non-current build is deferred consideration, putting the figure at $123,152M. [S5, S6]

### The balance sheet is not the risk; the asking price is

At 27 June 2026 cash and marketable securities were $146,517M against debt of $84,344M — net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M nine months earlier while $62,094M of stock was retired. FY2025 notes carried $91.3B of principal with $12.4B due within twelve months; leases add $16.8B and purchase obligations $86.3B. Two items need scrutiny: $2,604M of unrealised securities losses, and intangibles up to $25,417M net from $13,301M without the 10-Q saying what was bought. [S5, S6]

ROE of 148.8% and ROA of 36.1% are genuine; the 320.6% ROIC is an artefact of cash and negative working capital shrinking invested capital to $45,347M. The measure that survives is cash return on book capital: normalised free cash flow of $125.1B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, 65.2% against 57.3% in FY2025. With the ten-year Treasury at 4.93%, a 9-11% cost of equity is cleared several times; the constraint is the price. Nine-month buybacks and dividends of $73,872M are 72.4% of normalised free cash flow. [S6, S7, S10]

### What $9.79 requires

The $284 base case, the $270 entry and the $440 sale trigger all divide by one number: $9.79 of FY2027 EPS, which is $344.63 divided by the 35.21x forward multiple quoted on 2026-10-30, not a figure Apple publishes. [S97]

| FY2027 build to $9.79 | Value | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $520.8bn | iPhone consensus $277.4bn + $243.4bn of services and other hardware; +9.2% on FY2026E $477.1bn | S71, S72 |
| Gross margin | 48.0% | $250.0bn gross profit | S6 |
| Operating expense | $80.0bn | nine months $56.4bn, held to 6.5% growth after 21.9% | S6 |
| Operating income | $170.1bn | 32.7% margin | derived |
| Other income; tax at 17.3% | $1.0bn; $29.6bn | trailing rates | S6 |
| Net income; diluted shares | $141.5bn; 14,450M | 14,715M less 1.8% buyback | S6 |
| EPS | $9.79 | $141.5bn ÷ 14,450M | S97 |

The gross margin carries the bridge: 48.0% is above FY2025's 46.9% and above the 47-48% band the record quarter supports once the refund is stripped, while iPhone revenue grows 9.9% against 8.3% for everything else and products earn 39.9% against services' 76.3%. Each 100 basis points is $0.30 of FY2027 EPS — $9.19 at 46.0%, $10.08 at 49.0% — so the earnings base is a band of $9.19-10.08, not a point.

### The downside is larger than the up-cycle margin implies

The 30% revenue-fall stress cannot be run at 43%. That rate says $1 of lost revenue costs $0.43 of operating income, but Apple's cost base does not fall with revenue: R&D rose 14.0% in FY2023 while revenue fell 2.8%. On through-cycle margins — revenue 30% lower at $364.6bn, gross margin at the FY2023 trough of 44.1%, operating expense held at $80.0bn — operating income falls to $80.8bn from $170.1bn, a 57% decremental margin, and EPS to $4.68, 52% below what the price implies. At 43% the same stress returns $5.95, overstating stress EPS by 27%; at a 42.0% gross margin EPS is $4.24. At the 24.6x multiple Apple carried out of FY2022 that is $104-115, which is why the $133 cash-flow bear is the permanent-loss anchor rather than a trading drawdown. A 30% fall needs a memory and remedy convergence no filed evidence supports: tail, priced. [S2, S3, S5, S6]

### One share count, one multiple

The 10-Q states 14,608,963 thousand shares outstanding at 27 June 2026, so market value at $344.63 is $5,034bn. The $5,029.6bn used in the valuation and exit work implies 14,594M shares, 15M fewer or 0.1%; the $5,072bn used for the business model is the 14,715M diluted quarterly average, 106M shares and 0.8% more. The multiple is 39.5x either way — price divided by the $8.72 diluted EPS — against 39.0x on trailing net income over the outstanding count; the difference is 0.2 turns. [S6, S7, S97]

The ladder is a single-point bet because $270 is 27.6x $9.79: on the low end of the band the same $270 is 29.4x, on the high end 26.8x. Priced in multiples, the entry is $254-278 (27.6x $9.19 to $10.08), fair value $267-292 and a sale at 44-48x forward, $414-454. Three tranches at $278, $266 and $254 hold the multiple inside 27-28x whatever FY2027 delivers, and a 6% lower earnings path turns the 9.9% three-year return at $270 into 7.6%.

### What the next print has to clear

Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026, guided to 9-11% growth ($111.7-113.7B off $102,466M); consensus puts iPhone revenue at $252.4bn for FY2026 and $277.4bn for FY2027. After a 17.3% tax rate, 200 basis points of gross margin is $0.52 of trailing EPS (6.0%), 500 points $1.31 (15.0%), losing the $20B search payment $1.12 (12.9%) and a 10% fall in iPhone revenue $0.55 (6.3%). Gross margin moves the outcome most because it applies to all $466,823M of revenue. Earnings quality is not the constraint; the price is. Diligence: December-quarter gross-margin guidance, FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices, and what sits in the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities. [S71, S72]

arguments.markdown:
Apple's only exit is the public market and its own buyback, and at $344.63 the shares already discount the scenario bull. No peer is large enough to acquire it — Microsoft at $3,875.8bn, Alphabet at $3,461.1bn, Amazon at $2,598.9bn and Meta at $1,582.4bn are all smaller than Apple's $5,071.2bn market value (14,715m diluted shares at $344.63) — so a holder's realisation depends entirely on the multiple another investor will pay. With dividend and gross buyback yielding 1.9% and earnings per share compounding at 8-9%, the arithmetic is adequate only while the 39.3x multiple holds; if it reverts toward the four-year average of 31.0x, the three-year return from $344.63 falls to 1.3% a year. That sets the sell discipline: buy below $270, where the three-year return spans 5.0-13.3% around 9.9%, and treat $380 and above as a sale [S7, S11, S6].

| Metric | Value | Implication | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Average daily volume | 40.41m shares and $13.84bn (20-day); 41.34m and $13.56bn (3-month) | A $250m position is 1.8% of one day's value traded; $1bn is 7.2% | S7 |
| Shares outstanding | 14,715m diluted at 2026-06-27; the proxy's 14,697.9m basic at 2026-01-02 is 0.1% lower | Free float effectively 100%; one count for the market cap | S6, S11 |
| Largest holders | Vanguard 9.63%; BlackRock 7.10% | Index managers, no controlling or strategic holder | S11 |
| Directors and officers | 9,079,765 shares, 0.06% | Aligned, but immaterial to the register | S11 |
| Index role | Largest in the peer set; the weight itself is not publicly disclosed in the sources here | A structural passive bid, and correlated selling in redemptions | S7 |

Liquidity is the one exit risk that can be dismissed. As the table shows, Apple's daily turnover dwarfs any position a long-only fund would take, so the exit is never closed and market impact is measured in basis points. The intended holding period is three years, the horizon over which the reversion arithmetic is computed; what cannot be dismissed is price, because the buyers on the other side are the same index and active funds the seller competes with, and in a broad de-rating they mark the same multiple down together.

| Component | Rate | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Dividend yield | 0.31% ($1.08 annualised on $344.63) | S17, S7 |
| Buyback yield, gross | 1.62% ($82.2bn repurchased on a $5,071.2bn market value) | S6, S7 |
| Buyback yield, net of $13.7bn stock compensation | 1.35% | S6, S7 |
| Total shareholder yield | 1.93% | S6, S7 |
| EPS growth, FY2021 to TTM / FY2027E to FY2029E | 9.2% / 8.2% | S1, S6 |
| Of the historic growth, from a falling share count | 2.9 points a year | S1, S6 |
| Three-year return, multiple unchanged at 39.3x | 9.6% a year | S7, S97 |
| Three-year return, multiple reverts to 31.0x | 1.3% a year | S7, S97 |

Two things follow. First, the operating return is real but modest: a 1.9% yield plus 8% earnings growth is a high-single-digit compounding machine, not the 27.5% twelve-month return the shares have just delivered. Second, the buyback does much of the work in that growth, and at 39.3x it buys a 2.5% earnings yield per dollar spent, below the 4.93% ten-year Treasury, so the repurchase supports the share price without creating value at this level. That is not a scandal; it is what a mature cash machine should do with cash it cannot reinvest at its own cost of capital. But an investor paying 39.3x is paying for the cash return, not receiving a bargain from it [S6, S1].

The multiple, not the business, is the swing factor. Apple traded at 24.6x at the end of FY2022, 27.9x in FY2023, 37.5x in FY2024 and 34.2x in FY2025; it now trades at 39.3x trailing and 35.2x forward, against a twelve-month average of 35.7x. A reversion to the four-year mean of 31.0x costs 21.1% of the price, or 7.6% a year over three years, which swallows the entire shareholder yield and most of the earnings growth. That is how a higher-rate regime reaches a long-duration equity: with the ten-year Treasury at 4.93%, up 84 basis points in a year, the discount applied to cash flows arriving after 2035 is materially higher than it was when the shares traded at 27.9x [S7, S97, S10].

| Route | Named buyer or venue | Rationale | Timing | Likelihood | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open-market sale | NasdaqGS continuous auction | $13.8bn a day; exit complete in days | Any trading day | Near-certain, and the default route | S7 |
| Issuer repurchase | Apple Inc., under its board authorisation | $82.2bn in the twelve months to June 2026; $100bn authorised in May 2025 | Continuous; next authorisation with the May 2027 results | High | S6, S5 |
| Dividend | Apple Inc. | $0.27 a quarter, raised annually | Quarterly, with an annual increase each May | High | S17 |
| Strategic acquisition | No buyer large enough: the four largest peers are all smaller than Apple | Antitrust review in the US, EU, China and UK would follow any bid; a foreign buyer would also face CFIUS national-security review | Not foreseeable | Negligible | S14, S16, S108, S110 |
| Break-up or activist | None identified | Sum of the parts is $177-238 a share against a $5,071.2bn market value | No campaign disclosed | Negligible | S6, S17 |
| Passive flows | S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 index funds | Largest company in the peer set | Quarterly rebalancing | Structural, not a decision | S11 |

No listing or lock-up constraint applies: the shares already trade on NasdaqGS, and the only lock-up-like restriction on the issuer is the buyback blackout around results. The route that matters is therefore the open market, and the price at which it clears is the only variable the holder controls.

| Precedent realisation | Year | Value | Multiple at the time | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Repurchases, FY2022 | 2022 | $89.4bn | 24.6x year-end P/E | S2, S7 |
| Repurchases, FY2023 | 2023 | $77.6bn | 27.9x | S3, S7 |
| Repurchases, FY2024 | 2024 | $94.9bn | 37.5x | S4, S7 |
| Repurchases, FY2025 | 2025 | $90.7bn | 34.2x | S5, S7 |
| Observed drawdown, twelve months to 2026-10-30 | 2026 | $243.42 low | 29.4% below $344.63 | S7 |

The precedents are all capital returns, because that is the only exit a company of this size has ever offered its holders. They also show the cost of buying back stock at the top: the FY2024 and FY2025 programmes together spent $185.6bn at 34-38x earnings, and those shares would have been retired 18-26% cheaper at the FY2023 multiple. An investor buying today at 39.3x makes the same choice management made, at a higher price [S4, S5].

| Entry price | Exit at 27x | Exit at 31x | Exit at 34x | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $344.63 (2026-10-30) | -3.2% | 1.3% | 4.5% | S6, S7, S97 |
| $300 | 1.4% | 6.1% | 9.4% | S6, S7, S97 |
| $270 | 5.0% | 9.9% | 13.3% | S6, S7, S97 |
| $240 | 9.2% | 14.3% | 17.9% | S6, S7, S97 |

The sell discipline follows from that table, which assumes FY2029E EPS of $11.45, $3.55 of dividends and exit multiples of 27x to 34x. It also follows from the scenario range: at $344.63 the shares are 97% of the $357 scenario bull at 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 and 121% of the $284 scenario base at 29x, while the DCF bull at an 8.5% discount rate is $277, 20% below the market. A long-only fund earns its 9% hurdle from $270, not from $344; the shares are a hold only for a holder who owns them at a lower basis, and a buy only on a de-rating or on evidence that FY2027-28 earnings growth is running above 12% rather than the 9.9% consensus assumes for iPhone revenue. The conditions that would make me raise the entry price are specific and observable: services growing above 10% with the Google payment intact, gross margin held above 48% through the memory cycle, and a buyback authorisation above $100bn. The conditions that force a sale are equally specific: services growth below 8% for two quarters, gross margin below 46%, normalised free cash flow conversion below 0.9x net income, a buyback cut, or any remedy that removes the Google payment. A multiple above 45x forward, $440, would be a sale on valuation alone [S71, S72, S7].

The bear case sets the drawdown to expect, not just the return. Two independent methods converge on $241-243: a reversion to Apple's 2022 multiple of 24.6x on FY2027E earnings gives $241, and the $243.42 low the shares actually printed within the past twelve months is $243. That is a 30% drawdown, and it is the realistic bad case for a fund holding the shares. The DCF bear of $133 is a different animal — gross margin compression, 2-4% growth and a 9.5% discount rate together — and should be read as the permanent-loss scenario rather than the trading risk. The buyback limits both: the same $82-85bn a year retires 2.1% of the shares at $270 and 2.3% at $240, against 1.6% at today's price, so each leg down raises the forward earnings growth the buyer receives [S7, S6].

The strongest argument against this discipline is that it has been wrong before. Apple has compounded strongly while the technology sector fell in the last month, and a fund that sold on valuation last year would have forgone most of that gain; multiples of this quality have held through a high long-bond yield that most models said would compress them. That is a reason to size modestly and buy on weakness rather than to abandon the arithmetic: the exit route is liquid, the cash return is real and growing, and the only thing between today's price and the fund's required return is the multiple paid on entry. Confidence is high on the liquidity and the cash-return mechanics, medium on the multiple reversion, which is a forecast rather than an observation. The open diligence question is how much of services revenue the Google payment represents and when the appeal is decided, because neither figure is publicly disclosed in the sources here and both set the floor under the services multiple.

Base ($284, 50%): growth fades from 9% to 5%, margin normalises to 47-48%, services grows 12-14% and the search payment is renegotiated lower — 29 times $9.79, an 18% decline, with intrinsic value of $212-264. Bear ($241, 25%): memory breaks the hardware margin below 46%, services growth falls under 8% as the DMA and link-out remedies bite, and the payment is cut or banned — 24.6 times $9.79, a 30% drawdown, with the $133 DCF bear as the permanent-loss tail [S6, S7].

Three analogs set the decision rule. Microsoft's 1998 antitrust case ended in 2001 without a break-up: the asset survived, but the overhang ran three years and the settlement did not re-rate the stock — the cloud did, a decade later. Nokia held 49.4% of handset share in 2007, peaked near $250bn and sold its handset business for $7.2bn in 2013: a platform leader that loses the next interface loses developers first and volume second. Cisco took until December 2025 to exceed its March 2000 record, 25 years in which the company compounded and the share price did not [S143, S145, S147]. The rule they teach is that at a peak multiple the entry price, not the business, sets the return. Apple is cheaper than Cisco at its peak (39.3 times against 201), owns silicon and a services annuity Nokia never had, and holds $62.2bn of net cash; the analogy is about duration and multiple, not extinction.

The decision follows: watchlist today, zero position, with a staged entry set by price, not narrative. The first tranche of 0.75-1.0% of the fund is $270 only on a condition: the 2026-11-02 guide must hold FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and gross margin at 47%. At 27.6 times, $270 is a discount only on the $9.79 base EPS; on $9.27 it is 29.1 times, and on $8.07-8.53, after a 12.9% search-payment cut, 31.7-33.5 times, above the 31.0 times four-year mean. At 27.6 times those lower cases imply $223-235, so if the guide fails the first tranche moves to $235 and the second to $210. The position reaches its 5% cap below $225 or on evidence that FY2027 EPS growth is tracking above 12%. The red-team objection stands: $270 is a 5% discount to the $284 base case and sits above the $242 realistic bear, so it is a first price, not a margin of safety, and the ladder now prices the EPS bridge rather than a single point at $9.79. The counter-evidence is the stock's own record: 27.5% in the twelve months to 30 October 2026; a sale at 35 times forward would have missed it. The open diligence is the appellate outcome on the search payment and a primary consensus feed for FY2027 EPS, neither of which the register holds. Sell above $380 or above 45 times forward earnings ($440), or if two consecutive quarters show services growth below 10%, gross margin below 47%, or a services structure that removes the search payment [S6, S7].

arguments.markdown:
Apple's earnings are cash-true and its returns real; what an investor pays $344.63 for is 39.5x a margin that a memory cycle and two legal remedies can move, on FY2027 earnings that require a gross margin above any year before 2026. Trailing free cash flow was $136,683M against net income of $128,930M — 1.06x, or 0.97x on a normalised $125,084M, on capex of 2.2% of revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft and 33.9% at Alphabet. Revenue rose from $383,285M in FY2023 to $466,823M trailing with operating margin up from 29.8% to 33.2%, and the nine months to 27 June 2026 earned a 43.0% incremental operating margin: $21,809M more operating income on $50,662M more revenue. That 43% is an up-cycle rate. [S5, S6]
