{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 4 by Lead Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,989 characters)
Apple is a genuine compounder priced as a perpetual one. The installed base and services annuity are real, and FY2026 is strong: revenue rose 16.4% in the June quarter, iPhone revenue 22.4% in the nine months to 27 June 2026, and services earned 40.3% of gross profit on 25.8% of revenue. What is in dispute is the price: at $344.63 on 30 October 2026 the shares carry a $5,072bn market capitalisation, 39.3 times trailing and 35.2 times forward earnings, against an S&P 500 at 18.7 times forward. The decision is not whether Apple is a good business — it is — but whether a long-only fund should own it at a multiple that assumes the next five years go right [S6, S7, S97, S156].

Three valuation methods agree and none reaches the price. A discounted cash flow at a 9.0% cost of equity, built on the 4.93% ten-year Treasury, gives $212 a share; the DCF bull case at an 8.5% discount rate and a 35% operating margin gives $277; the sum of the parts is $177-238; the stock's own four-year average multiple of 31.0 times implies $303 [S6, S10, S97]. To justify $344.63 an investor needs a 7.0% discount rate or 6.4-6.9% perpetual growth in net operating profit after tax. Those assumptions make the price exactly fair rather than cheap; the base rate is modest, with revenue compounding 3.3% a year from FY2021 to FY2025.

The sell side sees fair value; this report sees 18% overvaluation: retail aggregator targets are $338-355, unverified, flat to +3% from the close [S142, S144]. Consensus expects iPhone revenue of $252.4bn in FY2026 and $277.4bn in FY2027 and capitalises the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin. The disagreement is specific: that margin included two points of tariff refunds, memory costs have turned (the iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials is up 38%, memory 34% of it), and our base case underwrites 47-48%. A 46% margin, which a full memory pass-through implies, takes FY2027 EPS to $9.3 and fair value to $270 at 29 times — the entry price below, not a discount to it. The non-consensus view is that the market is capitalising a peak margin and multiple at once.

Three scenarios weighted 25/50/25 put the probability-weighted value at $291.5, 15% below the price, and the recommendation rests on that weighted value and the $284 base case, not on the bull. The scenario bull ($357, 25%) — distinct from the $277 DCF bull above — assumes the AI and foldable cycle extends iPhone growth into FY2027-28, services grows above 15%, gross margin holds 48% and the search payment survives at a lower rate: 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20 for a 4% price return. Base ($284, 50%): growth fades from 9% to 5%, margin normalises to 47-48%, services grows 12-14% and the search payment is renegotiated lower — 29 times $9.79, an 18% decline, with intrinsic value of $212-264. Bear ($241, 25%): memory breaks the hardware margin below 46%, services growth falls under 8% as the DMA and link-out remedies bite, and the payment is cut or banned — 24.6 times $9.79, a 30% drawdown, with the $133 DCF bear as the permanent-loss tail [S6, S7].

Three analogs set the decision rule. Microsoft's 1998 antitrust case ended in 2001 without a break-up: the asset survived, but the overhang ran three years and the settlement did not re-rate the stock — the cloud did, a decade later. Nokia held 49.4% of handset share in 2007, peaked near $250bn and sold its handset business for $7.2bn in 2013: a platform leader that loses the next interface loses developers first and volume second. Cisco took until December 2025 to exceed its March 2000 record, 25 years in which the company compounded and the share price did not [S143, S145, S147]. The rule they teach is that at a peak multiple the entry price, not the business, sets the return. Apple is cheaper than Cisco at its peak (39.3x against 201), owns silicon and a services annuity Nokia never had, and holds $62.2bn of net cash; the analogy is about duration and multiple, not extinction.

The decision follows: watchlist today, zero position, with a staged entry set by price, not narrative. The first tranche of 0.75-1.0% of the fund is $270 only on a condition: the 2026-11-02 guide must hold FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and gross margin at 47%. At 27.6 times, $270 is a discount only on the $9.79 base EPS; on $9.27 it is 29.1 times, and on $8.07-8.53, after a 12.9% search-payment cut, 31.7-33.5 times, above the 31.0 times four-year mean. At 27.6 times those lower cases imply $223-235, so if the guide fails the first tranche moves to $235 and the second to $210. The position reaches its 5% cap below $225 or on evidence that FY2027 EPS growth is tracking above 12%. The red-team objection stands: $270 is a 5% discount to the $284 base case and sits above the $242 realistic bear, so it is a first price, not a margin of safety, and the ladder now prices the EPS bridge rather than a single point at $9.79. The counter-evidence is the stock's own record: 27.5% in the twelve months to 30 October 2026; a sale at 35 times forward would have missed it. The open diligence is the appellate outcome on the search payment and a primary consensus feed for FY2027 EPS, neither of which the register holds. Sell above 45 times forward earnings ($440), or if two consecutive quarters show services growth below 10%, gross margin below 47%, or a services structure that removes the search payment [S6, S7].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Comprehensive Scoring & Recommendation (scoring, revision 8 by Lead Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,772 characters)

### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

At 27 June 2026 cash and marketable securities were $146,517M against debt of $84,344M — net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M nine months earlier while $62,094M of stock was retired; FY2025 notes carried $91.3B of principal with $12.4B due within twelve months, leases add $16.8B and purchase obligations $86.3B, and two items need scrutiny in the $2,604M of unrealised securities losses and intangibles up to $25,417M net from $13,301M with no note saying what was bought. Apple is winning the hardware profit pool and losing control of the rent on top of it: it holds a 65% share of premium phone units and 20% of all phone units against Samsung's 19%, at a 40.1% product gross margin, but its App Store commission and assistant layer can now be contested without anyone building a better handset, so the question is who owns app discovery and the AI front door [S94, S92, S120, S17, S69].

China is where the share question splits. Counterpoint's 19.5% and IDC's 17.8% measure sell-through against shipments, and the 1.7-point gap is consistent with channel inventory drawing down after launch; both trackers agree Huawei leads (21.3% and 21.1%), that Apple gained share while the market fell 10% on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's, and that Apple's Greater China revenue grew 30% in 9M FY2026. The vulnerability is pool size, not lost share: Pro prices rose $100 and the standard iPhone 18 waits until spring 2027, so part of the Q3 gain is pull-forward. Huawei is the most dangerous rival to the hardware pool: the only one taking premium share in a large market while funding its own silicon, OS and supply chain, with CNY192.3B of R&D [S139, S140, S96, S87, S86].

The distribution pool is where the newest competition is. Epic won a Ninth Circuit ruling on 2025-12-11 that the 27% commission Apple charged on link-outs had a prohibitive effect, collapsing the gap between in-app purchase and external payment. Apple's EU answer from 1 October 2026 is a 26% commission on in-app purchases, 15% on link-outs and a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web. The rent at stake is Apple's highest-margin line: services earned $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026 at a 76.3% gross margin. No alternative storefront discloses meaningful EU share, so the near-term effect is a price war over 5-15 points of take rate, not a shift of volume [S69, S79, S77, S102, S78, S6].

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Epic Games and DMA storefronts | App Store commission | Services $120.5B TTM, 76.3% margin | Take rate falls from 30% to 5-15%; the 27% link-out fee is unenforceable | S69, S77, S6 |
| OpenAI and assistant apps | Search licensing and app discovery | Google pays Apple about $20B a year for the Safari default | Answers replace queries; the assistant becomes the discovery layer | S70, S80, S153 |
| Microsoft Copilot and Windows on Arm | Mac hardware | Mac $33.7B of FY2025 revenue | Copilot+ PCs at price and feature parity | S152, S5 |
| Open-weight models | Apple Intelligence differentiation | Not separately disclosed | A 2.7% capability gap removes any premium for model quality | S155 |
| WeChat mini-programmes | China App Store commission | Not disclosed | Commerce runs inside the super-app, outside Apple's billing | S154 |

The assistant layer is the threat Apple controls least. ChatGPT reached 900M weekly active users by 2026-02-27, and if users ask an assistant rather than search, the roughly $20B a year Google pays Apple loses its rationale. Microsoft attacks the same layer from the enterprise side with Copilot and Copilot+ PCs, yet the measurable outcome is the opposite of a rout: in Q2 2026 Windows personal computing device shipments fell 6.7% while macOS grew 17.4%. Windows on Arm share is undisclosed, and Microsoft's 10-K describes Windows as competing with alternative platforms without claiming share gains. Open-weight models matter more than either vendor: the AI Index puts DeepSeek-R1 level with the top US model in February 2025 and the US lead at 2.7% by March 2026, so model capability is not a moat Apple can charge for, and Apple has licensed Gemini for its next Siri, converting a differentiator into a cost line [S153, S70, S80, S152, S49, S155, S111].

In China the substitute is not a rival phone but a rival operating system inside the phone. Weixin reached 1,418M combined monthly users at 2025-12-31 and Tencent grew marketing services 19% to RMB145.0B on closed-loop advertising into Mini Programs and Mini Shops; commerce inside WeChat never passes through Apple's store, so the China services pool has a ceiling set by a company Apple does not compete with. Apple's newest hinge patent family is co-assigned with supplier Hangzhou Amphenol Phoenix, so even mechanical exclusivity over Samsung and Chinese entrants is partial [S154, S148, S150].

Apple's wedge is silicon, OS control and an installed base at an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter, which supports 40.1% product gross margins while Samsung's mobile division loses money. That wedge defends the hardware pool, not the distribution pool that regulation is dismantling. The position supports a quality-compounder view with a regulated ceiling on services and an unpriced assistant threat, not a share-gain story; confidence is high on hardware share, medium on China because the trackers use different bases, and medium-low on the assistant threat, where displacement is absent from services growth of 14.1% in nine months [S17, S91, S6].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Market & Industry Analysis (market, revision 7 by Market Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,896 characters)
Apple's markets are large but no longer volume-growth markets: the smartphone unit pool is contracting at the fastest rate on record in 2026 while its dollar value rises, so growth to 2030 must come from holding more than 40% of smartphone value, monetising a record installed base through services, and a foldable and AI-driven cycle, not from market growth. Apple's revenue compounded 3.3% from FY2021 to FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and then accelerated to 16% in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone revenue up 22% [S5, S6].

| Measure | Figure | Period | Method and note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global smartphone units | 1.26B | 2025 | Counterpoint full year, +2% YoY; Omdia 1.25B | S92 |
| Global smartphone units | just over 1.0B | 2026E | IDC, -16.7% YoY, steepest annual fall on record | S84 |
| Global smartphone value | $613B | 2026E | IDC, +6.3% YoY | S84 |
| Global smartphone ASP | $581 | 2026E | IDC, +27.6%; Omdia independently $565 (+21%) | S84, S88 |
| Premium segment (wholesale ASP $600+) | 29% of units | H1 2026 | Counterpoint; 25% in H1 2025, 20% in H1 2022 | S94 |
| Apple iPhone revenue | $209.6B FY2025; $196.5B 9M FY2026 | FY2025 / 9M FY2026 | Apple filings; +22% in 9M FY2026 | S5, S6 |
| Apple implied iPhone revenue per unit | $832 FY2025; $1,101 2026E | FY2025 / 2026E | Calculated: iPhone revenue / iOS units (252M = 20% of 1.26B; 238M = 23.6% of 1.01B) | S5, S6, S92, S84 |
| Apple share of smartphone value | 36% FY2025; 42.7% 2026 | FY2025 / 2026 | Calculated: iPhone revenue / market value | S5, S6, S92, S88 |

Two independent methods agree that the market is growing in dollars while shrinking in units. TAM: IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0B units, down 16.7%, while value rises 6.3% to $613B on a 27.6% ASP increase to $581, against Omdia's independent $565 (+21%). SAM: the premium segment (29% of units at $600 or more) plus the iOS installed base for services, where Apple's 65% premium share sets the addressable pool. SOM: Apple's current capture, $466.8B of trailing-twelve-month revenue to June 2026, of which $245.5B is iPhone and $120.5B services. Bottom-up, 1.0B units at $581 imply $581B, within 5% of IDC's value line. The mechanism is a memory cost shock: NAND and DRAM more than 300% above a year earlier are passed into shelf prices, so the market is being repriced, not expanded [S84, S88, S94, S6].

Apple's revenue sits where the market is concentrating. Premium handsets reached 29% of global unit sales in H1 2026 from 25% a year earlier and 20% in H1 2022, and Apple took 65% of those units with 9% growth. Its all-vendor unit share was 20% in 2025, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026 as Android shipments fall 24.3%. Apple captured 36% of global smartphone value in FY2025, $209.6B of iPhone revenue against a $588B market at 1.26B units and a $467 ASP, and annualising nine-month FY2026 iPhone revenue gives $262B, or 42.7% of IDC's $613B. Value capture, not unit share, is the franchise an investor is buying [S94, S92, S84, S5, S6, S88].

### The 27.6% price rise is cost pass-through, and Apple is pricing above it

The increase is not demand-led. IDC attributes the 27.6% ASP rise to a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM up more than 300% and passed into shelf prices, and TrendForce shows the cost landing on Apple directly: the iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials rose 38% year on year, memory reaching 34% of the BOM in Q3 2026 against one-tenth a year earlier. Apple then raised Pro and Pro Max list prices by $100 and held the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027. What supports willingness to pay is sell-through at those prices: Counterpoint recorded iPhone 18 Pro sales up 23.5% in the first three weeks in China, and Apple's installed base reached an all-time high in the June 2026 quarter. What weakens it: Apple discloses no upgrade rate or unit volumes, so an upgrade-cycle claim rests on third-party panels, and IDC attributes part of China's Q3 strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half increases, with the market possibly down 20% in H2 2026. On IDC's unit base Apple's implied revenue per iPhone rose from $832 in FY2025 to $1,101 annualised in 2026, 32% against the market's 27.6%; on the higher 261M unit estimate for FY2026 the rise is 21%. Apple is pricing above the market average, but the magnitude rests on a unit count it does not publish: the gain is cost recovery plus Pro mix, not proof of an upgrade super-cycle. A consumer-panel upgrade rate would settle it and is not available here [S84, S99, S112, S96, S17, S87, S74].

Three pools can add revenue to 2030, and only one is large enough to change the trajectory. Foldables: Apple enters in H2 2026, and IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at an ASP above $2,550, 40% of a category worth more than $45.7B. Services: $120.5B trailing twelve months to June 2026, up 14.1% in nine months at a 76.3% gross margin, against a $1.34T advertising pool in 2026 and an App Store ecosystem Apple says carried $149B of digital goods and services in 2025. Wearables and PC: a 2.4% CAGR market to 2030 with smartwatches shrinking 3.7% in 2026 while glasses grow 18.1%, and Apple took 18.2% of combined PC and tablet units in Q2 2026. The non-phone pools, $33.7B of Mac and $35.7B of wearables in FY2025, are too small to carry group growth alone [S84, S6, S17, S89, S83, S85, S152, S5].

| Region | Market size (latest dated) | Growth | Company's position | Barriers | Key competitors | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Americas | Not published; global $613B (2026E) | Apple +11.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; home market; 42.9% of FY2025 revenue | US tariffs; platform antitrust | Samsung, Google, Motorola | S84, S5, S6 |
| Europe | Not published | Apple +16.1% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 26.7% of revenue | DMA take-rate cuts from 2026-10-01; GDPR | Samsung, Xiaomi, Google | S77, S6 |
| Greater China | 66M units in Q2 2026 | Market -10% in Q3 2026 (Counterpoint), -15.4% (IDC); Apple +30.0% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 19.5% in Q3 2026 on Counterpoint and 17.8% on IDC, against Huawei's 21.3% and 21.1%; Apple +4.8 points YoY | Market access; local champion; data rules; WeChat as a distribution layer | Huawei, OPPO, vivo, Xiaomi, Honor | S139, S140, S96, S87, S6 |
| Japan | Not published | Apple +10.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 6.9% of revenue | Yen weakness; carrier-controlled channel | Samsung, Google, Sharp | S6 |
| Rest of Asia-Pacific | Not published; emerging markets forecast down more than 20% in 2026 | Apple +19.4% in 9M FY2026 | Entered; 8.1% of revenue; India manufacturing and retail | Price sensitivity; tariffs | Samsung, Xiaomi, vivo, OPPO, Transsion | S84, S6 |

Geography splits the durability question. Greater China was 15.5% of FY2025 revenue and grew 30% in the first nine months of FY2026; Europe is 26.7% and grew 16%, the Americas 42.9% and 11%, Japan 6.9% and 10%, Rest of Asia-Pacific 8.1% and 19%. China is the most fragile in size, not share: the market fell 10% in Q3 2026 to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 on Counterpoint's count, yet Apple's share rose 4.8 points to 19.5%, while IDC's lower 17.8% counts shipments rather than sell-through, a gap consistent with channel inventory drawing down. The EU cut the commission on externally distributed digital transactions to 5% from 1 October 2026. Demand is organic consumer replacement, not policy-created: China's subsidies faded in 2026 and India's incentives are supply-side. The budget owner is the consumer or a carrier financing plan; the procurement cycle follows the September launch. Confidence is high on 2026 data and low on 2027-2030 regional sizing, because regional market values are paywalled and Apple discloses no units; the open questions are how much iPhone growth is units versus price, whether services growth is users or price, and how much memory cost Apple can pass through in FY2027 [S6, S139, S140, S96, S77, S84].

::: evidence
**Apple's markets are growing in dollars while shrinking in units, so its growth is price- and share-led, not market-led.**

The global pool is $613B of smartphone value in 2026 against just over 1.0B units, with a 27.6% ASP increase doing the work volume used to do (IDC, S84). {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Risk Assessment (risk, revision 11 by Red Team Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,950 characters)
Apple is a high-quality compounder whose price already capitalises a peak margin and a contested services annuity, so the risks that matter destroy the multiple, not the balance sheet, and none is priced at $344.63. At that price on 2026-10-30 the shares trade at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and the base DCF at a 9.0% cost of equity is $212. Eight risks follow: two are fatal to the price, the rest execution. The strategic risk is AI defending the price without widening the moat. [S7, S97, S10]

::: risk-matrix
| Risk | Probability | Impact | Level | Timing | Signpost | Mitigation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Memory cost pushes hardware gross margin below 46% | High, over 60% | EPS -6% per 200bp; -25% to -30% value | Critical | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | Product margin under 37%; DRAM/NAND prices | Enter at $270 only on the $9.27+ EPS case | S17, S6, S99, S136 |
| Google search payment cut or banned on appeal | Medium, 20-25% | EPS -10% to -13%; value -15% to -20% | High | 2027, D.C. Circuit No. 26-5023 | Argument schedule; renewal terms | Cap the position | S70, S76, S135 |
| Multiple reverts to the 31.0x four-year mean | Medium-high, 40-60% | -21.5% at 31x; -38% at 24.6x | High | 0-12 months | Ten-year yield above 5%; forward P/E above 40x | No position at $344.63 | S97, S10 |
| EU DMA fee band spreads to other markets | Medium, 20-40% | EU operating income -1% to -2%; -5% if it spreads | Medium | From 2026-10-01 | Services growth below 10%; developer migration | Underwrite 10-12% services | S77, S78, S102 |
| AI cycle fails; Gemini reprices per device | Medium, 20-40% | EPS -5% to -8% | High | FY2027 | Siri beta exit; services margin | Treat AI as a cost line | S111, S6, S137 |
| China demand falls 20% in H2 2026 | Medium, 30-50% | Revenue -3.5%; EPS -5% to -6% | Medium | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | China revenue; Q4 tracker data | Do not capitalise 30% China growth | S96, S84, S87 |
| Cash quality and inventory | Medium, 30-50% | FCF -$1.9bn to $123.2bn, 40.8x; inventory -$3.3bn | Low | 10-K, 2026-11-02 | Other-liabilities note; inventory $11.1bn | Underwrite the $123.2bn case | S6, S5, S17 |
| Governance and key-person | Low, under 20% | Value -5% to -10% | Low | 12-24 months | No named successor; director exits | Board refresh; retention | S134, S133, S141, S11 |
:::

### The risk that breaks the thesis is the hardware margin, not the platform

The 50.1% gross margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; because that margin applies to $466.8bn of revenue, one point is $4.7bn of operating income. Memory prices rose 146% in Q1 2026 versus 2025; TrendForce's 30 September 2026 forecast puts Q4 DRAM contract prices 10-15% higher quarter on quarter and NAND 15-20% higher; the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials is up 38%, memory at 34% against 10%. Two hundred basis points off the margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of the trailing $8.72; a 46% margin, 200bp below the 48% top of the base range, takes FY2027 EPS from $9.79 to $9.27 and, at 29x, puts fair value at $269 — the entry price, not a discount. [S17, S6, S99, S136]

::: info danger
**A memory-led gross margin below 46% breaks earnings and the multiple at once.** The margin applies to all $466.8bn of revenue, Apple cannot re-price handsets inside a quarter, and 39.5x leaves no room for a 6% EPS cut: 200bp also invites a de-rating from 35x forward to the 31x mean, together a 25-30% drawdown. The signpost is the December-quarter margin guide on 2026-11-02 (S17, S6, S136).
:::

### The search payment is a renegotiation risk until the appeal says otherwise

The trial record put the payment at $20bn in 2022 — 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and 15% of operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy preserved non-exclusive payments; the American Antitrust Institute's 4 August 2026 brief asks the D.C. Circuit to strike it, and Google's appeal, No. 26-5023, with the DOJ's cross-appeal, stays live into 2027. I price a 20-25% probability of a ban at -10% to -13% of EPS and -15% to -20% of value. The EU fee schedule from 2026-10-01 — 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission — is modest in situ: Europe is 26.7% of nine-month revenue and each $1bn of commission lost is $0.75bn of gross profit. A 5-15% band extended to the United States would reset services growth to high single digits. [S70, S76, S77, S79, S135]

### The growth swing factors are AI and China

Siri shipped as an English beta on 2026-09-14 on a Gemini model licensed at a reported $1bn a year. Apple rents the capability and books the bill in operating expense; no filing names an AI profit-and-loss owner after the 2025-12-01 reorganisation, and X Corp. and xAI's suit survived dismissal. A $1bn licence is 0.6% of operating income, so the base case holds while pricing is annual; per-device pricing across 2.5bn devices would land in the 76.3% services margin, and whether a licensed assistant sells $1,199 handsets is the swing factor. China is a shrinking pool, not a lost share war: Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's, with Apple at 19.5% against Huawei's 21.3%. Greater China was 17.8% of nine-month FY2026 revenue; IDC sees the decline widening to 20% in H2 2026, and a 20% China decline is 3.5% of group revenue and 5-6% of EPS. Supply adds India — 25% of iPhones, incentives expired 2026-03-31, costs above China's — and Section 301 duties replacing the IEEPA tariffs struck down on 2026-02-20. [S111, S6, S127, S137, S96, S84, S87, S115]

### Valuation is the risk, and the entry ladder assumes the base EPS

At 39.5x, Apple sits at a five-year high for a company guiding 9-11% growth, and 40.2x trailing free cash flow of $125.1bn (39.5-41.0x across the $122.6-127.3bn band, on $5,029.6bn) makes the multiple the largest driver of return: reversion to the 31.0x mean costs 21.5%, reversion to the 24.6x FY2022 trough 38%. Each 50bp on the cost of equity moves the DCF 15-18%; the ten-year is 4.93% against a 7.0% implied return. A 30% revenue fall leaves $326.8bn; on the 43.0% nine-month incremental operating margin it leaves $94.6bn of operating income and $5.4 of EPS, but that is an up-cycle margin. On the FY2021-FY2025 average gross margin of 44.5%, with $72.3bn of operating expense held flat, gross profit is $145.3bn, operating income $73.0bn and EPS $4.10 at the 17.3% tax rate on 14.75bn diluted shares — a 58% decremental margin, not 43%; a 10% cost cut lifts EPS to $4.50, and the FY2016-FY2025 average margin of 41.4% gives $3.54. At 29x that is $103-131, at or below the $133 DCF bear. A market 50% smaller is revenue 35% lower and EPS $3.51, $70-88 at 20-25x. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn, 56.4-58.6x, covering the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of buybacks and dividends; a 30% inventory write-down is $3.3bn, 1.9% of operating income; 100 basis points on $84.3bn of debt is $0.84bn, 0.5%. Apple survives all of them on $62.2bn of net cash and $146.5bn of securities; the equity does not. The entry ladder is the same single-point bet: 0.75-1.0% at $270 is 27.6x only on FY2027 EPS of $9.79. A 46% gross margin takes EPS to $9.27 and $270 to 29.1x; a search cut of 12.9% takes $9.79 to $8.53 and, with the margin, to $8.07, so $270 becomes 31.7x to 33.5x against the 31.0x four-year mean and $245 becomes 28.7x to 30.4x. The same 27.6x is $223-235 on $8.07-8.53. The ladder needs a condition, not a new number: $270 only if the 2026-11-02 guide holds FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and December gross margin at 47%; otherwise the first tranche belongs at $235 and the second at $210, with the 5% cap unchanged. [S10, S97, S6, S5, S151, S70]

### Governance, unknowns and the call

Governance and key-person risk are monitors. Cook is Executive Chair and Ternus CEO under a nine-director board. Srouji's 2025-12-06 departure report is superseded by his 2026-04-20 promotion to Chief Hardware Officer with hardware engineering added to his silicon remit, which concentrates rather than removes the dependency. Cash quality is smaller than it looked: the $13,531M non-current liability build against $13,270M of gross intangibles added reads as deferred consideration, but net of a $4,128M current-liability fall it is $9,403M, inside the $10,016M line; if unpaid, free cash flow is $123.2bn, inside the $122.6-127.3bn band. Outside the filings: a Taiwan Strait disruption stopping 2nm supply, and an appellate remedy treating the Gemini default as the next search payment. The downside is a de-rating, not insolvency, so position size carries the risk; open diligence is the December-quarter margin guide, the 10-K working-capital note, the appellate schedule and the Gemini renewal terms. None changes the call: the price, not the business, is the problem, and the $270 entry holds only if December confirms the margin trough and EPS at $9.27 or better. [S134, S133, S141, S11, S5, S6]"}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Technology & Product (technology_product, revision 7 by Product Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,810 characters)
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a very large installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer the current upgrade cycle is sold on has been rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with a Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capital spending fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026, while the standard iPhone 18, 18e and a second-generation Air are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was repriced to $899. The mechanism is deliberate: sell the expensive, 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March, when yields and memory supply have matured. The risk is elasticity: prices rose into a memory-cost cycle, and December 2026 is the first test. [S112]

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as a beta in English, 23 months after Apple Intelligence first shipped in October 2024. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither company confirmed the price. Apple's own contribution is the interface, personal context and Private Cloud Compute. On 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI Safety passed under software chief Craig Federighi as John Giannandrea stepped down: Apple bought what it could not ship and reorganised the rest. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.**

Google confirmed a multi-year deal on 2026-01-12 to supply Gemini models for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year and 1.2 trillion parameters, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface, the data boundary and the device; it does not keep the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The AI bill lands in R&D, not capex

Rented intelligence sits in operating expense, not on the balance sheet: R&D rose a third in nine months while capital spending fell. Free cash flow stays intact and the buyback continues. The marginal AI dollar has no asset behind it, and bargaining power sits with the supplier that also owns Android.

### Silicon is the layer still widening

The A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem reported across the iPhone 18 line, are the parts of the stack Apple still owns end to end. At a fixed price a node advantage becomes margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing warns that advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints are expected to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. [S112]

| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue | 5+ years | S6 |

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions accuracy and usefulness. It is a monthly alert, not a measurement, so the clinical claim is narrow. Vision Pro and the watch add upgrade reasons and switching costs, but they are sold as features, not platforms with their own economics.

### The hinge is patented; the newest generation is not Apple's alone

Three records pulled from the patent database on 2026-10-31 correct what the aggregate grant count obscured. Apple has held a granted, active hinge patent since 2020-02-04 and a granted four-jurisdiction hinge family since 2024-12-10, both solely owned, so the Duo's folding mechanism is protected as a mechanism, not merely by know-how. U.S. utility grants still fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082, ranking Apple seventh, and no Apple-owned on-device inference patent was verified, so the AI layer's constraint is the Gemini licence rather than the patent estate. On replication: a funded team of 50 holding US12164344B2 could copy the linkage in two to three years but not the process yield behind it, and an A-series chip only after a full node cycle; it would still lack the installed base, and the assistant can be licensed, as Apple did. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Exit Strategy Analysis (exit, revision 6 by Valuation Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,957 characters)
Apple's only exit is the public market and its own buyback, and at $344.63 the shares already discount the scenario bull. No peer is large enough to acquire it — Microsoft at $3,875.8bn, Alphabet at $3,461.1bn, Amazon at $2,598.9bn and Meta at $1,582.4bn are all smaller than Apple's $5,071.2bn market value (14,715m diluted shares at $344.63) — so a holder's realisation depends entirely on the multiple another investor will pay. With dividend and gross buyback yielding 1.9% and earnings per share compounding at 8-9%, the arithmetic is adequate only while the 39.3x multiple holds; if it reverts toward the four-year average of 31.0x, the three-year return from $344.63 falls to 1.3% a year. That sets the sell discipline: buy below $270, where the three-year return spans 5.0-13.3% around 9.9%, and treat $380 and above as a sale [S7, S11, S6].

| Metric | Value | Implication | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Average daily volume | 40.41m shares and $13.84bn (20-day); 41.34m and $13.56bn (3-month) | A $250m position is 1.8% of one day's value traded; $1bn is 7.2% | S7 |
| Shares outstanding | 14,715m diluted at 2026-06-27; the proxy's 14,697.9m basic at 2026-01-02 is 0.1% lower | Free float effectively 100%; one count for the market cap | S6, S11 |
| Largest holders | Vanguard 9.63%; BlackRock 7.10% | Index managers, no controlling or strategic holder | S11 |
| Directors and officers | 9,079,765 shares, 0.06% | Aligned, but immaterial to the register | S11 |

Liquidity is the one exit risk that can be dismissed: Apple's daily turnover dwarfs any position a long-only fund would take, so the exit is never closed and market impact is measured in basis points. The intended holding period is three years. What cannot be dismissed is price: the buyers on the other side are the same index and active funds the seller competes with, and in a broad de-rating they mark the same multiple down together.

| Component | Rate | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Dividend yield | 0.31% ($1.08 annualised on $344.63) | S17, S7 |
| Buyback yield, gross | 1.62% ($82.2bn repurchased on a $5,071.2bn market value) | S6, S7 |
| Buyback yield, net of $13.7bn stock compensation | 1.35% | S6, S7 |
| Total shareholder yield | 1.93% | S6, S7 |
| EPS growth, FY2021 to TTM / FY2027E to FY2029E | 9.2% / 8.2% | S1, S6 |
| Three-year return, multiple unchanged at 39.3x | 9.6% a year | S7, S97 |
| Three-year return, multiple reverts to 31.0x | 1.3% a year | S7, S97 |

Two things follow. The operating return is real but modest: a 1.9% yield plus 8% earnings growth is a high-single-digit compounding machine, not the 27.5% twelve-month return the shares have just delivered. And the buyback does much of the work, buying a 2.5% earnings yield per dollar at 39.3x, below the 4.93% ten-year Treasury, so it supports the price without creating value at this level. That is what a mature cash machine should do with cash it cannot reinvest at its own cost of capital, but an investor paying 39.3x is paying for the cash return, not receiving a bargain from it [S6, S1].

The multiple, not the business, is the swing factor. Apple traded at 24.6x at the end of FY2022, 27.9x in FY2023, 37.5x in FY2024 and 34.2x in FY2025; it now trades at 39.3x trailing and 35.2x forward, against a twelve-month average of 35.7x. A reversion to the four-year mean of 31.0x costs 21.1% of the price, or 7.6% a year over three years, which swallows the entire shareholder yield and most of the earnings growth. With the ten-year Treasury at 4.93%, up 84 basis points in a year, the discount on cash flows after 2035 is materially higher than when the shares traded at 27.9x [S7, S97, S10].

| Route | Named buyer or venue | Rationale | Timing | Likelihood | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open-market sale | NasdaqGS continuous auction | $13.8bn a day; exit complete in days | Any trading day | Near-certain, and the default route | S7 |
| Issuer repurchase | Apple Inc., under its board authorisation | $82.2bn in the twelve months to June 2026; $100bn authorised in May 2025 | Continuous; next authorisation with the May 2027 results | High | S6, S5 |
| Dividend | Apple Inc. | $0.27 a quarter, raised annually | Quarterly, with an annual increase each May | High | S17 |
| Strategic acquisition | No buyer large enough: the four largest peers are all smaller than Apple | Antitrust review in the US, EU, China and UK would follow any bid; a foreign buyer would also face CFIUS national-security review | Not foreseeable | Negligible | S14, S16, S108, S110 |
| Break-up or activist | None identified | Sum of the parts is $177-238 a share against a $5,071.2bn market value | No campaign disclosed | Negligible | S6, S17 |
| Passive flows | S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 index funds | Largest company in the peer set | Quarterly rebalancing | Structural, not a decision | S11 |

No listing or lock-up constraint applies: the shares already trade on NasdaqGS, and only the buyback blackout around results restricts the issuer. The open market is the route that matters, and the price at which it clears is the only variable the holder controls.

The precedents are all capital returns, because that is the only exit a company of this size has ever offered its holders. They also show the cost of buying back stock at the top: the FY2024 and FY2025 programmes together spent $185.6bn at 34-38x earnings, and those shares would have been retired 18-26% cheaper at the FY2023 multiple. An investor buying today at 39.3x makes the same choice management made, at a higher price [S4, S5].

It also follows from the scenario range: at $344.63 the shares are 97% of the $357 scenario bull at 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 and 121% of the $284 scenario base at 29x, while the DCF bull at an 8.5% discount rate is $277, 20% below the market. A long-only fund earns its 9% hurdle from $270, not from $344; the shares are a buy only on a de-rating or on evidence that FY2027-28 earnings growth is running above 12% rather than the 9.9% consensus assumes for iPhone revenue. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Business Model (business_model, revision 6 by Fundamentals Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,497 characters)
Apple monetises the same customer twice: once through a hardware sale at a 39.9% gross margin that is paid for before the cost is incurred, and again through a services annuity at a 76.3% gross margin that costs almost nothing incremental to serve. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 the company recorded $466,823M of revenue and $227,123M of gross profit — iPhone $245,540M (52.6% of revenue), Services $120,478M (25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit), Mac $35,863M, Wearables, Home and Accessories $36,290M and iPad $28,652M. Services gross profit of $91,607M covers total company R&D of $42,901M 2.1 times, so the annuity already pays for the AI build-out. The mix, not the growth rate, is what an investor is underwriting. [S5, S6]

### The 2026 acceleration is hardware, not annuity

In the nine months to 27 June 2026 revenue grew 16.1%, but the engines ran at different speeds: iPhone +22.4%, Mac +8.6%, iPad +3.0%, Wearables +2.3%, Services +14.1%. Services therefore fell to 25.2% of revenue from 26.2% in FY2025 — the first year-over-year decline in the mix since at least FY2023, when services were 22.2% of revenue. Greater China grew 30% after shrinking 4% in FY2025. The standard account of Apple as a services compounder is not what the last three quarters show; they show an iPhone cycle carried by Pro-model mix, with the annuity growing at 14.1% against iPhone's 22.4%. Consensus puts iPhone revenue at $252.4bn for FY2026 and $277.4bn for FY2027, a 9.9% step that assumes the price-and-mix cycle repeats without unit growth. [S5, S6, S71]

### What one device earns

Apple stopped disclosing unit shipments, so the most defensible unit is the active device. The table divides trailing-twelve-month flows by Apple's own installed-base statement; because that base is an earnings-call figure rather than a filed one, every line is an estimate.

| Line item | Per unit — per active device, per year | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $186.7 | $466,823M TTM ÷ 2,500M devices | S6, S73 |
| of which Services | $48.2 | $120,478M TTM ÷ 2,500M | S6, S73 |
| Gross profit | $90.8 | 48.7% blended gross margin | S6 |
| Selling, general and administrative | ($11.7) | $29,363M TTM | S6 |
| Research and development | ($17.2) | $42,901M TTM | S6 |
| Operating profit | $61.9 | $154,859M TTM | S6 |
| Gross profit ÷ selling cost | 7.8x a year | $90.8 ÷ $11.7 | S6 |
| Cash payback on acquisition | immediate | cash conversion cycle −56.8 days | S5, S6 |

The waterfall ends where most hardware businesses begin: there is no customer-acquisition payback period to compute, because Apple is paid by carriers and retailers before it pays its assemblers. Payables of $64,525M against inventory of $11,092M produced a cash conversion cycle of −56.8 days at 27 June 2026, against +39.2 days at Alphabet; each new device is cash-positive on day one. The unit count is the weak link, and Apple discloses none: the $941 implied iPhone price rests on a 261M-unit estimate, and on a 20% share of the 1.26B units shipped in 2025 it is $832, while on about 238M units in 2026 (23.6% of IDC's 1.01B) the $252.4bn consensus is $1,060 — a 27% rise that is memory pass-through and Pro mix, not evidence of an upgrade cycle. That advantage is not a scale economy a rival can buy with capital; it is the accounting consequence of owning the customer and outsourcing the factory. [S6, S73, S74, S84, S92, S99]

| Offer | Price or take rate | Margin or peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone (upfront hardware) | implied ASP $941 on 261M estimated units; $832-1,060 across unit bases | products gross margin 39.9% | S6, S74, S92 |
| App Store (commission, ex-EU) | 15-30%; the 27% link-out commission was ruled prohibitive | services gross margin 76.3% | S6, S69 |
| App Store (EU, from 2026-10-01) | 26% in-app purchase, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission | EU band 5-26% against 15-30% elsewhere | S77, S78 |
| Safari default search | 36% of Safari search advertising; $20B in 2022 | 16.6% of TTM services revenue | S70 |
| Subscriptions and cloud | recurring, bundled at the device sale | services 76.3% vs Microsoft 67.9% in FY2026 | S6, S49 |
| Handset peer — Samsung devices (DX) | — | KRW 0.8tn operating loss in Q3 2026 | S75 |

### The annuity rests on two contested tolls

The 10-K describes Services as advertising (including third-party licensing arrangements), AppleCare, cloud, the App Store, subscription content and payment services, but never splits their revenue. Two of those lines are tolls on other people's commerce. The first is the App Store commission: on 11 December 2025 the Ninth Circuit held that Apple's 27% commission on purchases made after a user follows a link out of an app had a prohibitive effect, and remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, may be charged. The second is the Google default-search licence, where court records show Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and a 2022 payment put at $20B — 16.6% of trailing-twelve-month services revenue of $120,478M and 12.9% of trailing-twelve-month operating income of $154,859M; measured on FY2025 the same $20B would be 18.3% of $109,158M services revenue and 15.0% of $133,050M operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy kept the payments but barred exclusivity and capped any default arrangement at twelve months, and Google's D.C. Circuit brief of 22 May 2026 challenges that judgment. [S69, S70]

### The cost side has turned, and the multiple is buying a margin

The 2026 margin record is partly purchased. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% a year earlier, and the 10-Q attributes the gain to product mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher costs including memory; the third-quarter release put the refund benefit at 2 percentage points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS. Against that, memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 versus the 2025 average, Samsung's mobile memory costs rose 107%, and Apple's filing expects the component trends "to intensify, which may materially negatively impact" revenue, costs and gross margin — the elasticity admission a hardware model has to make. A 47-48% gross margin is the defensible base case, not the 50.1% just printed, and the FY2027 EPS of $9.79 that the $284 base case and the $270 entry divide by requires 48.0%, with each 100 basis points worth $0.30 of that EPS. The risk runs both ways: Apple has passed component cycles through before by raising prices and shifting to Pro models, and Greater China grew 30% in the nine months, so margin could hold above 47% rather than break below it, in which case the earnings band and the entry price move up together. At $344.63 on 30 October 2026 the market capitalisation is $5,034bn on the 14,608,963 thousand shares outstanding at 27 June 2026 — 39.5x trailing diluted EPS of $8.72 — and that price already assumes the annuity survives intact and that memory costs are passed through. The business is a negative-working-capital hardware engine bolted to a high-margin annuity, and the annuity is the terminal value: that justifies a premium to hardware peers but not a software multiple on the whole revenue base, because a quarter of revenue sits in a line where two tolls are being repriced in court. The open diligence is narrow and decisive: does services growth re-accelerate above 15% without hardware mix; what commission does the district court set on remand; and when does memory pricing peak in supplier guidance? Confidence in the mix arithmetic is high because it comes from filed segment data; confidence in the durability of the tolls is medium, because Apple discloses neither their size nor their terms, and the FY2026 10-K expected alongside the 2 November 2026 results is the document that would close the gap. [S6, S7, S17, S68]

::: evidence
**The services annuity is what the multiple buys, and it is a smaller share of revenue than it was a year ago.**

Services produced $120,478M of trailing-twelve-month revenue — 25.8% of the total but 40.3% of gross profit and 2.1x company R&D — while its revenue share fell to 25.2% in the nine months to 27 June 2026 as iPhone revenue grew 22.4% against services growth of 14.1% (S5, S6, S17). Two tolls inside that line, the App Store commission and the Safari search licence worth 16.6% of services revenue on a 2022 court figure, are both under active legal challenge (S69, S70).
:::"}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Risk Assessment (risk, revision 11 by Red Team Analyst, changed since the previous version, 8,950 characters)
Apple is a high-quality compounder whose price already capitalises a peak margin and a contested services annuity, so the risks that matter destroy the multiple, not the balance sheet, and none is priced at $344.63. At that price on 2026-10-30 the shares trade at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and the base DCF at a 9.0% cost of equity is $212. Eight risks follow: two are fatal to the price, the rest execution. The strategic risk is AI defending the price without widening the moat. [S7, S97, S10]

::: risk-matrix
| Risk | Probability | Impact | Level | Timing | Signpost | Mitigation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Memory cost pushes hardware gross margin below 46% | High, over 60% | EPS -6% per 200bp; -25% to -30% value | Critical | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | Product margin under 37%; DRAM/NAND prices | Enter at $270 only on the $9.27+ EPS case | S17, S6, S99, S136 |
| Google search payment cut or banned on appeal | Medium, 20-25% | EPS -10% to -13%; value -15% to -20% | High | 2027, D.C. Circuit No. 26-5023 | Argument schedule; renewal terms | Cap the position | S70, S76, S135 |
| Multiple reverts to the 31.0x four-year mean | Medium-high, 40-60% | -21.5% at 31x; -38% at 24.6x | High | 0-12 months | Ten-year yield above 5%; forward P/E above 40x | No position at $344.63 | S97, S10 |
| EU DMA fee band spreads to other markets | Medium, 20-40% | EU operating income -1% to -2%; -5% if it spreads | Medium | From 2026-10-01 | Services growth below 10%; developer migration | Underwrite 10-12% services | S77, S78, S102 |
| AI cycle fails; Gemini reprices per device | Medium, 20-40% | EPS -5% to -8% | High | FY2027 | Siri beta exit; services margin | Treat AI as a cost line | S111, S6, S137 |
| China demand falls 20% in H2 2026 | Medium, 30-50% | Revenue -3.5%; EPS -5% to -6% | Medium | Q4 FY2026-FY2027 | China revenue; Q4 tracker data | Do not capitalise 30% China growth | S96, S84, S87 |
| Cash quality and inventory | Medium, 30-50% | FCF -$1.9bn to $123.2bn, 40.8x; inventory -$3.3bn | Low | 10-K, 2026-11-02 | Other-liabilities note; inventory $11.1bn | Underwrite the $123.2bn case | S6, S5, S17 |
| Governance and key-person | Low, under 20% | Value -5% to -10% | Low | 12-24 months | No named successor; director exits | Board refresh; retention | S134, S133, S141, S11 |
:::

### The risk that breaks the thesis is the hardware margin, not the platform

The 50.1% gross margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; because that margin applies to $466.8bn of revenue, one point is $4.7bn of operating income. Memory prices rose 146% in Q1 2026 versus 2025; TrendForce's 30 September 2026 forecast puts Q4 DRAM contract prices 10-15% higher quarter on quarter and NAND 15-20% higher; the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials is up 38%, memory at 34% against 10%. Two hundred basis points off the margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of the trailing $8.72; a 46% margin, 200bp below the 48% top of the base range, takes FY2027 EPS from $9.79 to $9.27 and, at 29x, puts fair value at $269 — the entry price, not a discount. [S17, S6, S99, S136]

::: info danger
**A memory-led gross margin below 46% breaks earnings and the multiple at once.** The margin applies to all $466.8bn of revenue, Apple cannot re-price handsets inside a quarter, and 39.5x leaves no room for a 6% EPS cut: 200bp also invites a de-rating from 35x forward to the 31x mean, together a 25-30% drawdown. The signpost is the December-quarter margin guide on 2026-11-02 (S17, S6, S136).
:::

### The search payment is a renegotiation risk until the appeal says otherwise

The trial record put the payment at $20bn in 2022 — 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and 15% of operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy preserved non-exclusive payments; the American Antitrust Institute's 4 August 2026 brief asks the D.C. Circuit to strike it, and Google's appeal, No. 26-5023, with the DOJ's cross-appeal, stays live into 2027. I price a 20-25% probability of a ban at -10% to -13% of EPS and -15% to -20% of value. The EU fee schedule from 2026-10-01 — 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission — is modest in situ: Europe is 26.7% of nine-month revenue and each $1bn of commission lost is $0.75bn of gross profit. A 5-15% band extended to the United States would reset services growth to high single digits. [S70, S76, S77, S79, S135]

### The growth swing factors are AI and China

Siri shipped as an English beta on 2026-09-14 on a Gemini model licensed at a reported $1bn a year. Apple rents the capability and books the bill in operating expense; no filing names an AI profit-and-loss owner after the 2025-12-01 reorganisation, and X Corp. and xAI's suit survived dismissal. A $1bn licence is 0.6% of operating income, so the base case holds while pricing is annual; per-device pricing across 2.5bn devices would land in the 76.3% services margin, and whether a licensed assistant sells $1,199 handsets is the swing factor. China is a shrinking pool, not a lost share war: Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's, with Apple at 19.5% against Huawei's 21.3%. Greater China was 17.8% of nine-month FY2026 revenue; IDC sees the decline widening to 20% in H2 2026, and a 20% China decline is 3.5% of group revenue and 5-6% of EPS. Supply adds India — 25% of iPhones, incentives expired 2026-03-31, costs above China's — and Section 301 duties replacing the IEEPA tariffs struck down on 2026-02-20. [S111, S6, S127, S137, S96, S84, S87, S115]

### Valuation is the risk, and the entry ladder assumes the base EPS

At 39.5x, Apple sits at a five-year high for a company guiding 9-11% growth, and 40.2x trailing free cash flow of $125.1bn (39.5-41.0x across the $122.6-127.3bn band, on $5,029.6bn) makes the multiple the largest driver of return: reversion to the 31.0x mean costs 21.5%, reversion to the 24.6x FY2022 trough 38%. Each 50bp on the cost of equity moves the DCF 15-18%; the ten-year is 4.93% against a 7.0% implied return. A 30% revenue fall leaves $326.8bn; on the 43.0% nine-month incremental operating margin it leaves $94.6bn of operating income and $5.4 of EPS, but that is an up-cycle margin. On the FY2021-FY2025 average gross margin of 44.5%, with $72.3bn of operating expense held flat, gross profit is $145.3bn, operating income $73.0bn and EPS $4.10 at the 17.3% tax rate on 14.75bn diluted shares — a 58% decremental margin, not 43%; a 10% cost cut lifts EPS to $4.50, and the FY2016-FY2025 average margin of 41.4% gives $3.54. At 29x that is $103-131, at or below the $133 DCF bear. A market 50% smaller is revenue 35% lower and EPS $3.51, $70-88 at 20-25x. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn, 56.4-58.6x, covering the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of buybacks and dividends; a 30% inventory write-down is $3.3bn, 1.9% of operating income; 100 basis points on $84.3bn of debt is $0.84bn, 0.5%. Apple survives all of them on $62.2bn of net cash and $146.5bn of securities; the equity does not. The entry ladder is the same single-point bet: 0.75-1.0% at $270 is 27.6x only on FY2027 EPS of $9.79. A 46% gross margin takes EPS to $9.27 and $270 to 29.1x; a search cut of 12.9% takes $9.79 to $8.53 and, with the margin, to $8.07, so $270 becomes 31.7x to 33.5x against the 31.0x four-year mean and $245 becomes 28.7x to 30.4x. The same 27.6x is $223-235 on $8.07-8.53. The ladder needs a condition, not a new number: $270 only if the 2026-11-02 guide holds FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and December gross margin at 47%; otherwise the first tranche belongs at $235 and the second at $210, with the 5% cap unchanged. [S10, S97, S6, S5, S151, S70]

### Governance, unknowns and the call

Governance and key-person risk are monitors. Cook is Executive Chair and Ternus CEO under a nine-director board. Srouji's 2025-12-06 departure report is superseded by his 2026-04-20 promotion to Chief Hardware Officer with hardware engineering added to his silicon remit, which concentrates rather than removes the dependency. Cash quality is smaller than it looked: the $13,531M non-current liability build against $13,270M of gross intangibles added reads as deferred consideration, but net of a $4,128M current-liability fall it is $9,403M, inside the $10,016M line; if unpaid, free cash flow is $123.2bn, inside the $122.6-127.3bn band. Outside the filings: a Taiwan Strait disruption stopping 2nm supply, and an appellate remedy treating the Gemini default as the next search payment. The downside is a de-rating, not insolvency, so position size carries the risk; open diligence is the December-quarter margin guide, the 10-K working-capital note, the appellate schedule and the Gemini renewal terms. None changes the call: the price, not the business, is the problem, and the $270 entry holds only if December confirms the margin trough and EPS at $9.27 or better. [S134, S133, S141, S11, S5, S6]"}],"isError":false}

Apple monetises the same customer twice: once through a hardware sale at a 39.9% gross margin that is paid for before the cost is incurred, and again through a services annuity at a 76.3% gross margin that costs almost nothing incremental to serve. ### The 2026 acceleration is hardware, not annuity

In the nine months to 27 June 2026 revenue grew 16.1%, but the engines ran at different speeds: iPhone +22.4%, Mac +8.6%, iPad +3.0%, Wearables +2.3%, Services +14.1%. ### The annuity rests on two contested tolls

The 10-K describes Services as advertising (including third-party licensing arrangements), AppleCare, cloud, the App Store, subscription content and payment services, but never splits their revenue. Two of those lines are tolls on other people's commerce. The first is the App Store commission: on 11 December 2025 the Ninth Circuit held that Apple's 27% commission on purchases made after a user follows a link out of an app had a prohibitive effect, and remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, may be charged. The open diligence is narrow and decisive: does services growth re-accelerate above 15% without hardware mix; what commission does the district court set on remand; and when does memory pricing peak in supplier guidance? {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Business Model (business_model, revision 7 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,517 characters)
Apple monetises the same customer twice: once through a hardware sale at a 39.9% gross margin that is paid for before the cost is incurred, and again through a services annuity at a 76.3% gross margin that costs almost nothing incremental to serve. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 the company recorded $466,823M of revenue and $227,123M of gross profit — iPhone $245,540M (52.6% of revenue), Services $120,478M (25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit), Mac $35,863M, Wearables, Home and Accessories $36,290M and iPad $28,652M. Services gross profit of $91,607M covers total company R&D of $42,901M 2.1 times, so the annuity already pays for the AI build-out. The mix, not the growth rate, is what an investor is underwriting. [S5, S6]

### The 2026 acceleration is hardware, not annuity

In the nine months to 27 June 2026 revenue grew 16.1%, but the engines ran at different speeds: iPhone +22.4%, Mac +8.6%, iPad +3.0%, Wearables +2.3%, Services +14.1%. Services therefore fell to 25.2% of revenue from 26.2% in FY2025 — the first year-over-year decline in the mix since at least FY2023, when services were 22.2% of revenue. Greater China grew 30% after shrinking 4% in FY2025. The standard account of Apple as a services compounder is not what the last three quarters show; they show an iPhone cycle carried by Pro-model mix, with the annuity growing at 14.1% against iPhone's 22.4%. Consensus puts iPhone revenue at $252.4bn for FY2026 and $277.4bn for FY2027, a 9.9% step that assumes the price-and-mix cycle repeats without unit growth. [S5, S6, S71]

### What one device earns

Apple stopped disclosing unit shipments, so the most defensible unit is the active device. The table divides trailing-twelve-month flows by Apple's own installed-base statement; because that base is an earnings-call figure rather than a filed one, every line is an estimate.

| Line item | Per unit — per active device, per year | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $186.7 | $466,823M TTM ÷ 2,500M devices | S6, S73 |
| of which Services | $48.2 | $120,478M TTM ÷ 2,500M | S6, S73 |
| Gross profit | $90.8 | 48.7% blended gross margin | S6 |
| Selling, general and administrative | ($11.7) | $29,363M TTM | S6 |
| Research and development | ($17.2) | $42,901M TTM | S6 |
| Operating profit | $61.9 | $154,859M TTM | S6 |
| Gross profit ÷ selling cost | 7.8x a year | $90.8 ÷ $11.7 | S6 |
| Cash payback on acquisition | immediate | cash conversion cycle −56.8 days | S5, S6 |

The waterfall ends where most hardware businesses begin: there is no customer-acquisition payback period to compute, because Apple is paid by carriers and retailers before it pays its assemblers. Payables of $64,525M against inventory of $11,092M produced a cash conversion cycle of −56.8 days at 27 June 2026, against +39.2 days at Alphabet; each new device is cash-positive on day one. The unit count is the weak link, and Apple discloses none: the $941 implied iPhone price rests on a 261M-unit estimate, and on a 20% share of the 1.26B units shipped in 2025 it is $832, while on about 238M units in 2026 (23.6% of IDC's 1.01B) the $252.4bn consensus is $1,060 — a 27% rise that is memory pass-through and Pro mix, not evidence of an upgrade cycle. That advantage is not a scale economy a rival can buy with capital; it is the accounting consequence of owning the customer and outsourcing the factory. [S6, S73, S74, S84, S92, S99]

| Offer | Price or take rate | Margin or peer benchmark | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone (upfront hardware) | implied ASP $941 on 261M estimated units; $832-1,060 across unit bases | products gross margin 39.9% | S6, S74, S92 |
| App Store (commission, ex-EU) | 15-30%; the 27% link-out commission was ruled prohibitive | services gross margin 76.3% | S6, S69 |
| App Store (EU, from 2026-10-01) | 26% in-app purchase, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission | EU band 5-26% against 15-30% elsewhere | S77, S78 |
| Safari default search | 36% of Safari search advertising; $20B in 2022 | 16.6% of TTM services revenue | S70 |
| Subscriptions and cloud | recurring, bundled at the device sale | services 76.3% vs Microsoft 67.9% in FY2026 | S6, S49 |
| Handset peer — Samsung devices (DX) | — | KRW 0.8tn operating loss in Q3 2026 | S75 |

### The annuity rests on two contested tolls

The 10-K describes Services as advertising (including third-party licensing arrangements), AppleCare, cloud, the App Store, subscription content and payment services, but never splits their revenue. Two of those lines are tolls on other people's commerce. The first is the App Store commission: on 11 December 2025 the Ninth Circuit held that Apple's 27% commission on purchases made after a user follows a link out of an app had a prohibitive effect, and remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, may be charged. The second is the Google default-search licence, where court records show Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and a 2022 payment put at $20B — 16.6% of trailing-twelve-month services revenue of $120,478M and 12.9% of trailing-twelve-month operating income of $154,859M; measured on FY2025 the same $20B would be 18.3% of $109,158M services revenue and 15.0% of $133,050M operating income. Judge Mehta's remedy kept the payments but barred exclusivity and capped any default arrangement at twelve months, and Google's D.C. Circuit brief of 22 May 2026 challenges that judgment. [S69, S70]

### The cost side has turned, and the multiple is buying a margin

The 2026 margin record is partly purchased. Products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% a year earlier, and the 10-Q attributes the gain to product mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher costs including memory; the third-quarter release put the refund benefit at 2 percentage points of gross margin and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS. Against that, memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 versus the 2025 average, Samsung's mobile memory costs rose 107%, and Apple's filing expects the component trends "to intensify, which may materially negatively impact" revenue, costs and gross margin — the elasticity admission a hardware model has to make. A 47-48% gross margin is the defensible base case, not the 50.1% just printed, and the FY2027 EPS of $9.79 that the $284 base case and the $270 entry divide by requires 48.0%, with each 100 basis points worth $0.30 of that EPS. The risk runs both ways: Apple has passed component cycles through before by raising prices and shifting to Pro models, and Greater China grew 30% in the nine months, so margin could hold above 47% rather than break below it, in which case the earnings band and the entry price move up together. At $344.63 on 30 October 2026 the market capitalisation is $5,071.2bn on 14,715M diluted shares — 39.3x trailing net income of $128,930M, or 39.5x on the $8.72 sum-of-quarters diluted EPS — and that price already assumes the annuity survives intact and that memory costs are passed through. The business is a negative-working-capital hardware engine bolted to a high-margin annuity, and the annuity is the terminal value: that justifies a premium to hardware peers but not a software multiple on the whole revenue base, because a quarter of revenue sits in a line where two tolls are being repriced in court. The open diligence is narrow and decisive: does services growth re-accelerate above 15% without hardware mix; what commission does the district court set on remand; and when does memory pricing peak in supplier guidance? Confidence in the mix arithmetic is high because it comes from filed segment data; confidence in the durability of the tolls is medium, because Apple discloses neither their size nor their terms, and the FY2026 10-K expected alongside the 2 November 2026 results is the document that would close the gap. [S6, S7, S17, S68]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 4 by Lead Analyst, 8,989 characters)
Apple is a genuine compounder priced as a perpetual one. The installed base and services annuity are real, and FY2026 is strong: revenue rose 16.4% in the June quarter, iPhone revenue 22.4% in the nine months to 27 June 2026, and services earned 40.3% of gross profit on 25.8% of revenue. What is in dispute is the price: at $344.63 on 30 October 2026 the shares carry a $5,072bn market capitalisation, 39.3 times trailing and 35.2 times forward earnings, against an S&P 500 at 18.7 times forward. The decision is not whether Apple is a good business — it is — but whether a long-only fund should own it at a multiple that assumes the next five years go right [S6, S7, S97, S156].

Three valuation methods agree and none reaches the price. A discounted cash flow at a 9.0% cost of equity, built on the 4.93% ten-year Treasury, gives $212 a share; the DCF bull case at an 8.5% discount rate and a 35% operating margin gives $277; the sum of the parts is $177-238; the stock's own four-year average multiple of 31.0 times implies $303 [S6, S10, S97]. To justify $344.63 an investor needs a 7.0% discount rate or 6.4-6.9% perpetual growth in net operating profit after tax. Those assumptions make the price exactly fair rather than cheap; the base rate is modest, with revenue compounding 3.3% a year from FY2021 to FY2025.

The sell side sees fair value; this report sees 18% overvaluation: retail aggregator targets are $338-355, unverified, flat to +3% from the close [S142, S144]. Consensus expects iPhone revenue of $252.4bn in FY2026 and $277.4bn in FY2027 and capitalises the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin. The disagreement is specific: that margin included two points of tariff refunds, memory costs have turned (the iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials is up 38%, memory 34% of it), and our base case underwrites 47-48%. A 46% margin, which a full memory pass-through implies, takes FY2027 EPS to $9.3 and fair value to $270 at 29 times — the entry price below, not a discount to it. The non-consensus view is that the market is capitalising a peak margin and multiple at once.

Three scenarios weighted 25/50/25 put the probability-weighted value at $291.5, 15% below the price, and the recommendation rests on that weighted value and the $284 base case, not on the bull. The scenario bull ($357, 25%) — distinct from the $277 DCF bull above — assumes the AI and foldable cycle extends iPhone growth into FY2027-28, services grows above 15%, gross margin holds 48% and the search payment survives at a lower rate: 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20 for a 4% price return. Base ($284, 50%): growth fades from 9% to 5%, margin normalises to 47-48%, services grows 12-14% and the search payment is renegotiated lower — 29 times $9.79, an 18% decline, with intrinsic value of $212-264. Bear ($241, 25%): memory breaks the hardware margin below 46%, services growth falls under 8% as the DMA and link-out remedies bite, and the payment is cut or banned — 24.6 times $9.79, a 30% drawdown, with the $133 DCF bear as the permanent-loss tail [S6, S7].

Three analogs set the decision rule. Microsoft's 1998 antitrust case ended in 2001 without a break-up: the asset survived, but the overhang ran three years and the settlement did not re-rate the stock — the cloud did, a decade later. Nokia held 49.4% of handset share in 2007, peaked near $250bn and sold its handset business for $7.2bn in 2013: a platform leader that loses the next interface loses developers first and volume second. Cisco took until December 2025 to exceed its March 2000 record, 25 years in which the company compounded and the share price did not [S143, S145, S147]. The rule they teach is that at a peak multiple the entry price, not the business, sets the return. Apple is cheaper than Cisco at its peak (39.3x against 201), owns silicon and a services annuity Nokia never had, and holds $62.2bn of net cash; the analogy is about duration and multiple, not extinction.

The decision follows: watchlist today, zero position, with a staged entry set by price, not narrative. The first tranche of 0.75-1.0% of the fund is $270 only on a condition: the 2026-11-02 guide must hold FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and gross margin at 47%. At 27.6 times, $270 is a discount only on the $9.79 base EPS; on $9.27 it is 29.1 times, and on $8.07-8.53, after a 12.9% search-payment cut, 31.7-33.5 times, above the 31.0 times four-year mean. At 27.6 times those lower cases imply $223-235, so if the guide fails the first tranche moves to $235 and the second to $210. The position reaches its 5% cap below $225 or on evidence that FY2027 EPS growth is tracking above 12%. The red-team objection stands: $270 is a 5% discount to the $284 base case and sits above the $242 realistic bear, so it is a first price, not a margin of safety, and the ladder now prices the EPS bridge rather than a single point at $9.79. The counter-evidence is the stock's own record: 27.5% in the twelve months to 30 October 2026; a sale at 35 times forward would have missed it. The open diligence is the appellate outcome on the search payment and a primary consensus feed for FY2027 EPS, neither of which the register holds. Sell above 45 times forward earnings ($440), or if two consecutive quarters show services growth below 10%, gross margin below 47%, or a services structure that removes the search payment [S6, S7].

arguments.markdown:
Apple is a superior franchise whose price already capitalises the scenario bull. At $344.63 on NasdaqGS (2026-10-30 20:00 UTC) and 14,715m diluted shares its market capitalisation is $5,071.2bn — not the $5,029.6bn screens show on 14,594m shares — and its enterprise value $5,009.1bn after $84.3bn of debt and $146.5bn of cash and securities. That is 39.3x trailing earnings ($5,071.2bn over $128,930M of net income) and 39.1x trailing NOPAT; the data feed's 39.5x is price over the $8.72 sum-of-quarters diluted EPS, a 0.2x gap that is the EPS approximation, not a different earnings base. Forward, 35.2x on the $9.79 that multiple implies, is 1.9 times the S&P 500's 18.7x forward multiple (FactSet, 2026-10-23) and a 95% premium to the 20.2x peer median. The price needs 6.5-7.0% perpetual growth at a 9.0-9.5% discount rate, or a 7.1% discount rate on my forecast, for revenue that compounded 3.3% a year from FY2021 to FY2025 [S6, S7, S97, S156].

Samsung and Xiaomi file no US GAAP statements; their multiples are not disclosed here, so the hardware leg leans on HP and Dell.

The operating story that supports 39.3x is real but narrower than the headline. The June 2026 quarter grew revenue 16.4% to $109.4bn, with iPhone up 21.7% and Greater China up 22.4%, and the September quarter is guided to 9-11% growth. Against that, IDC expects global smartphone shipments to fall 16.7% in 2026, and TrendForce puts the iPhone 18 Pro's bill of materials up 38% year on year with memory at 34% of it, from 10% a year earlier. Apple is growing by price and mix in a shrinking unit market while its cost base rises; Samsung's mobile division lost money for the same reason. Price-led growth is the most reversible kind, and FY2027 gross margin is where the memory cycle will show [S17, S84, S99, S72].

Free cash flow is what the buyback and the model rest on, and the trailing figure carries an accrual that has to come out. Trailing FCF of $136.7bn is a 2.7% yield, but it includes $14.1bn from other current and non-current liabilities — $10.0bn in the nine months to June 2026 and $4.1bn in the September 2025 quarter — against a $2.5bn three-year average. Netting the line to those levels gives normalised FCF of $122.6-127.3bn, $125.1bn central: 0.95-0.99x net income, a 2.4-2.5% yield and 40.5x P/FCF on the $5,071.2bn market value. The $122.6bn floor treats the build as deferred consideration for $13.3bn of gross intangibles added. Shareholders have received $438.6bn of repurchases and $75.0bn of dividends in the five fiscal years to FY2025; no equity has been raised [S5, S6, S1].

A discounted cash flow is the right instrument for a company whose value is almost all terminal, and the least forgiving. I take FY2026 revenue of $477.1bn (nine months actual $364.4bn plus the guided $112.7bn fourth quarter), growth fading from 9% to 5%, a 33% operating margin and a 17.5% tax rate. At a 9.0% cost of equity — a 4.93% ten-year Treasury, a 4.5% equity risk premium and a 1.05 beta — the shares are worth $212; the market price is reached near a 7.1% discount rate. The two bulls are not the same animal. The DCF bull at an 8.5% cost of equity, a 35% margin and 14% first-year growth is worth $277 — 20% below the price — because it still discounts at 3.6 points above the 4.93% risk-free rate. The $357 that the thesis weights as its bull is a multiple-based target: 35 times FY2027 EPS of $10.20, today's 35.2x forward multiple held on earnings 4.2% above the $9.79 base. It is what the market would pay if the multiple holds, not what the business is worth on its cash flows; the $80 gap is the value of the multiple itself [S6, S7, S10, S97].

| Scenario bull (multiple) | 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 | $357 | S7, S97 |
| Sum of the parts | 23x services EBIT of $62.7bn, 12x hardware EBIT of $92.1bn, plus $62.2bn net cash; 28x/18x gives $238 | $177 | S6, S17, S14, S104 |
| Own-history multiple | 31.0x four-year mean P/E (FY2022-25; FY2021 price not available) on FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $303 | S7, S97 |

The bridge matters. Trailing diluted EPS is $8.72: FY2025 $7.46 plus nine months of FY2026 $6.88 less nine months of FY2025 $5.62. The September quarter, on the guided 9-11% revenue growth at the $112.7bn midpoint, a 47.5% gross margin, operating expenses near the June quarter's $19.1bn and a 17.3% tax rate, adds $1.93-1.99, for FY2026E EPS of $8.81-8.87. The 35.2x forward multiple then implies FY2027E EPS of $9.79 — 10.4-11.1% growth, consistent with S&P Global Market Intelligence's consensus iPhone revenue of $277.4bn (+9.9%) plus a 1.8% lower share count. FY2029E EPS of $11.45 in the exit analysis is 8.2% a year from there. The $9.79 is implied by the multiple rather than taken from a licensed consensus feed [S5, S6, S71, S72, S97].

| Scenario | Assumptions | Value per share | vs $344.63 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DCF bear | growth 4/3/2/2/2%, margin 30%, discount 9.5% | $133 | -61% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario bear | 24.6x FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $241 | -30% | S7, S97 |
| DCF base | growth 9/8/7/6/5%, margin 33%, discount 9.0% | $212 | -38% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario base | 29x FY2027E EPS of $9.79 | $284 | -18% | S7, S97 |
| DCF bull | growth 14/11/9/7/6%, margin 35%, discount 8.5% | $277 | -20% | S6, S10 |
| Scenario bull | 35x FY2027E EPS of $10.20 | $357 | +3.6% | S7, S97 |
| Probability-weighted | 25/50/25 on the scenario values | $291.5 | -15% | S6, S7 |

Three scenarios bracket the answer, and the price sits at the top of them. The scenario range runs from $241 at 24.6x FY2027E EPS to $357 at 35x $10.20, around a $284 base and a $291.5 probability-weighted value 15% below the price; the DCF range of $133-$277 sits mostly beneath it, and the sum of the parts is $177-238. At $344.63 the buyer pays 121% of the scenario base and 97% of the scenario bull, so the bull returns 3.6% before the dividend while the base costs 18% and the bear 30%. A margin of safety has to come from entry: $270 is 27.6x FY2027E $9.79, 95% of the scenario base and 12% above the scenario bear, and it is where the three-year return spans 5.0-13.3% across 27-34x exits. The $20bn Google search payment survives as a renegotiation rather than a ban, but it is on appeal. The dated catalysts are the 2026-11-02 fourth-quarter release, the May 2027 buyback authorisation and the D.C. Circuit's search-remedy decision expected in 2027. The conclusion is a price range, not a point: own Apple below the high-$200s, or on evidence that FY2027 EPS is tracking above $10.20; at $344.63 the market has paid for the bull. The sell-side targets I can see — $338-355 across four retail aggregators, TickFlow $339.35 from 50 analysts and vcpscanner $340.88 from 112 — are unverified and cluster at the price rather than at intrinsic value [S5, S7, S70, S97, S101, S142, S144, S157, S158].

The counter-case deserves its weight. The discount rate is a judgement: at the low end of the range the base DCF reaches the market price, and quality franchises have held premium multiples for years. What I will not concede is a margin of safety: on every operating assumption I can defend, the buyer's return is set by the exit multiple, already at the top of its own historical range. Confidence is high on the arithmetic and medium on the gap to intrinsic value.
