gates: Confirm company identity, legal entity, geography, stage, and business model.
Decide whether the geographic market context lens is material; if yes, map home, revenue, expansion, supplier, comparable-company, capital, exit markets and the investor perspective.
Decide whether the policy and geopolitics lens is material; if yes, map jurisdictions and perspective.
Complete the profile requirements before drafting.
Build the source register with source type, date, confidence, claims and a link or file/page reference.
Use visible source IDs such as [S1] as citations in the report.
Complete the evidence matrix for all material sections before drafting.
Run the pre-draft evidence gate and fix failures.
Draft the report from evidence, not from outline memory.
Run the red-team pass and rewrite weak sections.
research_plan.hypothesis: Watchlist, not ownership, at $344.63 on 2026-10-30. Apple is a genuine cash compounder — 0.97x normalised cash conversion on $125.1bn, $62.2bn of net cash, services at 40.3% of gross profit — but the price capitalises a peak margin and a peak multiple: DCF $212 at a 9.0% cost of equity, sum of the parts $177-238, base case $284, probability-weighted value $292. It becomes an actionable long through a staged entry: 0.75-1.0% of the fund at $270, a second tranche at $245, the 5% cap below $225, and a stop-review above $380. The two facts that would change the call are a 46% gross margin and a D.C. Circuit ban on the Google search payment.
research_plan.author: Lead Analyst

items: Use web and data tools for fresh facts whenever a company, market, price, policy, filing, funding, or executive fact may have changed.
For each major section, record targeted search strings, opened sources, source IDs, and why the selected sources are decision-grade rather than merely convenient.
Use the server's checks for deterministic QA, extraction, citation checks and the delivery folder; do not rely on a one-shot narrative draft.
Do not generate repeated filler paragraphs such as per-section original-document priority, citation-anchor blocks, or repeated metric-card copy; each section must contain content-specific analysis.
Before drafting, write a section distinctness plan: the unique decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence, and best visual artifact for each section.
For each section, draft one final-report thesis sentence that directly analyzes the company; never copy internal plan labels or rubric language into the report.
Remove repeated visible scaffolds such as "Economic mechanism", "Comparison and benchmark", "Counter-evidence and risk" and "Investor implication"; keep the scaffold internal.
Use a verdict strip, compact decision cards, selected tables, and at most a few KPI strips; do not repeat the same card, grid or dashboard pattern in every section.
Before writing the executive briefing, summarize the non-consensus or consensus view and the exact evidence that changes the decision.
Treat OCR as a pipeline: inventory files, OCR scan- or slide-heavy material, and keep page, slide or table references for every extracted claim.
Check every page holding numbers, TAM, valuation, customers, clinical or regulatory claims, policy claims, financing terms or team credentials before relying on it.
Mark OCR-derived claims low confidence until checked or corroborated; use ranges for OCR-derived financial inputs.
Build a claim verification table for material company-provided claims: verified, partially verified, unverified, contradicted, or not publicly disclosed.
profile_requirements.evidence: Completed across the run. Fresh facts: the team pulled Apple's FY2025 10-K, the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-27, the 2026 proxy and 8-Ks from SEC EDGAR [S5, S6, S11, S56], timestamped market data at $344.63 on 2026-10-30 20:00 UTC [S97], the market regime (S&P 500 7,580.07, VIX 19.42 at the 77th percentile, ten-year 4.93%) [S9, S10], and dated regulatory records: the EU DMA fee schedule and EUR500M fine [S77], the D.C. District remedy of 2025-12-05 and the D.C. Circuit appeal No. 26-5023 [S70, S76], the Ninth Circuit contempt of 2025-12-11 and Supreme Court certiorari of 2026-06-30 [S79]. Source register: 147 sources with type, date, confidence and claims, cited by visible [S#] IDs in every section; each section's evidence block records its targeted queries and why each source is decision-grade. Section distinctness: every evidence block carries a plan with the unique decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence, best visual, thesis sentence and what makes the section different; sections were checked to remove scaffold labels and repeated card patterns. Evidence matrix: all fourteen sections carry an evidence block with its gate passed (two independent sources, a primary or near-primary source, two numeric facts or a missing-data note, mechanism, comparison, counter-evidence, investor implication, diligence questions). OCR: no client documents were attached and no scanned or slide-heavy material entered the report, so the OCR pipeline and low-confidence OCR rules have no items to apply; no claim in the report rests on OCR text. Company claims: material company-provided claims carry a status label — the 2.5bn installed base, the ~$1bn Gemini licence, the Siri and Private Cloud Compute capability claims and the $1.4tn ecosystem are marked unverified or reported-not-confirmed, and the product section's patent table is marked low confidence. Red-team pass: completed and filed, section 10 written, and five cross-section corrections pushed to their owners. Gaps: seven user data requests filed for records behind logins or paywalls, and the FY2026 10-K is not due until results on 2026-11-02.
profile_requirements.author: Lead Analyst

rows.belief: Replacement demand is mature and price-led: buyers upgrade for battery, camera and now AI, but a 27.6% ASP increase is the live test of willingness to pay.
rows.evidence: Global 2026 smartphone units fall 16.7% to just over 1.0B while value rises 6.3% to $613B and ASP rises 27.6% to $581; Apple's iPhone revenue rose 22.4% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 against that market [S84, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: IDC attributes part of the China strength to purchases pulled forward ahead of Apple's own second-half 2026 price rises and sees China's decline widening to 20% in H2 2026; the sub-$100 segment fell nearly 60% in Q2 2026 [S84, S87].
rows.confidence: medium-high
rows.change: Discounting or a lower-capacity model to hold volume, or a December 2026 quarter that shows unit and mix elasticity.

rows.belief: The moat is real in silicon and the operating system and rented in AI: the intelligence layer protects the franchise without widening it.
rows.evidence: 2nm A20 Pro and in-house C2 modem, 65% of premium phone units, 40.1% product gross margin in the June 2026 quarter (39.9% for the nine months); Siri AI shipped 2026-09-14 as an English beta on a licensed Gemini model confirmed 2026-01-12 [S113, S94, S17, S111].
rows.counter_evidence: The flagship feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's TPUs; U.S. patent grants fell 12% to 2,722 in 2025 and no blocking family was verified [S118, S117].
rows.confidence: high on hardware, low on AI
rows.change: Siri exits beta with usage evidence that Apple's integration beats standalone assistants, or a second slip in availability.

rows.belief: 2026 is a price re-pricing cycle, not a growth cycle; the base rate for revenue is mid-single digits.
rows.evidence: Revenue compounded 3.3% a year FY2021-FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and 5.0% to the last twelve months; the 2026 acceleration is iPhone price/mix and China share gain [S5, S6, S84].
rows.counter_evidence: Foldables could add more than 17M units by 2027 at a $2,550+ ASP, 40% of a $45.7B category, and an AI upgrade cycle could pull demand forward [S84].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Two consecutive quarters of unit growth in a stable-ASP market.

rows.belief: Distribution scales without new capital: 40% direct and 60% indirect, with India at 25% of assembly and six stores.
rows.evidence: FY2025 net sales of $416,161M at 40/60 direct/indirect; 55M iPhones assembled in India in 2025 against 36M; India sales above $9B [S5, S115].
rows.counter_evidence: Indian assembly and components still cost more than China or Vietnam, and smartphone production subsidies expired on 2026-03-31 [S115].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Renewal of India's production incentives or evidence of cost parity with China.

rows.belief: The best unit economics in hardware: negative working capital bolted to a 76.3% services annuity.
rows.evidence: TTM revenue $466,823M and gross profit $227,123M; services are 25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit and cover company R&D 2.1 times; cash conversion cycle of -56.8 days [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Services fell to 25.2% of revenue from 26.2% as iPhone grew faster, and two services tolls, the App Store commission and the search licence, are being repriced in court [S6, S69, S70].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Services growth below 10% for two quarters or a structural cut in the App Store take rate.

rows.belief: The bench is deep and insider-built in hardware, operations and finance, and thin and newly reorganised in AI.
rows.evidence: Ternus became CEO on 2026-09-01 with Cook Executive Chair; the CFO (2025-01-01) and COO (2025) were internal promotions; 92% say-on-pay; AI moved under Federighi on 2025-12-01 [S56, S11, S127].
rows.counter_evidence: No filing names an owner of the AI P&L; Srouji was named Chief Hardware Officer on 2026-04-20, which supersedes the December 2025 departure report but leaves key-person concentration with no disclosed successor; the general counsel changed in 2026-03 while the DOJ and DMA cases are live [S133, S141, S132].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A disclosed AI leader with P&L ownership, or the loss of Srouji without a named successor.

rows.belief: Not attractive at this price: the franchise is exceptional, the multiple is not.
rows.evidence: 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and 32.1x EV/EBIT against 20.5x; the DCF is $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% [S7, S14, S6, S10].
rows.counter_evidence: Forward 35.2x is in line with its own twelve-month forward average of 35.7x, and a 148.8% return on equity has historically held a premium multiple [S7, S6].
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on the intrinsic-value gap
rows.change: A de-rating to about $270, or evidence of EPS growth above 12% into FY2027-28.

rows.belief: The exit is the public market and the buyback: liquidity risk is nil, multiple risk is everything.
rows.evidence: 40.41M shares and $13.84B trade daily; no peer is large enough to acquire Apple; the three-year IRR is -3.2% to +4.5% across 27-34x exits on a 1.94% shareholder yield [S7, S14, S6, S97].
rows.counter_evidence: A reversion to the 31.0x four-year mean from 35.2x forward costs 11.9% of the price, about 4.1% a year over three years, and the same daily liquidity is the channel that de-rates in a broad sell-off [S7, S97].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A sustained multiple above 45x forward, about $440, would be a sale condition rather than a buy signal.

rows.belief: The shares trade above a defensible intrinsic value and above every point of the DCF grid.
rows.evidence: $344.63 on 2026-10-30 against $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% and $193 at 9.5%/4.0%; sum of the parts $177-238; the own-history multiple implies $303 [S7, S6, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: The bull operating case at 8.5% reaches $277, and a 4.93% ten-year Treasury makes a lower discount rate defensible for some buyers, but no grid point on the base operating case reaches the price [S6, S10].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A fall in the ten-year yield toward 4.0%, or long-term growth proven above 6%.

rows.belief: Cash-true but flattered at the margin by tariff refunds and by buybacks.
rows.evidence: Normalised free cash flow covers net income 0.97 times at the centre of a 0.95-0.99x band on capex of 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x at Microsoft and 0.08x at Alphabet; buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% nine-month EPS growth [S6, S49, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: The 50.1% June-quarter gross margin includes 2 points of one-off tariff refunds worth $0.11 of $2.02 EPS, and FY2025 returned 107% of free cash flow [S17, S5].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A December-quarter guide below 48% gross margin, a slowdown in repurchases, or a FY2026 10-K that confirms the other-liabilities swing is an unpaid purchase.

rows.belief: Conversion is structurally strong, but the trailing figure overstates the run-rate by a working-capital swing that is partly an Irish tax artefact.
rows.evidence: $136,683M of TTM free cash flow; nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,176M, with other current and non-current liabilities at +$10,016M against -$15,161M a year earlier; the line's clean three-year average is $2,502M, so normalised free cash flow is $122.6-127.3B with $125.1B central, 0.97x conversion, a 2.4-2.5% yield and 40.2x price to free cash flow on the basic market value (40.5x diluted) [S6, S7].
rows.counter_evidence: The normalisation is an analyst estimate, not a filed figure; a $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities against $13,270M of gross intangibles added is consistent with deferred consideration for intangibles, which puts free cash flow at $123.2B, inside the band at 40.8x on the basic market value [S6].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: The FY2026 10-K working-capital and intangible detail due with the 2026-11-02 results.

rows.belief: A fortress: net cash, no debt-funded buyback, manageable maturities.
rows.evidence: Cash and marketable securities of $146,517M against debt of $84,344M, net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M while $62,094M of stock was retired; $12.4B of debt due within twelve months [S6, S5].
rows.counter_evidence: $2,604M of unrealised securities losses, $57.0B of purchase obligations and $16.8B of lease commitments [S6, S5].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A move to net debt, or repurchases funded by new issuance.

rows.belief: Our reading is that the price capitalises the 2026 margin as a base; we expect it to normalise. That is an assumption about the price, not a sourced consensus estimate.
rows.evidence: Guidance of 9-11% revenue growth for the September quarter; consensus iPhone revenue of $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4%) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%), with no group-revenue or gross-margin consensus held; our base underwrites 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1% [S71, S72, S6, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: Management beat guidance through FY2026 and launched the iPhone 18 Pro and Duo into the holiday quarter [S17, S113].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A December-quarter guide at or above 49% gross margin with FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices.

rows.belief: The next twelve months are event-dense and mostly adversarial for the multiple.
rows.evidence: Q4 FY2026 results on 2026-11-02; the DMA fee schedule in force from 2026-10-01; Supreme Court review of link-out fees after certiorari on 2026-06-30; the Google remedy appeal likely in 2027; standard iPhone 18 in spring 2027 [S77, S79, S76, S112].
rows.counter_evidence: There are positive catalysts too: Siri out of beta in five more languages from October 2026 and the spring 2027 iPhone cycle [S113, S112].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: An appellate ruling or settlement that removes the search-payment tail.

rows.belief: Zero today; a first tranche at $270 or below, a second at $245, and the 5% cap only below $225.
rows.evidence: A 9% three-year return needs an entry near $270; $1B is 7.2% of one day's traded value; the realistic bear drawdown is 30% to $241; the full Kelly on the scenario inputs is 337% of the fund, so the 5% cap is a risk-budget limit rather than a sizing output [S7, S6, S97].
rows.counter_evidence: The discipline has been wrong before: the shares returned 27.5% in twelve months, and a valuation-based sale would have missed it [S7, S97].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A de-rating to $270, or a December-quarter guide at or above 49% with memory contracted.

scenarios.driver: The AI upgrade cycle and the foldable Duo extend the iPhone cycle into FY2027-28; services growth stays above 15%; gross margin holds 48% through the memory cycle; the search payment survives at a lower rate.
scenarios.evidence: iPhone revenue rose 22.4% in nine months; iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max list at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable Duo launched 2026-09-09; IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at a $2,550+ ASP [S6, S113, S84].
scenarios.outcome: FY2027 EPS of $10.20 at 35x gives $357, +4% price and about +4.3% total return over twelve months; the DCF at an 8.5% cost of equity on a 35% margin and 14% initial growth is $277; a three-year IRR of up to +9% needs a 34x exit.
scenarios.implication: Own it, but the upside comes from a multiple that stays elevated, not from a margin of safety at entry.

scenarios.driver: Growth fades from 9% to 5%, gross margin normalises to 47-48% as memory costs reset, services grows 12-14%, and the search payment is renegotiated lower.
scenarios.evidence: The DCF is $212 at a 9.0% cost of equity on a 33% margin and 9% initial growth; the 31.0x four-year mean P/E implies $303 on FY2027 EPS of $9.79; revenue compounded 3.3% a year FY2021-25 and 5.0% to the last twelve months [S6, S10, S7, S97].
scenarios.outcome: $284 at 29x FY2027 EPS of $9.79, -18% price and -17.7% total return; the DCF is $212 at 9.0% (33% margin) and $277 at 8.5% (35%); the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0%; the three-year IRR is 1.3% at a 31x exit.
scenarios.implication: Do not own at $344.63: the compounding is real but already paid for, and the three-year return is roughly the shareholder yield.

scenarios.driver: Memory costs break the hardware margin below 46%, services growth falls under 8% as the DMA and link-out remedies bite, and the search payment is cut or banned on appeal.
scenarios.evidence: The iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials is up 38% year on year with memory 34% of it; the Ninth Circuit affirmed civil contempt on 2025-12-11; the DOJ cross-appeal seeks a payment ban; losing $20B is 12.9% of EPS [S99, S79, S76, S6].
scenarios.outcome: $241 at 24.6x FY2027 EPS of $9.79, a 30% drawdown; the $133 DCF at a 9.5% cost of equity on 30% margins and 4% growth is the permanent-loss tail; three-year IRR -12% at a 27x exit.
scenarios.implication: The entry price has to price this: even from $270 the three-year return is only 5.0-13.3% across 27-34x exits, so size, not conviction, carries the risk.

assumptions.assumption: Gross margin normalises to 47-48%, not the 50.1% June-quarter print, as tariff refunds lapse and memory costs reset.
assumptions.disproof: A December 2026 quarter guided at or above 49% gross margin with FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices.
assumptions.impact: -6.0% EPS per 200 basis points of gross margin, and multiple compression on a peak-earnings read [S6, S17].
assumptions.early_warning: The 2026-11-02 guidance and TrendForce bill-of-materials data, where the iPhone 18 Pro BOM is up 38% with memory at 34% of it [S99, S72].

assumptions.assumption: The Google default-search payment survives the D.C. Circuit appeal, renegotiated lower rather than banned.
assumptions.disproof: An appellate ruling banning payments or capping them below the current economics.
assumptions.impact: A ban is -12.9% of EPS and about 15% of FY2025 operating income; a materially lower rate resets the services multiple [S6, S80].
assumptions.early_warning: D.C. Circuit briefing and decision expected in 2027; DOJ and state cross-appeal filed February 2026 [S76, S80].

assumptions.assumption: Services grows 12-14% without relying on hardware mix, and the EU take-rate cut does not accelerate.
assumptions.disproof: Two consecutive quarters of services growth below 10%, or faster migration to external distribution in the EU after 2026-10-01.
assumptions.impact: A 3-point cut in services growth removes roughly a tenth of the sum-of-the-parts value; each $1B of EU commission lost is $0.75B of gross profit [S78].
assumptions.early_warning: The quarterly services line and developer take-up of the 5% Core Technology Commission [S77, S6].

assumptions.assumption: The buyback continues at $80B a year or more with net cash positive, so EPS growth keeps its 2-3 point financial tailwind.
assumptions.disproof: A cut to the authorisation, or repurchases funded by new debt.
assumptions.impact: Buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% nine-month EPS growth; losing that cuts EPS growth to mid-single digits [S6, S17].
assumptions.early_warning: The May 2027 authorisation and the FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement [S5, S6].

assumptions.assumption: The Gemini licence stays an R&D expense and is not repriced per device or per query into services margin.
assumptions.disproof: Renewal terms disclosed that price the model per device or per query.
assumptions.impact: A $1B annual licence is 0.65% of TTM operating income and $0.06 of EPS; per-device pricing at $0.50/$1/$2 across 2.5B devices is $1.25B/$2.5B/$5.0B a year, $0.07/$0.14/$0.28 of EPS [S111, S73].
assumptions.early_warning: Renewal commentary from Apple or Google, and any services margin step-down unexplained by mix [S111].

consensus.consensus: The market pays 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings. Our reading is that the price capitalises the 2026 margin as a base; that is an assumption about what the price discounts, not a sourced consensus estimate, because no dated consensus gross-margin or group-revenue figure is in the register. The only consensus in the register is iPhone revenue: $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4%) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%).
consensus.our_view: Non-consensus on price, not on franchise: the business is a genuine compounder, but the 2026 margin is a peak and no point of the DCF grid reaches $344.63. The evidence supports a watchlist place and an entry near $270, not ownership at the current multiple.
consensus.evidence: The DCF is $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% and $193 at 9.5%/4.0%; the sum of the parts is $177-238; and the June-quarter margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds [S6, S10, S71, S72, S17].
consensus.proof_event: The December-quarter gross-margin guide on 2026-11-02, and the D.C. Circuit decision on the Google payments expected in 2027.

one_question.question: Will the Google default-search payment survive the D.C. Circuit appeal, and at what annual rate?
one_question.why: The payment, put at $20B in 2022 by the trial record, is 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and about 15% of FY2025 operating income at near-pure margin. A ban or a materially lower rate resets the services multiple that carries most of the valuation, and it moves fair value from the base case toward the bear case regardless of how well the hardware cycle trades.

modules.position_sizing: Watchlist, zero position today. First tranche 0.75-1.0% of the fund at $270 or below, where a 9% three-year return becomes reachable across 27-34x exits; second tranche to 2.5-3.0% at $245; cap the position at 5% below $225. Maximum loss at the cap is 1.5% of the fund on the 30% drawdown; the full Kelly at $270 on the stated inputs is 337% of the fund, so the 5% cap is 1.5% of full Kelly and a risk-budget decision. Sell review above $380 (38.8x the FY2027 build); sell on valuation alone above 45x forward, about $440; sell outright on two quarters of sub-10% services growth, gross margin below 47%, or a structure that removes the search payment.

answers.most_damaging_fact: The survival and size of the Google search payment. The base case assumes it is renegotiated lower, not lost, but a D.C. Circuit ban is -10% to -13% of EPS and, with a services de-rating, -15% to -20% of value (sections 6 and 10, S70, S76, S135). The $20bn figure is a 2022 trial estimate, not a disclosure: if the 2026 payment is 25% larger, the EPS hit is about 16%. The second candidate is the gross-margin assumption: the base case capitalises 47-48%, while TrendForce has DRAM contract prices plus 10-15% in 4Q26 and NAND plus 15-20% with supply tight into 2027 (S136), and a 46% margin puts fair value at $269 at 29x, the entry price itself.
answers.company_only_claims: Five positive claims rest only on Apple material: the 2.5bn active installed base (an earnings-call figure, used for the per-device economics in section 6 and the per-device AI stress in section 10); the Gemini licence at a reported $1bn a year, which is not confirmed by either company (S111); the Siri capability and Private Cloud Compute privacy claims (Apple Newsroom, S113, S127); the $1.4tn App Store ecosystem (S83); and the 'record installed base' and upgrade-cycle framing. Each is labelled as company-sourced in its section. The $20bn search payment is the opposite case: a litigated estimate, not a company disclosure, and therefore not a company claim.
answers.generic_section: Section 2 (Team) was the thinnest and has been corrected in revision 4: Srouji was named Chief Hardware Officer on 2026-04-20, adding Hardware Engineering to Hardware Technology (S133, confirmed by S141), superseding the December 2025 departure report (S131); what remains is thin disclosure, with no degrees for six of seven executives and AI accountability argued from the absence of disclosure. Section 3 (Technology & Product) is now the weakest: its patent table is mostly 'not verified' and no blocking patent family is established.
answers.unpriced_risk: The AI cost curve. The base case holds a 33% operating margin and treats the Gemini licence as a roughly $1bn R&D expense, but R&D is already up 33% to $34.04bn with no disclosed AI revenue (section 6, S6), and the scenario analysis gives the licence only a low-confidence assumption with no number attached. A per-device or per-query price across the 2.5bn installed base would be several times $1bn and would land in the 76.3% services margin, a 2-4% EPS risk that the $270 entry and the 1.5-2.0% starter size do not adjust for. The same gap covers the xAI suit against Apple over AI distribution, which no section prices.
answers.first_challenge: Why own nothing at 35.2x forward when the franchise compounds at 8-11% and the buyback adds 2.4 points of EPS growth? The answer is the exit multiple, not the business: section 12 shows a 1.3% three-year return from $344.63 if the multiple reverts to the 31.0x mean (S97). A partner would challenge the $270 entry as arbitrary, and the lower-EPS case makes it worse: $270 is 27.6x only on FY2027 EPS of $9.79; on $9.27 (46% gross margin) it is 29.1x, and on $8.07-8.53 (margin plus a 12.9% search cut) it is 31.7-33.5x, above the four-year mean. At 27.6x those EPS cases imply $223-235, so the entry ladder needs an EPS condition, not just a price.
answers.downside_survival: The recommendation survives; the entry price does not. A market 50% smaller takes group revenue down about 35% and, on the 44.5% five-year normalised gross margin with operating expense held flat, EPS to $3.51, $70-88 at 20-25x; $62.2bn of net cash means the company survives and the buyback stops rather than the balance sheet breaking. Revenue 30% lower gives operating income of $73.0bn and EPS of $4.10 on the normalised margin, a 58% decremental margin, not the $95bn and $5.4 the 43.0% up-cycle incremental margin implied; a 10% cost cut lifts EPS only to $4.50, and at 29x that is $119-131, at or below the $133 DCF bear. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn on the $122.6-127.3bn band (central $125.1bn, 0.97x conversion), 56.9-59.1x on the $5,071.2bn market value, which covers the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of trailing buybacks and dividends; the deferred-consideration case at $123.2bn changes neither. Net cash absorbs three or more years of the gap. CAC doubling and a six-month financing delay do not apply (no customer acquisition cost; net cash and $12.4bn due within a year), so the analogues are a licence doubling to $2bn, 1.3% of operating income, and a buyback pause, -2.4 points of EPS growth. Multiple compression from 35.2x forward to 24.6x is -30.1%.
answers.ocr_claims: There are no OCR-derived claims in the report. Every figure in section 10 and in the review comes from an SEC filing, a market-data feed, a named research firm's release or a cited publication, and no client document was read through OCR in this run.

rows.finding: The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500 million on 2025-04-23 for breaching the DMA anti-steering obligation; Apple's revised EU terms effective 2026-10-01 cut in-app-purchase commission to 26% (from 30%), alternative payment to 20%, link-outs to 15%, and set a 5% Core Technology Commission for apps distributed via alternative marketplaces or the web.
rows.mechanism: The fine is a rounding error; the fee schedule transfers take rate from Apple to developers and lowers the cost of distributing outside the App Store, compressing the highest-margin revenue pool.
rows.benchmark: EUR 500 million is about 0.1% of FY2025 net sales of $416.2 billion; the DMA allows fines up to 10% of worldwide annual turnover.
rows.weakens: Apple says the terms resolve its disagreements with the Commission and keeps a 26% in-app rate; EU developer groups called the terms unacceptable, so the settlement is contested and may not be durable.
rows.implication: Underwrite EU App Store revenue at a lower take rate: each $1 billion of annual commission lost equals roughly $0.75 billion of gross profit at the 75.4% Services gross margin.

plan.decision_question: Which regulatory, policy and ESG issues are material enough to change the investment case for a long-only holder, and what is their dollar or margin impact?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's regulatory exposure, not its ESG record, is the material issue: EU and US platform remedies now target the two purest-margin revenue streams, the roughly $20 billion Google default payment and App Store commissions, so a long-only case must price a 10-15% operating-income tail and a lower Services multiple, while the tariff refund that lifted Q3 FY2026 gross margin by about 2 points is a one-off rather than a new margin level.
plan.why_different: This section prices legal and policy tails and governance quality; it does not re-tell demand, product or valuation, and it treats ESG only where an issue can change cash flow, the cost of capital or the multiple.
plan.mechanism: Platform regulation transfers take rate and default-placement rent from Apple to developers and rivals; fines are small relative to revenue, so remedies and fee schedules rather than penalties drive the dollar impact; tariffs shift product cost between periods; governance affects oversight and legal-risk control.
plan.comparison_set: DMA gatekeeper peers (Google, Meta), the pre-2024 App Store regime, Apple's FY2025 gross margin of 46.9% and Services margin of 75.4%, and the historical base rate that US antitrust appeals rarely produce structural breakup.
plan.counter_evidence: Judge Mehta preserved Google's payments; Apple's August 2026 EU terms concede little on the headline in-app rate; DMA fines are about 0.1% of revenue; the DOJ seeks equitable relief only; tariff refunds are a cash tailwind; and Apple's brand has absorbed labour and privacy controversies without visible demand damage.
plan.visual: Policy impact matrix with exposure, probability and dollar or margin impact, plus the regulatory record table.
plan.prohibited: ESG is strong; risks are manageable; well positioned; committed to sustainability without evidence; vague counts such as many investigations; treating the $20 billion as an Apple disclosure.

rows.finding: Trailing-twelve-month to 2026-06-27 revenue was $466,823M: iPhone $245,540M (52.6%), Services $120,478M (25.8%), Mac $35,863M, Wearables $36,290M, iPad $28,652M. Services is 25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit ($91,607M of $227,123M).
rows.mechanism: A low-frequency, high-ticket hardware transaction installs an annuity: each device creates a multi-year stream of 76%-gross-margin services (App Store, iCloud, advertising, AppleCare) that costs almost nothing incremental to serve.
rows.benchmark: FY2023: Services 22.2% of revenue and 35.7% of gross profit; FY2025: 26.2% and 42.2%.
rows.weakens: Services share of revenue FELL to 25.2% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 from 26.2% in FY2025 because iPhone grew 22.4% and Services 14.1%, so the 2026 acceleration is hardware-led, not annuity-led.
rows.implication: Underwrite the hardware cycle for the next 12 months and the services annuity for the terminal value; do not treat 2026 growth as proof of services compounding.
rows.confidence: high — both figures are filed segment data
rows.follow_up: Does services growth re-accelerate after the Siri AI launch and the iPhone Duo foldable in FY2027, or does the hardware mix keep rising?

rows.finding: Services gross profit of $91,607M on a trailing-twelve-month basis covers total company R&D of $42,901M 2.1 times, and R&D rose 32.5% year over year in the nine months to 2026-06-27 (to $34,035M) mostly on AI infrastructure.
rows.mechanism: Ownership of the silicon, operating system and billing rails turns third-party distribution and advertising demand into a toll: Apple books the margin without carrying the content or the inventory.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft's FY2026 gross margin was 67.9% on $331,839M of revenue; Apple's blended gross margin was 48.7% TTM.
rows.weakens: The toll rests on two contested arrangements: the App Store commission (Ninth Circuit vacated the 27% link-out commission on 2025-12-11) and the Google default-search revenue share (36% of Safari search advertising, about $20bn in 2022, now capped at 12-month terms).
rows.implication: The services annuity is the valuation floor and the regulatory attack on it is the main threat to the multiple, not to near-term revenue.
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on durability
rows.follow_up: What share of Services gross profit is App Store commission plus search licensing, and what is management's contingency plan if the link-out remand sets the commission at zero?

rows.finding: On the 2.5 billion active devices Apple cited in January 2026, TTM revenue is about $187 per device per year, gross profit $91, SG&A $11.7, R&D $17.2 and operating profit $62 — a selling cost of 6.3% of revenue.
rows.mechanism: The installed base is a pre-paid distribution network: the next service or accessory sold to an existing customer carries no acquisition cost, so contribution margin approaches gross margin.
rows.benchmark: Samsung's device (DX) division posted a KRW 0.8tn operating LOSS in Q3 2026 on the same handset demand, versus Apple's 32.6% operating margin.
rows.weakens: 2.5 billion is an earnings-call statement, not a filed figure, and Apple has not disclosed device counts in its 10-K; a 20% error in the base moves every per-device number by 20%.
rows.implication: Per-device LTV:CAC is not the constraint on the business — price is. The model is worth owning at a hardware-plus-annuity multiple, not at a software multiple.
rows.confidence: medium — the base is company-stated and unverifiable in filings
rows.follow_up: Will Apple resume disclosing the installed base numerically, and what is the paid-subscription count behind the services line?

rows.finding: Cash conversion cycle was -56.8 days TTM (DSO 24.5, DIO 16.9, DPO 98.3) with accounts payable of $64,525M against inventory of $11,092M at 2026-06-27; suppliers and channel finance the cycle.
rows.mechanism: Apple collects from carriers and retailers before it pays assemblers, so growth releases working capital instead of consuming it and the buyback is self-funded.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft -67.5 days and Alphabet +39.2 days TTM; Apple's own FY2024 cycle was -75.8 days.
rows.weakens: The benefit narrowed: payables fell $5,335M and inventory rose $5,374M in the nine months to 2026-06-27, consistent with pre-buying memory ahead of price increases.
rows.implication: Near-zero CAC payback in cash terms is a structural advantage that does not depend on scale economies others could copy quickly.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: How much of the inventory build is strategic memory pre-buy versus unsold iPhone 18 channel stock?

rows.finding: Products gross margin rose to 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 from 36.9% a year earlier, and Q3 FY2026 total gross margin of 50.1% included about 2 percentage points from tariff refunds ($0.11 of the $2.02 EPS); memory ASPs rose about 146% in Q1 2026 versus the 2025 average.
rows.mechanism: Brand pricing power plus a Pro-model mix shift lift revenue per handset, but the cost side is set by a memory oligopoly whose prices are now rising faster than Apple can re-price.
rows.benchmark: Products gross margin was 36.5% in FY2023, 37.2% in FY2024 and 36.8% in FY2025 — a 36-37% band before this year's 39.9%.
rows.weakens: Two of the levers are temporary: tariff refunds are a one-time recovery and the memory cycle is turning against Apple, with Samsung guiding 2027 memory demand above supply.
rows.implication: Do not capitalise the 50% gross margin; a 47-48% normalised margin is the defensible base case and the gap is roughly 5% of TTM EPS.
rows.confidence: high on the facts, medium on the normalised level
rows.follow_up: What gross-margin range did management guide for the December 2026 quarter, and how much memory cost is contracted versus spot?

rows.finding: The Google default-search relationship is disclosed only through litigation: Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and about $20bn in 2022; the remedy bars exclusivity and caps any default deal at 12 months, and Google appealed on 2026-05-22.
rows.mechanism: Apple rents the default slot on a device it already owns; the rent is pure margin but is now renegotiated annually against rival bidders and against AI answer engines that shrink search query volume.
rows.benchmark: $20bn is about 17% of TTM Services revenue of $120,478M and about 13% of TTM operating income of $154,859M.
rows.weakens: Apple has never disclosed the payment in a filing, so the share of the current $120bn services line that is search rent is unverified; the $20bn is a 2022 court figure.
rows.implication: A halving of the payment costs about 6-7% of EPS and a full loss about 13%; this is the largest single identifiable risk to the services annuity.
rows.confidence: medium — a dated court figure, not a company disclosure
rows.follow_up: Has Apple disclosed any revenue-share terms in its FY2026 10-K risk factors, and what did Microsoft or others bid in the 2026 renegotiation?

rows.finding: Apple's four hardware lines are sold through direct channels for 40% of net sales and indirect for 60%, with iPhone revenue up 22.4% and Greater China up 30% in the nine months to 2026-06-27.
rows.mechanism: Carrier and reseller channels carry inventory and credit risk, which keeps Apple's receivables at 24.5 days while the carrier subsidises the handset at the point of sale.
rows.benchmark: Greater China was the only segment to shrink in FY2025 (-4%) and is now the fastest-growing (+30% in 9M FY2026), a swing of about 34 percentage points.
rows.weakens: China growth of 30% is partly a rebound from a -4% FY2025 base and partly renminbi strength, so the underlying unit recovery is smaller than the reported rate.
rows.implication: Geographic concentration in Greater China ($64,839M, 17.8% of 9M revenue) is a swing factor for both revenue and the political risk premium.
rows.confidence: high on the segment figures, medium on the decomposition
rows.follow_up: What share of Greater China growth was price/mix versus units, and how exposed is the supply chain to tariffs on China-assembled devices?

plan.decision_question: How does Apple actually make money, and how durable are those economics?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple monetises the same customer twice — a 40%-gross-margin hardware sale that is paid for before the cost is incurred, then a 76%-gross-margin services annuity sold into an installed base of over 2.5 billion devices — and the durability of that second leg, not the first, is what a 39x multiple is paying for.
plan.why_different: This section prices the revenue model and the unit economics: product-line mix, the products-versus-services gross-margin bridge, a per-device waterfall, take rates and working capital. Demand, rivals and capability belong to the market, competition and technology sections.
plan.mechanism: Negative-working-capital hardware funds the balance sheet; the installed base converts into near-zero-CAC services at 76% gross margin; the two contested tolls (App Store commission and search default rent) sit inside that annuity.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own FY2023-FY2025 history for mix and margin; Samsung Electronics device division (Q3 2026 operating loss) for handset economics; Microsoft FY2026 gross margin 67.9% for the software-margin ceiling; Alphabet for platform take rates.
plan.counter_evidence: Services share of revenue fell in 2026 as hardware outgrew it; product gross margin is boosted by one-off tariff refunds while memory costs rise at triple-digit rates; the App Store link-out commission was vacated and the search deal is now a 12-month re-bid.
plan.visual: Unit economics table per active device per year, plus a pricing and take-rate table.
plan.prohibited: huge market, strong team, high barriers to entry, clear business model, fierce competition, well positioned, ecosystem moat unless evidenced, world-class, best-in-class

business_model.author: Fundamentals Analyst
queries: 10-K FY2025 and 10-Q 9M FY2026 segment revenue and gross margin by line (iPhone, Services, Mac, iPad, Wearables)
Quarterly release 2026-07-30 and 10-Q MD&A: products gross margin 39.9% versus 36.9%, tariff refunds 2 points
Epic v. Apple Ninth Circuit 2025-12-11 and the Google search remedies ruling: App Store and Safari tolls under challenge
Apple EU App Store fee changes (2026-08-18) and DMA decision: take rates 5-26% in the EU
S&P Global earnings preview: consensus iPhone revenue $252.4bn FY2026 and $277.4bn FY2027 — iPhone line, not company revenue
Unit-base check for implied iPhone ASP: 261M units (S74), 20% of 1.26B market units 2025 (S92), 23.6% of ~1.01B in 2026 (S84), memory 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials (S99)

rows.finding: Implied revenue per iPhone is $832 on a 20% share of the 1.26B units shipped in 2025 and about $1,060 on 238M units in 2026 (23.6% of IDC's 1.01B), a 27% rise that is cost pass-through and Pro mix rather than a proven upgrade cycle.
rows.mechanism: Price and mix rather than volume: carriers and retailers pay before Apple pays its assemblers, so higher ASPs convert straight into cash and gross profit without working capital.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 ASP $832 on a 20% share of 1.26B units; $941 on the 261M-unit estimate
rows.weakens: Apple discloses no units; every per-unit figure rests on a third-party estimate, and the 261M estimate carries low confidence.
rows.implication: Revenue growth is price-led and therefore reversible; the unit base, not the ASP, is the variable to watch because a 10% unit fall at a 39.9% product margin costs $0.55 of EPS.
rows.confidence: medium — the direction is robust, the level depends on an undisclosed unit count
rows.follow_up: What unit count does the FY2026 10-K imply once the September quarter is reported, and does Pro mix hold into FY2027?

rows.finding: Services produced $120,478M of trailing revenue, 25.8% of the total but 40.3% of gross profit, and $91,607M of gross profit covers company R&D of $42,901M 2.1 times.
rows.mechanism: A high-margin annuity on an installed base whose marginal cost of service is near zero converts installed-base growth into gross profit far faster than hardware does.
rows.benchmark: Services 76.3% gross margin against Microsoft's 67.9% in FY2026
rows.weakens: Apple does not split services revenue, so the mix inside the 76.3% margin is not observable.
rows.implication: The annuity is what the multiple buys, and it already funds the AI build; the risk is that its revenue share fell to 25.2% in the nine months of FY2026 as iPhone grew faster.
rows.confidence: high — segment gross profit is filed
rows.follow_up: Does services grow above 15% once hardware growth normalises, and what is the split between the App Store, advertising and subscriptions?

rows.finding: Per active device the model earns $186.7 of revenue, $90.8 of gross profit and $61.9 of operating profit a year, with a 7.8x ratio of gross profit to selling cost and immediate cash payback because the cash conversion cycle is −56.8 days.
rows.mechanism: Owning the customer while outsourcing the factory turns working capital into a source of funds, so growth is self-financing.
rows.benchmark: Cash conversion cycle −56.8 days against Alphabet's +39.2 days
rows.weakens: The 2.5B active-device base is an earnings-call statement, not a filed figure, and payables of $64,525M against inventory of $11,092M flatter the cycle.
rows.implication: There is no customer-acquisition payback to underwrite; the investment question is the multiple, not unit profitability.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: How much of the payables benefit reverses if suppliers demand shorter terms as memory costs rise?

rows.finding: Two tolls inside services are contested: the App Store commission, where the Ninth Circuit held the 27% link-out commission had a prohibitive effect and remanded, and the Safari search licence, worth about $20B in 2022 and 16.6% of trailing services revenue.
rows.mechanism: Both lines are rents on other companies' commerce rather than product advantages, so a court or a regulator can reprice them without Apple losing a customer.
rows.benchmark: App Store 15-30% ex-EU against 5-26% in the EU; Microsoft's 67.9% services margin
rows.weakens: The remedies ruling kept the Google payments and barred only exclusivity, so the payment may be renegotiated rather than lost.
rows.implication: Price the annuity at a discount until the remedies are known; a $20B loss is $1.12 of EPS, 12.9%.
rows.confidence: medium — the legal outcomes are unsettled
rows.follow_up: What commission will the district court set on remand, and how much of the Google payment survives the appeal?

rows.finding: The 50.1% quarterly record includes 2 points of tariff refunds, while memory prices rose 146% in 1Q26 and memory is 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials against 10% a year earlier; a 47-48% gross margin is the defensible base case, and the FY2027 EPS of $9.79 that the entry price divides by needs 48.0%.
rows.mechanism: Component costs pass through the bill of materials faster than handset prices reset, so a hardware-led mix shift compresses margin exactly when revenue grows fastest.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 gross margin 46.9%; FY2023 trough 44.1%
rows.weakens: Apple has historically passed memory costs through via ASP and Pro mix, and Greater China grew 30% in the nine months of FY2026.
rows.implication: Every 100 basis points of gross margin is $0.30 of FY2027 EPS, so the margin, not unit volume, sets the value.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Can Apple reprice handsets fast enough in FY2027 to hold 47% as memory contracts renew?

plan.decision_question: Where does the gross profit actually come from per unit and per device, and which of those pools is being repriced or competed away?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple monetises one customer twice — hardware at a 39.9% gross margin paid for before the cost is incurred, and a services annuity at 76.3% — and the annuity, a quarter of revenue and two-fifths of gross profit, is what the multiple buys, but its share of revenue fell in 2026 and two of its tolls are being repriced in court.
plan.why_different: This section explains how a dollar of revenue becomes gross profit per device and per user and where the price is set; the financial section tests the statements and the market section sizes demand.
plan.mechanism: Apple is paid by carriers and retailers before it pays assemblers, so each device is cash-positive on day one; the annuity (services at 76.3% gross margin) then monetises the installed base a second time, and its two toll lines are legal constructs rather than product advantages.
plan.comparison_set: Services gross margin 76.3% against Microsoft's 67.9% in FY2026; products 39.9% against Samsung's mobile division loss in Q3 2026; cash conversion cycle −56.8 days against Alphabet's +39.2; implied iPhone ASP $832-1,060 across unit bases against the $565 market average price.
plan.counter_evidence: The iPhone ASP rise may be a one-off Pro-mix and memory pass-through that reverses when the cycle turns; the App Store and search tolls are being repriced in court and the remedies are not yet fixed; services is still growing 14.1% in absolute dollars.
plan.visual: The per-active-device unit-economics waterfall with the implicit unit assumption stated, plus the pricing/take-rate table.
plan.prohibited: fierce competition, strong team, well positioned, risks are manageable, huge market, clear business model, high barriers to entry

financials.author: Fundamentals Analyst
queries: get_sec_financials AAPL 5 years + TTM + latest quarter (income statement, cash flow, balance sheet, returns, working capital)
read_sec_filing 10-K FY2025 item 7 — effective tax rate, State Aid Decision, debt maturities, capital return program
read_sec_filing 10-Q Q3 FY2026 item 2 — liquidity, purchase obligations, buybacks and dividend, ETR
read_sec_filing 10-Q Q3 FY2026 item 1 — deferred revenue, marketable securities, intangibles, commitments and contingencies
read_sec_filing 8-K 2026-07-30 item 2.02 — Q3 FY2026 press release with statements and balance sheet
get_sec_financials MSFT FY2024-FY2026 and GOOGL FY2024-FY2025/TTM — capex intensity and free-cash-flow conversion
get_price_history AAPL 2 years — price, 52-week range, market backdrop
web_search Apple Q4 FY2026 earnings date and September-quarter guidance

rows.finding: TTM to 2026-06-27: operating cash flow $146,724M, capex $10,041M, free cash flow $136,683M, net income $128,930M — conversion 1.06x on capex of 2.2% of revenue.
rows.mechanism: Assembly is outsourced and the tooling is owned by suppliers, so growth needs almost no capital; the cash thrown off goes to buybacks rather than to plant.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft FY2026: FCF/net income 0.50x, capex 39.2% of revenue. Alphabet TTM: 0.08x, capex 33.9%. Apple FY2025: 0.88x.
rows.weakens: Nine-month operating cash flow rose 43% ($116,996M from $81,754M) while net income rose 20%, so part of the record is a working-capital and tax-timing release that will not repeat; FY2025 conversion was only 0.88x.
rows.implication: Cash conversion is not the risk in this multiple; the risk is that the market pays 39x earnings (2.5% free-cash-flow yield) for a business whose growth is cyclical.
rows.confidence: high — filed statements for all three companies
rows.follow_up: What is the capex plan for AI infrastructure, and does Apple intend to fund data centres directly rather than through partners?

rows.finding: Q3 FY2026 gross margin of 50.1% included about 2 percentage points from tariff refunds worth $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS; nine-month products gross margin was 39.9% against 36.9% a year earlier, attributed to mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher costs including memory.
rows.mechanism: A tariff refund reverses a cost already expensed, so it lifts margin without any pricing action; memory inflation then works the other way with a lag of two to three quarters.
rows.benchmark: FY2023 44.1%, FY2024 46.2%, FY2025 46.9% — the 2026 level is 3 points above any prior year.
rows.weakens: Management expects component supply and cost pressure to intensify, and Samsung reports memory prices still rising across applications with 2027 demand expected to exceed supply.
rows.implication: Model a 47-48% gross margin, not 50%; 200 basis points off TTM gross margin is about $0.52 of EPS, or 6% of the $8.72 TTM figure.
rows.confidence: high on the disclosed items, medium on the normalised level
rows.follow_up: How much of the refund is still to come in the December quarter, and what memory cost is locked in for FY2027?

rows.finding: The FY2024 effective tax rate of 24.1% carried the State Aid Decision, and the FY2025 provision fell $10.7bn year over year on that base effect; normalising FY2024 to the FY2025 rate lifts FY2024 net income to about $104.2bn, cutting FY2025 EPS growth from a reported 22.7% to roughly 10%.
rows.mechanism: A one-off European Commission State Aid charge depressed FY2024 earnings and simultaneously inflated the next year's growth rate — a base effect, not a change in earning power.
rows.weakens: The nine-month FY2026 rate of 17.6% is already higher than FY2025 and FY2023, so the tax line has stopped flattering reported growth.
rows.implication: Do not extrapolate the 20%+ EPS growth of FY2025 into FY2027; the underlying rate was nearer 10% and the tax line is now a headwind.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the sustainable ETR under the OECD Pillar Two rules, and does the FY2026 10-K disclose a new unrecognised tax benefit?

rows.finding: Nine months to 2026-06-27: buybacks $62,094M plus dividends $11,778M, or 67% of free cash flow of $110,197M, while net cash rose to $62,173M from $33,763M and debt fell to $84,344M from $98,657M; diluted shares fell 1.7% (15,005M to 14,750M) against net income growth of 20.0%, so buybacks added only about 2.4 points of the 22.4% EPS growth.
rows.mechanism: Buybacks lift EPS only in proportion to shares retired; at $344.63 a $62bn programme retires about 1.7% of the count, so the earnings matter more than the shrink.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 distributions were 107% of FCF; FY2024 101%; FY2023 93%.
rows.weakens: Repurchases at an average of roughly $244 a share in the nine months were accretive against today's $344.63, but a repeat at 39x earnings is far less value-creating than the 2023-2024 programmes.
rows.implication: The buyback is not debt-funded and not the main driver of EPS, which removes one of the bear-case pillars; the corollary is that Apple is now under-distributing and building a cash buffer.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Will the $100bn authorisation be spent at 39x earnings, and has the board raised the dividend again in 2026?

rows.finding: At 2026-06-27 cash and marketable securities totalled $146,517M against debt of $84,344M, a net cash position of $62,173M — 39% of total assets; the FY2025 notes carried $91.3bn of principal with $12.4bn due within 12 months and $37.0bn of future interest, and other income turned to +$670M in the nine months from -$698M.
rows.mechanism: Fixed-rate debt raised at low coupons is cheaper than the yield on the securities it holds only if the cash is genuinely strategic; here the spread is negative, so the debt is a tax and repatriation artefact rather than leverage.
rows.benchmark: Net cash was $33,763M at 2025-09-27 and $65,797M at 2021-09-25; debt peaked at $124,719M in FY2021.
rows.weakens: Unrealised losses of $2,604M on the securities portfolio (adjusted cost $148,631M against $146,517M fair value) mean the cash is slightly impaired if liquidated early, and $5.0bn of intangibles are current assets.
rows.implication: There is no refinancing or coverage risk; the balance sheet is a strategic asset that lets Apple absorb a memory cycle or a regulatory fine without diluting.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the weighted-average coupon and maturity profile after the 2026 repayments, and are any notes callable?

rows.finding: Management states there is not at least a reasonable possibility of a material loss on asserted claims, carrying no disclosed accrual, while the DMA allows fines up to 10% of worldwide net sales and the Epic contempt finding is before the Supreme Court in the term that began in October 2026.
rows.mechanism: Antitrust remedies bite the take rate rather than the headcount, so a small percentage change in commission flows almost entirely to operating income.
rows.benchmark: The April 2025 DMA fine was EUR500M; the statutory ceiling is 10% of worldwide net sales.
rows.weakens: Apple has a long record of absorbing single-digit-billion fines without a visible earnings effect, and the remedies so far have been conduct-based rather than structural.
rows.implication: Treat the legal tail as a separate, unaccrued liability of low single-digit billions a year rather than as a base-case deduction — it is a sizing question for a watchlist entry price.
rows.confidence: medium — the exposure is unquantified by the company
rows.follow_up: Has the Supreme Court scheduled argument in No. 25-1311, and what commission did the district court set on remand for link-out purchases?

plan.decision_question: Are earnings quality and cash conversion as strong as the multiple implies?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's profit is unusually cash-true — trailing-twelve-month free cash flow of $136.7bn is 1.06x net income with capex at 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x at Microsoft and 0.08x at Alphabet — but the FY2026 records are flattered by roughly $2bn of tariff refunds, a working-capital release and a 17.6% tax rate, so the quality sits in the model, not in the growth rate the multiple is paying for.
plan.why_different: This section rebuilds the statements and notes and tests quality of earnings, returns and capital allocation; the multiple, the demand outlook and the legal exposure are handled by the valuation, market and regulatory sections.
plan.mechanism: An asset-light, negative-working-capital model with outsourced assembly converts nearly all net income into free cash, so the multiple is a claim on durability and growth rather than on conversion; the swing variables are product gross margin (memory), the tax rate and the pace of buybacks, not capex or leverage.
plan.comparison_set: Microsoft FY2026 (capex 39.2% of revenue, FCF/NI 0.50x, gross margin 67.9%) and Alphabet TTM (capex 33.9%, FCF/NI 0.08x) for the AI-capex contrast; Apple's own FY2023-FY2025 conversion and margin history; a ~10% cost of equity against a 2.5% earnings yield.
plan.counter_evidence: About $2bn of Q3 FY2026 gross profit and $0.11 of EPS came from tariff refunds; memory input costs are rising at triple-digit rates and management expects the trend to intensify; the FY2024 tax one-off makes FY2025 growth look better than it was; no accrual is carried against DMA or DOJ antitrust exposure.
plan.visual: Financial statements table (FY2023-FY2025, nine months FY2026, TTM), returns and working-capital table, and one info warning on the quality of the FY2026 margin record.
plan.prohibited: huge market, strong team, high barriers to entry, clear business model, fierce competition, well positioned, risks are manageable, clean balance sheet without the good-will caveat

financials.author: Fundamentals Analyst
queries: SEC XBRL statements for AAPL, FY2021-FY2025 plus 9M FY2026, Q3 FY2026 and TTM (get_sec_financials, 5 years)
10-Q 2026-06-27 balance sheet: shares issued and outstanding 14,608,963 thousand, used to reconcile the market-cap figures
AAPL price history to 2026-10-30: $344.63 on NasdaqGS, used for market value, P/E and the entry ladder
S&P Global earnings preview (S71): consensus iPhone revenue $252.4bn FY2026 and $277.4bn FY2027 — relabelled as iPhone, not company revenue
FinanceCharts (S97): trailing P/E 39.52x, forward 35.21x — $9.79 = $344.63 / 35.21x, reverse-engineered into a full FY2027 bridge
Web search for an independent FY2027 consensus EPS: no disclosed consensus figure obtained; bridge built from filed inputs and labelled derived

rows.finding: The $9.79 FY2027 EPS that anchors the $284 base case, the $270 entry and the $440 sale trigger is $344.63 divided by the 35.21x forward multiple quoted on 2026-10-30, not a published consensus figure. Rebuilt from filed and consensus inputs it requires revenue of $520.8bn (+9.2%), a 48.0% gross margin, $80.0bn of operating expense, a 17.3% tax rate and 14,450M diluted shares.
rows.mechanism: Forward multiple inverted: the price divided by a market multiple fixes the earnings base, so the operating assumptions are a consequence of the multiple rather than an independent forecast.
rows.benchmark: FY2025 gross margin 46.9%; 47-48% band after stripping the 2-point tariff refund; $9.19 at 46.0% and $10.08 at 49.0%
rows.weakens: S97 is a market-data aggregator, not a primary consensus feed, and the forward year convention is unstated; no filed or exchange consensus EPS was obtained.
rows.implication: The whole valuation case divides by a margin assumption at the top of its own historical range; every 100bp of gross margin is $0.30 of FY2027 EPS, so the entry and sale prices should be quoted in multiples of a band, not a point.
rows.confidence: medium — arithmetic is exact, but $9.79 rests on one market-data forward multiple
rows.follow_up: What will FY2027 EPS consensus be after the 2 November 2026 print, and does the sell side model 48% gross margin?

rows.finding: A 30% revenue fall rerun on through-cycle margins (revenue $364.6bn, gross margin at the FY2023 trough of 44.1%, operating expense held at $80.0bn) gives operating income of $80.8bn, a 57% decremental margin, net income of $67.6bn and EPS of $4.68. Reusing the 43.0% up-cycle incremental margin returns $5.95 and overstates stress EPS by 27%.
rows.mechanism: Apple's cost base is sticky downward: R&D rose 14.0% in FY2023 while revenue fell 2.8%, so decremental margins exceed incremental ones and the up-cycle marginal rate cannot be run in reverse.
rows.benchmark: FY2023 decremental margin 46.5% on a 2.8% revenue fall; 24.6x FY2022 exit multiple
rows.weakens: A 30% revenue fall is a tail scenario with no filed evidence behind it; the gross margin trough of 44.1% may be too generous if memory costs stay elevated through a demand collapse.
rows.implication: At 24.6x the tail case is worth $104-115 a share, which corroborates the $133 DCF bear as the permanent-loss anchor and argues for sizing, not for a lower base case.
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on the scenario's plausibility
rows.follow_up: What did gross margin do in the 2016 and 2019 revenue declines, and how much of operating expense is genuinely variable within a year?

rows.finding: Shares outstanding were 14,608,963 thousand at 2026-06-27; at $344.63 that is $5,034bn of market value. The $5,029.6bn used elsewhere implies 14,594M shares (15M fewer, 0.1%) and the $5,072bn figure is the 14,715M diluted quarterly average (106M more, 0.8%). The multiple is 39.5x on price / $8.72 diluted EPS and 39.0x on trailing net income / the outstanding count.
rows.mechanism: Market value belongs on shares outstanding; per-share multiples belong on diluted counts; mixing them shifts the multiple by 0.2 turns.
rows.benchmark: Quoted trailing P/E of 39.52x (S97); peer median 20.2x
rows.weakens: A cover-page count at a date after 27 June 2026 could give 14,594M legitimately; the filing text retrieved carried the balance-sheet count only.
rows.implication: The discrepancy is 0.1-0.8% of value and 0.2 turns, so no conclusion changes, but the report should quote one convention: $5,034bn market value and 39.5x.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Which count does the 2 November 2026 10-K cover page report, and how many shares were retired in the September 2026 quarter?

rows.finding: Trailing free cash flow of $136,683M contains $14,101M from other current and non-current liabilities, a line whose clean three-year average is $2,502M. Normalised free cash flow is $122.6-127.3bn, $125.1bn central, or 0.97x net income.
rows.mechanism: A working-capital and accrual build inflates operating cash flow without a matching earnings charge; the Irish State Aid settlement distorts the prior-year comparison.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft 0.50x conversion, Alphabet 0.08x
rows.weakens: If the build is deferred consideration for $13,270M of acquired intangibles, it is an unpaid purchase rather than an accrual and the figure is $123,152M — still inside the band.
rows.implication: Earnings quality is sound after normalisation and the pricing question dominates; the lower bound of the band, not the headline, should feed any free-cash-flow yield.
rows.confidence: medium — the line is disclosed but its composition is not
rows.follow_up: What was acquired for $13,270M of gross intangibles, and what is inside the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities?

rows.finding: Gross margin reached 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter, of which 2 points and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS are tariff refunds; products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% while memory prices rose 146% in 1Q26 and memory is 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials against 10% a year earlier.
rows.mechanism: A refund is non-recurring and a component-cost cycle reverses through the bill of materials faster than handset prices can be reset.
rows.weakens: Apple has passed memory costs through before via ASP and mix; the iPhone 18 Pro launch and Greater China growth of 30% show pricing power.
rows.implication: Two hundred basis points off the trailing margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of $8.72, so the multiple is being paid on a margin that is already past its peak.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What gross-margin guidance accompanies the 2 November 2026 print, and how much FY2027 memory is contracted at fixed prices?

rows.finding: Return on equity of 148.8% and return on assets of 36.1% are genuine; cash return on book capital is 65.2% on normalised free cash flow of $125.1B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, against 57.3% in FY2025. Nine-month buybacks and dividends of $73,872M are 72.4% of normalised free cash flow.
rows.mechanism: A high-margin, negative-working-capital model needs little invested capital, so returns clear the cost of equity several times and the only binding constraint is the entry multiple.
rows.benchmark: Ten-year Treasury 4.93%; cost of equity 9-11%
rows.weakens: Returns are flattered by a small equity base and $146.5bn of cash; a share buyback at this multiple creates no value if the multiple reverts.
rows.implication: Own the business at a price that does not require the multiple to hold; capital allocation is sound but buybacks at 39.5x buy a 2.5% earnings yield.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the incremental return on R&D now growing 32.5%, and does it justify the margin the market pays?

plan.decision_question: Is Apple's reported earnings quality and cash generation strong enough to justify a 39.5x trailing multiple, and what has to be true for FY2027 EPS of $9.79?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's earnings are cash-true and its returns are real; what an investor pays $344.63 for is 39.5x a margin that a memory cycle and two legal remedies can move, on FY2027 earnings that require a 48% gross margin, and the downside case is larger than the up-cycle incremental margin implies.
plan.why_different: This section tests the statements and their notes for accounting quality and derives the earnings base; it does not describe the products, size the market or set the multiple.
plan.mechanism: Negative working capital and low capex convert profit into cash at 1.06x, but the conversion is lifted by a $14.1bn liability build that normalisation cuts to $2.5bn; the marginal margin of 43% is an up-cycle rate whose reverse is a 57% decremental margin, and the FY2027 EPS the price divides by needs a gross margin above any year before 2026.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own FY2021-FY2025 history and FY2023 trough; Microsoft and Alphabet on cash conversion and capex intensity; peer median 20.2x P/E; the ten-year Treasury at 4.93%.
plan.counter_evidence: The liability build may be deferred consideration for acquired intangibles rather than an accrual, memory costs have been passed through before via ASP and mix, and a 30% revenue fall has no precedent in the modern franchise — so the tail may be over-weighted.
plan.visual: The FY2027 bridge to $9.79 and the FY2027 EPS band table that replaces the single-point entry.
plan.prohibited: fierce competition, strong team, well positioned, risks are manageable, huge market, clear business model, high barriers to entry

rows.finding: A 30% revenue fall from trailing $466.8bn leaves $326.8bn; on the FY2021-FY2025 average gross margin of 44.5% with $72.3bn of operating expense held flat, gross profit is $145.3bn, operating income $73.0bn and EPS $4.10 at the 17.3% tax rate on 14.75bn diluted shares — a 58% decremental margin. The FY2023 44.1% trough gives $4.03 on the same base; the earlier $4.68 paired 44.1% with $364.6bn of revenue (a 21.9% fall, not 30%) and is retired.
rows.mechanism: Apple's cost base is sticky downward: R&D rose 14.0% in FY2023 while revenue fell 2.8%, so the 43.0% up-cycle incremental margin cannot be run in reverse; at 43% the same fall leaves $94.6bn of operating income, 30% more.
rows.benchmark: FY2021-FY2025 average gross margin 44.5%; FY2023 trough 44.1%; FY2016-FY2025 average 41.4%; 29x cycle multiple
rows.weakens: A 30% revenue fall is a tail scenario with no filed evidence behind it; a 10% cost cut lifts stress EPS to $4.50, and the 41.4% ten-year average gives $3.54.
rows.implication: At 29x the $3.54-4.50 stress range is $103-131, at or below the $133 DCF bear, so the tail argues for position sizing, not a lower base case.
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on the scenario's plausibility
rows.follow_up: What did gross margin do in the 2016 and 2019 revenue declines, and how much of operating expense is genuinely variable within a year?

rows.finding: Market value at $344.63 on 30 October 2026 is $5,071.2bn on 14,715M diluted shares, 39.3x trailing net income of $128,930M. The 10-Q count of 14,608,963 thousand outstanding gives $5,034bn, 0.7% lower, disclosed as a cross-check in the exit share-count row; the 39.5x feed figure is price divided by the $8.72 sum-of-quarters diluted EPS, a 0.2x arithmetic gap.
rows.mechanism: Market value and the per-share multiple must share one share count; the diluted quarterly average is the count that matches diluted EPS and the $5,071.2bn basis used in funding and exit.
rows.benchmark: Quoted trailing P/E of 39.52x (S97); peer median 20.2x
rows.weakens: A cover-page count dated after 27 June 2026 could differ; the two bases differ by 0.7% of value and 0.2 multiple turns.
rows.implication: The memo carries one basis — $5,071.2bn, 14,715M diluted, 39.3x trailing net income — and the 14,609M / $5,034bn count is a cross-check, not a second valuation.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Which count does the 2 November 2026 10-K cover page report, and how many shares were retired in the September 2026 quarter?

rows.finding: One conditional ladder replaces the three-tranche alternative: 0.75-1.0% at $270 only if the 2026-11-02 guide holds FY2027 EPS at $9.27 or better and December gross margin at 47%, then 2.5-3.0% at $245; failure sends the first tranche to $235 and the second to $210 under the 5% cap below $225. The $278/$266/$254 tranches are deleted, not recommended.
rows.mechanism: A ladder priced on one EPS point breaks when margin moves 200bp: $270 is 27.6x $9.79 but 29.4x at the 46% low end, so the entry must be conditioned on the guide rather than scaled across guessed multiples.
rows.benchmark: 31.0x four-year mean; $9.27 at 46% gross margin; $8.07 after a 12.9% search-payment cut
rows.weakens: The guide may not disclose a FY2027 EPS figure, in which case the condition has to be read from gross-margin and revenue guidance.
rows.implication: One ladder, one EPS condition and one fallback: no second entry schedule competes with the thesis.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Does the 2026-11-02 release give a FY2027 EPS or margin frame explicit enough to trigger the $270 tranche?

rows.finding: Trailing free cash flow of $136,683M contains $14,101M from other current and non-current liabilities, a line whose clean three-year average is $2,502M. Normalised free cash flow is $122.6-127.3bn, $125.1bn central, or 0.97x net income.
rows.mechanism: A working-capital and accrual build inflates operating cash flow without a matching earnings charge; the Irish State Aid settlement distorts the prior-year comparison.
rows.benchmark: Microsoft 0.50x conversion, Alphabet 0.08x
rows.weakens: If the build is deferred consideration for $13,270M of acquired intangibles, it is an unpaid purchase rather than an accrual and the figure is $123,152M — still inside the band.
rows.implication: Earnings quality is sound after normalisation and the pricing question dominates; the lower bound of the band, not the headline, should feed any free-cash-flow yield.
rows.confidence: medium — the line is disclosed but its composition is not
rows.follow_up: What was acquired for $13,270M of gross intangibles, and what is inside the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities?

rows.finding: Gross margin reached 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter, of which 2 points and $0.11 of the $2.02 EPS are tariff refunds; products gross margin rose to 39.9% from 36.9% while memory prices rose 146% in 1Q26 and memory is 34% of the iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials against 10% a year earlier.
rows.mechanism: A refund is non-recurring and a component-cost cycle reverses through the bill of materials faster than handset prices can be reset.
rows.weakens: Apple has passed memory costs through before via ASP and mix; the iPhone 18 Pro launch and Greater China growth of 30% show pricing power.
rows.implication: Two hundred basis points off the trailing margin is $0.52 of EPS, 6.0% of $8.72, so the multiple is being paid on a margin that is already past its peak.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What gross-margin guidance accompanies the 2 November 2026 print, and how much FY2027 memory is contracted at fixed prices?

rows.finding: Return on equity of 148.8% and return on assets of 36.1% are genuine; cash return on book capital is 65.2% on normalised free cash flow of $125.1B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, against 57.3% in FY2025. Nine-month buybacks and dividends of $73,872M are 72.4% of normalised free cash flow.
rows.mechanism: A high-margin, negative-working-capital model needs little invested capital, so returns clear the cost of equity several times and the only binding constraint is the entry multiple.
rows.benchmark: Ten-year Treasury 4.93%; cost of equity 9-11%
rows.weakens: Returns are flattered by a small equity base and $146.5bn of cash; a share buyback at this multiple creates no value if the multiple reverts.
rows.implication: Own the business at a price that does not require the multiple to hold; capital allocation is sound but buybacks at 39.3x buy a 2.5% earnings yield.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What is the incremental return on R&D now growing 32.5%, and does it justify the margin the market pays?

plan.decision_question: Is Apple's reported earnings quality and cash generation strong enough to justify a 39.3x trailing multiple, and what has to be true for FY2027 EPS of $9.79?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's earnings are cash-true and its returns are real; what an investor pays $344.63 for is 39.3x a margin that a memory cycle and two legal remedies can move, on FY2027 earnings that require a 48% gross margin, and the downside case is larger than the up-cycle incremental margin implies.
plan.why_different: This section tests the statements and their notes for accounting quality and derives the earnings base; it does not describe the products, size the market or set the multiple.
plan.mechanism: Negative working capital and low capex convert profit into cash at 1.06x, but the conversion is lifted by a $14.1bn liability build that normalisation cuts to $2.5bn; the marginal margin of 43% is an up-cycle rate whose reverse, run on trailing revenue at a 44.5% through-cycle gross margin, is a 58% decremental margin, and the FY2027 EPS the price divides by needs a gross margin above any year before 2026.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own FY2021-FY2025 history, FY2023 trough and FY2016-FY2025 average; Microsoft and Alphabet on cash conversion and capex intensity; peer median 20.2x P/E; the ten-year Treasury at 4.93%.
plan.counter_evidence: The liability build may be deferred consideration for acquired intangibles rather than an accrual, memory costs have been passed through before via ASP and mix, and a 30% revenue fall has no precedent in the modern franchise, so the tail may be over-weighted.
plan.visual: The FY2027 bridge to $9.79 and the corrected 30% revenue-fall stress on the trailing revenue base.
plan.prohibited: fierce competition, strong team, well positioned, risks are manageable, huge market, clear business model, high barriers to entry
